- **yq: a write pipe whose `del` renumbers an array keeps each element's comment and style** (#2512). `del(.arr[0]) | del(.arr[0])` over `arr: [a # ca, b # cb, c # cc, d # cd]` printed `c # ca` / `d # cb`, each survivor wearing the comment of the slot it moved into; it now prints `c # cc` / `d # cd` as yq does, and so do a write before or after a `del` of the same array (`.arr[2] = "Z" | del(.arr[0])`, `del(.arr[0]) | .arr[1].x = 9`), a `del` of a field of an element another `del` renumbers, and a replaced element that carries a node of the old one (`.arr[1] = (["new"] + .arr[1]) | del(.arr[0])`). Each stage's static indexes are now read in the array it saw; a negative index into an array a `del` renumbers, a write at or past the end of the array next to a `del`, and a single `del(...)` whose comma branches nest still print each element with the comment of the slot it moved into.
- **yq: a write no longer re-declares the anchors of a merge source** (#2513). `.item.b = 3` over `default: &d` / `  a: &y 1` / `item:` / `  <<: *d` / `  b: 2` printed a second `a: &y 1` under `item` (the merge is expanded on the write path), so every later `*y` resolved to the copy instead of the declaration; the merged-in fields now carry no `&anchor` or tag of their own, as an alias expansion's do (#2500). An inline source (`<<: {a: &y 1}`), written nowhere else, keeps its declaration, and an alias inside the merged fields is kept. The expansion itself, where yq keeps `<<: *d`, stays recorded in the yq limitations.
- **yq: an assignment's right side, and an `and`/`or`/arithmetic operand, now re-emit from a
  context-free stage the way yq does** (#2588). Under yq's read-only context an absent key yields
  no node, but the first literal, `[...]`, `{...}`, operator or comma that follows it re-emits a node
  of its own and every later stage runs on it: `.x = (.a.zz | true)` is `x: true` (was unchanged),
  `.x = (.a.zz | true | not)` is `false`, `.x = (.a.zz | (true, false))` is `false`,
  `(.a.zz | 1) + 1` is `2` (was `1`) and `(.a.zz | (true, false)) and true` is `true false` (was
  `false`). #2540 modelled only the pipe's last stage and only `and`/`or`; the classifier is now
  `yq_empty_context_reemit`, a rewrite shared by `=`/`+=`/…, `and`/`or` and the arithmetic and
  comparison fanout in both evaluators. jq mode is untouched. Still open: a re-emitting stage inside
  `[...]`, under `|=`, and as the left operand of a parenthesised `//` (see
  `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`).
- **yq: a mapping key's `&anchor` survives a write** (#2598). `&k key: 1` / `b: 2` with `.b = 5`
  printed `key: 1`; it now prints `&k key: 1`, as yq does, for `=`, `|=`, `del()`, `-P` and
  `--arg`, and in flow mappings and nested keys. A value alias that targets a key's anchor
  (`b: *k`) used to be expanded to `b: key` on every such write, because the anchor-soundness
  gate never saw a declaration; it now stays `b: *k` while the key is still emitted before it
  (deleting or sorting the key below its alias still expands the alias, a documented divergence
  from yq, which prints an unresolvable `*k`).
- **yq: `-o json` escapes U+2028 and U+2029 on the streaming path too** (#2607, #2663). A line or paragraph separator that arrived as a raw UTF-8 byte in a scalar was written raw wherever the cursor streamed (`.`, `.a`, `.[]`, the default for a read) and escaped to ` `/` ` only when a write or `--arg` forced the DOM; a ` ` or `\U00002029` YAML escape was raw on the streaming path too. Real yq v4.53.3 escapes all of them. The streaming writer kept a private copy of the escaper, which never learned the separator rule; it now calls the one shared definition (`jq::escape::write_json_body_yq`), so the two routes cannot drift again. The fork existed because `#[inline]` on the shared body seemed to cost jq's `arrays keys_unsorted` 13.9% on a 7950X (#1638); re-measured under the pinned release profile, every jq row executes the same instructions with or without the fork and with or without `#[inline]` on a 7950X and an M4 Pro, so that figure was code layout. The separator check is a real cost on the YAML-to-JSON streaming path: +1.0% to +3.4% instructions on a 7950X and +0.9% to +3.0% on an M4 Pro over 10 MB of users, strings, unicode and block-scalar YAML, about +3% to +5% wall-clock on string- and unicode-heavy documents on both chips. Numbers in `docs/parsing/yaml.md` (O3).
- **yq: a write through an `as`-bound variable changes the bound copy, as in yq** (#2643). yq's `X as $y` binds a copy of the node, so `.a as $y | $y.b = 5` leaves the document as it was and `.a as $y | $y.b = 5 | $y` is `{"b":5}`; the same for `|=`, `+=` and the other `op=` forms, `//=`, `$y = 5` and `del($y.b)`, with the right side of `=` read against the stage's input as yq does. `succinctly yq` refused these with `Invalid path expression` (exit 1), and `. as $y | $y.a.b = 5` and `. as $y | del($y.a)` wrote the document where yq leaves it alone. The rows that write through `$y` as a stage of the `as` body (also inside a nested pipe, a comma path or a nested `as`) agree with yq v4.53.3 now; a bare `del($y)`, a variable-rooted path inside a write's left side and a write inside a construction (`[$y.b = 5]`) are still different (limitations). `succinctly jq` is unchanged.
- **yq: a variable bound from an absent key has no candidates** (#2650). `.zz as $x | $x` on `a: null` printed `null` and `[.zz as $x | $x]` printed `[null]`; both now print nothing and `[]` as yq does, and `.c | (.a as $x | $x) | path` no longer answers `["c","a"]` for a position yq never creates. The `as` source reads under the same read-only absent-key rule as a binary-operator operand (#2470), on the lazy, eager, owned-identity and path-position routes; the body keeps its own scope, so `.zz as $x | .zz = 3` still creates `zz`. An index on a mapping (`.[0] as $x`) is unchanged.
- **yq: `.a | .b line_comment = "hi"`, `.a.b | .c style = "double"` and `.[0] | .a anchor = "x"` apply the metadata write** (#2679), where they exited 1 with a `#2679` error (and, before #4599, exited 0 with the write dropped). A metadata write behind a static navigation (`.a`, `.a.b`, `.[0]`, or a pipe of them) now runs on the navigated node as a document of its own, so the subtree keeps its comments (a comment after a sequence item's `-` included), flow collections and quoting and takes the write, as yq v4.53.3 prints it (checked against it on a hand-written battery and on 600 random document, navigation and write combinations; every difference is recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`). A navigation to an absent node or one that answers several nodes (`.[]`, `.a[]`), a write that reads the node's own context (`key`, `path`, `line`, a comment), a document with an alias in it, and a stage that calls a `def` are still refused.
- **yq: `module`/`import`/`include` directives are a parse error, as in yq** (#2683). `succinctly yq 'include "mylib"; length'` parsed the directive, dropped it and answered `1` for a module that does not exist; yq v4.53.3 rejects all three at the lexer (`invalid input text`) because it has no module system. yq mode now fails at parse time, with or without `--jq-extensions`; `succinctly jq` still loads modules, and a field merely named `include`/`import` is unchanged.
- **yq: a metadata assignment under an `as` binding now applies** (#2705). `.b as $x | .a line_comment = $x` on `a: 1` / `b: hi` was refused with `only supported as a top-level pipe stage`, where yq prints `a: 1 # hi`. The write pass now evaluates the binding's source, substitutes each output into the body and resolves the writes there (chains, `|=`, a value write ahead of the comment, a parenthesised binding followed by more stages, and a source that yields several values, whose forks share the node so the last write wins in each result). A write in a binding's *source*, a destructuring pattern, or a `reduce`/`foreach` body is still refused.
- **yq: a write followed by a navigation keeps the comments, anchors and styles the write did not
  touch** (#2706). `.a.b = "y" | .a` on `a:` / `  b: x # c` / `  d: &z "q"` / `  e: [1, 2]` printed
  `b: y`, `d: q` and a block `e:`; it now prints `b: y # c`, `d: &z "q"` and `e: [1, 2]`, as yq
  does. The same holds after `|=`, `del()` and a metadata write (`.a.b line_comment = "cc" | .a`
  no longer loses the write itself), for a tail of any static path (`.a.e`, `.a[0].b`, `.a?`), and
  per document in a multi-document stream. A navigated scalar still drops its style and anchor
  and a navigated mapping value shows neither the standalone comments printed with its key. A
  navigation that is not the tail of the pipe (`... | .a | .f = 2`) is unchanged.
- **yq: block scalars survive a write, and `style = "literal"`/`"folded"` work** (#2707). Any DOM
  write to a document holding a block scalar (`.b = 1` on `a: |\n  x\n  y`) re-rendered it as
  `a: "x\ny\n"`; it now stays `a: |` with its chomping (`|-`, `|+`), indentation (`|2`) and folded
  (`>`) forms, a trailing comment on the header line and an anchor before it. `.a style = "literal"`
  and `"folded"`, which exited with `not yet supported`, write a block scalar (a non-string scalar
  becomes a string), and a string with a line break and no style of its own is written as one too
  (`.b = "x\ny"` is `b: |-`), as go-yaml does. A string go-yaml cannot write as a block (a trailing
  space or a space before a break, a character it will not write raw) keeps double quotes, in the
  go-yaml spelling. Ported from libyaml's emitter and checked against yq v4.53.3 on about 5,000
  random strings, in a literal and a folded block, in a mapping, a sequence and a flow collection.
  `style = "tagged"` is still refused.
- **yq: a line comment on a flow collection's element keeps the collection in flow style** (#2708).
  `.a[1] line_comment = "y"` on `a: [1, 2]` printed the block form (`a:` / `  - 1` / `  - 2 # y`);
  it now prints yq's `a: [1, 2, # y` / `]`, with the comma first after a scalar, the comment after
  the closing bracket for a nested collection (`[[1] # y` / `, 2]`), `]` at the enclosing indent,
  `}` at column 0, and each flow level continuing at go-yaml's rounded indent (`-I3`, `-I4`, `-I6`).
  A comment written below the container's direct children (`.a[0][1]`, `.a.b[0]`) used to be dropped
  silently; it is now kept. Checked against yq v4.53.3 on about 1,000 random flow collections.
- **yq: a side effect ahead of a metadata write fires once** (#2709). `.a = (.b | debug) | .a line_comment = "y"` printed `["DEBUG:",2]` twice, `.a = (.b | stderr) | .a line_comment = "y"` wrote `2` twice, and `halt_error` there printed its payload twice before exiting: the metadata pass re-ran every stage ahead of the write to learn the document the write sees, and that re-run wrote to stderr as well. The re-run is now silent, so the real evaluation is the only one to fire `debug`, `stderr` and `halt_error`; a `debug` inside the write's own right-hand side (`.a line_comment = (.b | debug | tostring)`) still prints once. Output, exit codes and the comments written are unchanged.
- **yq: `line` and `column` of a node with an `&anchor` or `!tag` are the property's position** (#2712).
  `b: &anc [1,2]` answered column 9, the `[`, where yq v4.53.3 answers 4, the `&`; the same held for
  every tagged or anchored scalar (`a: !!str 5` was column 10, yq 4), and for an anchored or tagged
  mapping or sequence whose value starts on the next line the *line* was wrong too (`e: &z` / `  k: 1`
  was line 6, yq 5). The position is the node's first property token whichever order the anchor and
  tag come in (`&x !!str 5` and `!!str &y 5`), in block, flow, sequence-item and explicit-key
  positions; a node with no property, an alias, and `at_offset`/`yq-locate` are unchanged. Still
  different from yq, as before: the root of a first document that opens with `---` or a comment
  (yq says 1:1; #4363), and columns after multi-byte text (bytes here, characters in yq; #4364).
- **yq: an unquoted `*` or a leading digit is part of a field name, so `.ab*`, `.*`, `.*c`, `.a**`, `.a*b` and `.1` read as yq reads them, and `*` and `has()` match a mapping key by its text** (#2800). yq's unquoted field is any run of name bytes, so `.ab*` on `abc: 1 / abd: 2 / x: 3 / 1: y` is `1` `2` and `.*` is `1` `2` `3` `"y"` (both were parse errors), `.1` is `"y"`, `.a*2` is the key `a*2` (not a product; `.a * 2` still is one) and `.a*=2` is `.a* = 2`. A wildcard now also finds a typed key by its text (`[.*] | length` is 4, not 3: `*` matches `1: y`, `true: t`, `1.5: w`), and `has(1)`/`has(true)`/`has(1.5)` on a mapping compare the key text where they answered `false`. 47 rows captured from yq v4.53.3 pin it. Once a name holds a `*` the rest of the run stays in it (`.a*+=3` writes the key `a*+`, as in yq). Still open (#4079): `.[1]`/`.[true]`/`.[null]` as an *index* on a mapping (they answer `null`), `.a+1`-style names with other punctuation, and a mapping key whose spelling is lost (`~`, `null:`, `0x10`), which a pattern leaves out.
- **yq: `path` reports an integer-spelled mapping key as an integer** (#2801). yq's `path` renders a key through `getParsedKey`: a `!!str` key stays a string and any other key is `parseInt64(text)` when that parses, so on `1: x` / `0x1f: y` / `+4: z` / `true: w` `[.[] | path]` is `[[1],[31],[4],["true"]]` in yq. `succinctly yq` answered `[["1"],["0x1f"],["+4"],["true"]]`, and `.[] | select(key == 1) | path` was `["1"]` where yq prints `[1]`. The component is now the parsed integer for `path`, `..` and `.[]` walks, and for `paths`/`leaf_paths` under `--jq-extensions`; quoted and `!!str` keys, JSON input, `true`/`~`/`1.5`/`1.0`/`0b11` and an overflowing digit string stay strings. `setpath` (and `getpath` under the flag) read an integer over a mapping by its decimal text, so a `path` result for a decimal-spelled key round-trips (`setpath([1]; "Q")` used to fail with `Cannot index object with number`); a literal lookup such as `.["1"] | path` now reports the matched key's integer too. jq mode is unchanged.
- **yq: an integer written `0x1f`, `0o17`, `01`, `+5` or `007` keeps its spelling** (#2802).
  `tostring`, string interpolation, `join`, `sort`, `max`, `unique` and `==` read the text yq reads (`.a | tostring` on `a: 0x1f` is `"0x1f"`, `.a == 31` is `false`), a tag or style assigned to the node (`.a tag = "!!str"`) quotes it as written, and `.[] | key | tostring` of a `01:` key is `01`.
  yq's JSON writers still print the number (`31`), and a value that crosses the reindex bridge carries its spelling in a bridge-only token.
  Arithmetic on a hex or octal integer still drops its base (#3027) and `tonumber` of a spelled string is unchanged (#1356).
- **yq: `-P` and every write keep both comments on a key that holds two** (#2806). A key whose
  deferred value comes after an anchor's own comment (`a: &anc # floated` / `  b: # own` /
  `    c: 1`) holds two comments, and the DOM route printed only the floated one: `-P '.'` and
  `.a.b.c = 2`, `del(.a.d)`, `|=` all lost `# own`. They now print `b: # floated` and `# own` on
  a line of its own at the key's indent, as yq does (#1085 had fixed the plain read). A key
  whose value is a flow collection or empty still keeps the first comment only.
- **yq: the first error a program raises ends the run** (#2810). `printf 'a: x\n---\na: 1\n' | yq '.a | tonumber'` prints one error and nothing else in yq, because the documents after the failing one are never evaluated; succinctly kept evaluating them and printed their results, with one diagnostic per failing document. It now stops at the first error across documents and files on every stdout route and `--split-exp`, and keeps what the earlier documents printed, as yq does. A failure to decode a value and an evaluator resource cap still let the run reach the next document. The issue's premise, that yq also erases the earlier documents' output, was not true: its example fails in document 1 too, because yq's `error` fires when `select` yields nothing.
- **yq: `//` decides per left output, as real yq does** (#2817). `succinctly yq` evaluated `L // R` with jq's rule (keep the truthy outputs of `L`, run `R` only if none survived), while yq v4.53.3 maps over `L`:
  a truthy output passes, a falsy one is replaced in place by `R`'s outputs, or stays itself when `R` yields nothing, and `R` answers on its own only when `L` yields nothing.
  `(null, 1) // 2` is `2`, `1` (was `1`), `(null, 1) // (3, 4)` is `3`, `4`, `1`, and `{} | (null // .[])` is `null` (was nothing). Outputs keep their positions (`(.a, .b) // .c | key`, `.a[] // 9 | line`).
  Implemented behind a new `EvalSemantics::ALTERNATIVE_IS_PER_LEFT_OUTPUT` on every evaluation route, assignment and `del` targets included (`((.a, .b) // .c) = 9` writes `b` and `c`); `succinctly jq` keeps jq's rule. Checked against yq on 2,590 filter/input rows (863 differed before, 25 now: yq's
  auto-creating key lookup, which is independent of `//`). Removes the three #2817 rows from the path-context sweep's known divergences.
  Pinned by `test_yq_alternative_decides_per_left_output_2817`, `test_yq_alternative_in_path_position_2817` and `test_yq_alternative_keeps_source_positions_2817`.
- **`succinctly yq` reads a non-scalar mapping key's entry through `.[""]`** (#2822). Real yq addresses a mapping entry whose key is a sequence or mapping by the `""` it collapses that key to: `printf '? - a\n  - b\n: v\nb: 2\n' | yq '.[""]'` is `v`; it was `null`. A real `""` key and a second non-scalar key are matched the same way, the last one winning. `.[""] | key` (the key node) and the plain-YAML round-trip of such a mapping are still unfixed.
- **yq: a tag or anchor alone on the line under a bare `-` or `key:` is kept, and the sibling key after it is no longer swallowed** (#2835).
  `printf -- '-\n  !!str\n- 2\n' | yq .` is `- !!str` / `- 2` and was a bare `-` here (`.[0] | tag` answered `!!null`, `.[0] | anchor` empty); `a:\n  !!str\nb: 1` is `a: !!str` / `b: 1` and lost `b` altogether (`.a` read `b`, `keys` listed one key). The properties name an empty node, as they do on the dash's own line. A comment on that bare `-` (`- # c` / `  !!str` / `- 2`) now goes forward as the next node's head (`- !!str` / `# c` / `- 2`), where it was dropped with the tag; it does not become the owner key's foot the way an absent item's does (`k:` / `  - # c` / `    !!str` / `z: 1` heads `z`). Pinned against yq v4.53.3 for a tag, an anchor, both, nested, at end of input and with a comment on the dash; the comment after the properties (`!!str # d`) still sits on the item where yq moves it onto the next one.
- **yq: a comment floated off an absent bare item heads a compact-mapping or nested-sequence sibling, not its first key** (#2835). `- # c` / `- b: 1` printed the comment inside the second item (`- # c` / `  b: 1`) and answered it as `.[1].b | key | head_comment`; yq prints it above the item and answers `.[1] | head_comment`, and so does this now, for a sibling in the same open sequence (`- # c` / `- - 1`, `a:` / `  - # c` / `  - b: 1`, a following comment or blank line, an explicit-key sibling `- ? k`, a sibling that is a nested sequence; an anchored or tagged one keeps the comment inside the item, as yq prints it). A float from a sequence that has since closed (`k:` / `  - - # c1` / `  - - # c2`) is still the key's foot. 22 documents match yq v4.53.3; two neighbouring shapes still differ (a second absent item in between, a float from a nested sequence that closed at the sibling) and are recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: `-p json` reads a stream of concatenated top-level values** (#2839).
  `printf '1 2' | yq -p json -o=json -I=0 .` printed an error here and `1` / `2` in yq; `{"a":1}{"a":2}`, `[1][2]` and `1,2` likewise. The input is re-read as one document per value once the single-value parse has failed, so a well-formed object or array pays nothing on the streaming routes. `"a": 1` and `true: 1` are two values, as in yq.
- **yq: a `-p json` stream that turns bad prints its good values first, and `--eval-all`/`--slurp`/`--inplace` read the whole stream** (#2839). `printf '1 2 ]' | yq -p json -o=json -I=0 .` printed `1` / `2` and then failed in yq, and failed with nothing printed here; `1 {"a":` was read as a one-key mapping. `--eval-all`/`--slurp` over `1 2` answered for `1` alone, and `{"a":1} x` silently succeeded; they now read every value and fail, before printing or writing, when one is bad. A later file is not read after a stream's bad value, as in yq.
- **yq: `sort_keys(f)` no longer creates a field the path names past a fan-out** (#2870, #2855).
  `sort_keys(.a[].b)` over `a: [{b: 2, q: 1}, {q: 3}]` added `b: null` to the second element and yq leaves it alone (`sort_keys(.nope)` already did). A path through `.[]` is now spelled out element by element and an element that lacks a field the path names is dropped, in sequences and mappings and past a nested field (`.a[].b.z`); an index past the end still pads and a path with a slice keeps its route (`sort_keys(.a[0:1][])` stays unchanged).
- **yq: a scalar the source wrote as nothing, `~` or `True` keeps its text on the DOM route** (#2875). `-P '.a'` on `a:` printed `null` where yq prints an empty line (and `~` for `a: ~`, `0x1F` for `a: 0x1F`): the pass that clears a bare result's styling also cleared its spelling. A comment-only document (`# c`) or a bare `---` under `-P` printed a `null` line after its header, and `.c = .a` wrote `c: null` for an empty `a:`. Each now matches yq byte for byte, and a plain `=` from a static read (`.c = .a`, `.c.d = .a.x`, `.[2] = .[0]`) copies the spelling of the node it reads. Not part of this change: a construction (`[.a]`, `{"x": .a}`), `map(.)` over a mapping, and the rest of the node yq copies (quoting, flow style, a trailing comment) still print the plain value.
- **yq: a stray comma in a YAML flow collection is a parse error, as in yq** (#2886). `printf '{"a":{"b":{,}}}' | succinctly yq -o json .` answered `{"": null}` for `{,}` (and `[1,,2]` read as `[1, null, 2]`, `{a: 1,,b: 2}` gained an empty-string key); yq v4.53.3 rejects each with `did not find expected node content`, since `,` cannot start a flow node. Both flow sequences and mappings now fail at parse time; a trailing comma (`[1,]`, `{a: 1,}`) is still accepted, as in yq. JSON-sourced input (`.json`) already rejected these (#2279, #2777).
- **yq: an unbound `$variable` is no output, as in yq, instead of a runtime error** (#2981, #2776, #2767, #3976). `$nope` printed `Error: undefined variable: $nope` (exit 1); yq prints nothing and exits 0, `[.[] | $nope]` is `[]`, `[$nope, 1]` is `[1]`, `1 + $nope` is `1` and `$nope // 5` is `5`. The same rule makes `$__loc__` (no builtin in yq) print nothing, and `5 as $x | $x-1` (the variable `x-1`) print nothing. Checked against yq on 40 positions, with and without `-P`. `succinctly jq` keeps the compile error (`$nope is not defined`, exit 3). The rule lives on `EvalSemantics::UNBOUND_VARIABLE_YIELDS_NOTHING`. Not fixed, and not specific to variables: `.[empty]`, `del(.[empty])` and `empty as $y | 3` (#4139).
- **yq: `path` and `parent` keep the prefix above a root-level owned node, and a debug build no longer panics** (#3019).
  `.[1:] | .[] | select(.c == 3) | .c | path` on `[{a: 1}, {b: 2}, {c: 3}]` is `[1,"c"]` in yq and answered `["c"]` here, and `.[1:] | .[] | select(.c == 3) | parent` is `[{"b":2},{"c":3}]` in yq and printed nothing; a debug or test build panicked with `an absent position hangs under a real ancestor`. The walk looks for the deepest live document node above a position to hang its identity on, and a yq slice of the document has none -- its position is the root's. The identity now carries every component below the owned root over the value each was taken from, so `path`, `key` and `parent` (and the second `parent`, up to the slice itself) answer as yq does. Swept 7 shapes x 5 middles x 5 tails x 6 getters over two documents against yq v4.53.3: 534 -> 442 differing rows, 0 regressed; the rest read an absent field, which yq vivifies (#2435).
- **yq: arithmetic on a hex or octal integer keeps its base** (#3027).
  `0x10 + 1` is `0x11` and `0o17 + 1` is `0o20`, as in yq, which writes `+`, `-`, `*` and `%` results with the left operand's format (upper-case hex digits, the sign after the prefix: `0x-10`; `1 + 0x10` is `17`).
  `/`, and a float operand, now fail with yq's `strconv.ParseFloat: parsing "0x10": invalid syntax` instead of computing a result.
  `-o=json` still prints the number.
- **yq: a write keeps the way an untouched scalar was spelled** (#3028). Any DOM write (`=`, `|=`,
  `del()`, `-P`, `-i`) re-printed every null, bool and number in canonical form, so editing one line of
  a GitHub Actions workflow turned `on:` / `  push:` into `push: null` (about 490 of 2,178 real YAML
  files on a developer machine differed from yq on this alone) and `~`, `Null`, `True`, `0x1F`, `017`,
  `+1`, `.5`, `2.` became `null`, `true`, `31`, `17`, `1`, `0.5`, `2.0`. They are printed back as
  written, the empty value as nothing after the colon, while the spelling still names the node's
  value; a node a write replaces takes the new value's text. Checked against yq v4.53.3 on about 3,000
  random documents. Reads (`tostring`, `==`) still see the resolved value (#2802), and arithmetic on a
  hex or octal integer does not keep its base (#3027).
- **yq: a comma-grouped `del()` or write whose branch steps into a string, number or boolean no longer raises and loses its siblings** (#3039). `del(.c, .a[0])` on `{"a":"ab","c":1}` raised `Cannot index string with number`, so the `.c` deletion was lost too; yq answers `{"a":"ab"}`. yq's `traverse` yields no candidate for a field or index step into a scalar, so the static-tail navigator now prunes that branch in yq mode. `(.a.b, .x.y) = 99` on `a: 5, x: {}` now writes `.x.y` (#1419), and a failing RHS reports `boom` as yq does. `null` still autovivifies, a container of the wrong kind still raises, and jq mode still raises as jq 1.7.1 does. An iterate step into a scalar (`del(.c, .a[])`) is unchanged (#2376).
- **yq: a YAML float with more than 17 significant digits keeps its source text instead of being rewritten to the shortest `f64` spelling** (#3040). `yq -i '.n = 1'` on `z: 2.7293109604053567083` rewrote the untouched `z` to `2.729310960405357`, and `.c == 2.7293109604053567083` was `false`. Real yq keeps a scalar's text until an operation computes a new number, so `is_preservable_float_literal` no longer caps the mantissa (#1008, #1211 added the cap); arithmetic still uses the plain `f64` parse. Streams, `-o json`, `tostring`, `==`, `sort` and writes now match yq v4.53.3 as captured in the issue; a bare digit run above `i64` is unchanged (#1129).
- **yq: a metadata write buried in a destructuring pattern's computed key is refused, not dropped** (#3203).
  `. as {((.a line_comment = "x") | .a): $v} | .` printed the document and exit 0 with the comment
  silently missing, because the gate that decides whether the metadata pass runs
  (`is_alias_sensitive_assign`) looked only at the `as` body and never at the pattern's keys; it now
  refuses it with `only supported as a top-level pipe stage`, like every other buried write (#798). A
  value-shaped write in a key (`=`, `|=`, `del`) still opens nothing: it runs against the bound value
  to build a key, never against the document the body returns.
- **yq: `del()` of a variable that holds the root keeps the document** (#3244). `. as $y | del($y)`, `del(. as $y | $y)`, `del(($y))`, `del($y | .)` and `del(. as $y | ($y, $y))` printed nothing and exited 0, silently dropping the document, where yq v4.53.3 prints it unchanged (`{"a":1}` on `a: 1`, and `true`/`null` on those scalars); so did `.a as $y | .a | del($y)` on a null or boolean `a`. yq's bare `del(.)` empties the document, but a variable holds a node and the root node has no parent to be removed from. The shapes yq does empty (`del(.)`, `del(select(true))`, `. as $y | $y | del(.)`) are unchanged, as is jq mode (`del(. as $y | $y)` is `null`). A variable bound below the root, and the order-dependent mixes such as `del(., $y)`, are the node-identity semantics of #2643 and are untouched.
- **`succinctly yq` reports a filter-built value past the 384-level tree ceiling as an error** (#3278). A write such as `.a |= deep(400)` panicked uncaught (exit 101, raw `thread panicked` line) inside the YAML emission pipeline; it now prints `nesting depth exceeds limit of 384` and exits 1.
- **`succinctly yq` treats `*` and `?` in a mapping key as wildcards** (#3374). Pinned yq emits the value of every key a pattern matches, in document order: `.["x??"]` on `{"x??":3,"x?y":4,"xyz":5}` is `3`, `4`, `5` (it was `3`). `=`, `|=`, `+=` and `del()` follow every matching key, and a pattern that matches nothing reads `null` and writes the literal key. An unquoted `*` (`.a*`) and a computed string key are still not wildcards. `succinctly jq` keeps exact-key lookups.
- **`succinctly yq` refuses a fractional or float-spelled slice bound** (#3415). Real yq hands every slice bound's text to `strconv.ParseInt`, so `.[0:1.5]`, `.[(1.5):]`, `.[1.0:]` and `.[1e0:]` are errors on every target (and under `?`); `succinctly yq` floored/ceiled them like jq. A float that is integral by computation (`.[(1.0+1):]`) is still accepted, as in yq. `succinctly jq` is unchanged.
- **yq: `map(.)` over an empty container keeps the node's position, as yq does** (#3450).
  `a: []` with `.a | map(.) | path` is `["a"]` in yq and printed `[]` here, `key` printed nothing where yq says `"a"`, and `parent` printed nothing where yq says `{"a":[]}`; the same for `{}`. A non-empty container still detaches (`[]`, no `key`, no `parent`), as in yq, and a scalar still keeps its position. An alias of a non-empty container and a mapping holding only a `<<` entry are still decided differently (#4690).
  The rule asked `is_container`, which is "has a subtree" for JSON and "is a sequence or mapping" for YAML; it now asks whether the node has members, and the owned-value twin whether the array or object is non-empty. jq mode is unchanged.
- **jq: a `foreach` step now carries the accumulator's node identity across source elements, and a full slice of it** (#3460).
  `path(foreach (1, .a) as $k (.; .a))` on `{"a":{"a":1},"b":{"c":2}}` raised `Invalid path expression near
  attempt to access element "a"` on its second step where jq answers `["a"]` then `["a","a"]` -- step 1's UPDATE leaves
  the accumulator on the very node element 2's `.a` moves the register onto, so jq's `jv_identical` holds. The same gap
  made `path(foreach (..) as $k (.; .a))` (and `recurse`) raise one element early, and `(foreach (.[0:]|tostring) as $k
  (.; .[0])) = 9` on `[1,2]` refuse where jq writes `[9,2]` (a full slice is the same `jv` as its input). A different
  path holding an equal value, a string slice and an empty-array slice still refuse, as in jq. jq mode only.
- **jq: `path()` and updates accept `tostring`/`@text` of a string and `tonumber` of a number** (#3460).
  jq returns the input as the very same `jv` for those, so `path(.b|tostring)` is `["b"]`, `(.b|tostring) = 9`
  writes `9` and `(.n|tonumber) |= 5` updates `.n`; succinctly raised `Invalid path expression with result`. Any
  other input (`tostring` of a number or array, `tonumber` of a string, `tojson`, `@json`) builds a fresh value and
  still refuses, as in jq. `tonumber` of a number also writes in yq mode (as in yq v4.53.3); yq's `(.b|tostring) = "z"` stays a no-op.
- **yq: `[.]` over a mapping with a collection as its key prints the key as yq does** (#3475).
  `printf '? [a, b]\n: 1\n' | yq '[.]'` prints `- ? [a, b]` / `  : 1`, where it printed `- '': 1`. It follows from an array of the
  document's own nodes streaming from the nodes instead of copying them, so a document with a comment or an alias keeps the
  old output.
- **jq: `limit`/`first` over a pipe stop the stages after the bound on the `key`/`path` walk** (#3514). `.a | limit(1; .[] | if ("A"|stderr) then . else . end) | key` on `{"a":[1,2]}` wrote `AA` where jq's `path(...) | last` writes `A`: the cursor route's walk stepped the whole pipe before truncating it, so every stage after `.[]` ran at the positions past the bound too, and a `?//` in it retried once more per dropped position (`AAAA` against jq's `AA`). The pipe is now streamed with a sink that stops at the bound, and each branch of a comma body gets only the budget the earlier branches left, so a pipe inside a comma branch stops as well. Output and exit status are unchanged on well-formed input; only the side effects (`stderr`, `debug`, `input`) and retries of positions jq never reaches go away.
- **yq: `keys`, `length` and `has` count a mapping's `<<` merge key as the entry it is** (#3556). yq splices a merge for value reads but lists the mapping's own entries in a key list, so with `base: &base {p: 1, q: 2}` and `item: {<<: *base, r: 3}`, `.item | keys` is `["<<","r"]`, `.item | length` is `2`, `.item | has("p")` is `false` and `.item | has("<<")` is `true`; `succinctly yq` answered `["p","q","r"]`, `3`, `true` and `false`. Fixed for one source, a sequence of sources, an own key around the merge key, an inline source and a source that merges another, all captured from yq v4.53.3. `succinctly jq` keeps the merged view. `to_entries`, `pick`, `..` and a mapping a write or `+` already materialized still list the merged members; see `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: a computed or multi-key index reads its target's explicit tag before its text** (#3563). `.[$k]`, `.["b","c"]` and `.[0,1]` tested the target's text for null, so `a: !!null foo | .a | .[0,1]` answered nothing where yq answers `null null`, and `a: !!str null | .a | .[0,1]` answered `null null` where yq answers nothing. The index now carries the cursor the target was read from and asks `cursor_is_null`, as the literal field and index arms have since #3533. Checked against yq v4.53.3 on 19 rows pinned in `tests/yq_cli/i3563.rs`. Still different: a container tagged `!!null` (`a: !!null {b: 1}`) is read as the mapping it holds (#4111).
- **yq: a float read from JSON input prints through yq's float formatter** (#3576).
  `echo '{"big":1e20,"t":-1e-7,"m":1234567.5}' | yq -p json -o json .` printed `100000000000000000000`, `-0.0000001` and
  `1234567.5`; yq prints `1e+20`, `-1e-07` and `1.2345675e+06` (shortest digits, scientific past its magnitude threshold,
  the same rule it applies to a computed float). The streaming JSON and YAML printers, the `-P` DOM route and the YAML
  emitter now agree with yq for `-o=json`, `-o=yaml` and `-P`; whole floats inside `i64` stay integers, as before.

Verified byte for byte against yq over about 1,800 strings in eight contexts; the one deliberate difference is a string starting with a break and then a space, which yq writes without the indentation indicator and so reads back without the space (ours writes `|2-`). The two `json_string_style_line_break_*_3587` goldens now pass.

The walk collected a `try` body and a nested pipe whole before delivering their first position, so every `stderr`, `debug` or `input` in a later stage ran at positions the bound never reaches. Both now deliver position by position, so the stop reaches them; a `try` still catches only its own body's errors, and the computed-bracket rollback is unchanged. Over a 2,520-row base-vs-branch-vs-jq-1.7.1 sweep, 38 rows changed to jq's answer, none regressed, and 432 yq-mode rows are byte-identical.
- **jq: `path()` and updates accept a non-matching `ltrimstr`/`rtrimstr`** (#4016). jq returns the input as the same `jv`
  when the input or the literal argument is not a string or the edge does not match, so `path(.b|ltrimstr("x"))` on
  `{"b":"s"}` is `["b"]` and `(.b|ltrimstr("x")) = 9` writes; succinctly raised `Invalid path expression`. A matching
  edge (an empty argument matches) builds a fresh string and still refuses, as in jq. A non-literal argument still
  refuses. jq mode only.
- **jq: a variable bound to a stage that returns its input is the register in `path()` and updates** (#4017).
  `path(.b|tostring as $y|$y)` on `{"b":"s"}` is `["b"]` and `path(.n|tonumber as $x|$x)` is `["n"]` in jq, where
  succinctly raised `Invalid path expression with result`; the same holds for `@text`, a non-matching
  `ltrimstr`/`rtrimstr`, `delpaths([])` and `setpath([]; .)`, and for the writes through them
  (`(.b|tostring as $y|$y) = 9`, `del(.b|tostring as $y|$y)`). It also closes a silent write drop:
  `(.d|ltrimstr("s") as $v|try ($v|.b?)) = 9` on `{"d":{"b":1}}` left the document unchanged, where jq writes `{"d":{"b":9}}`.
  An input that gets a fresh result (`{"b":5}|tostring`) is still refused, as in jq, and so is the stage under a
  `//`, `?` or `try` (a refusal there stays loud). jq mode only.
- **jq: a `catch` handler that navigates the node its `try` body raised is a path for scalar registers and for more body shapes** (#4019). `path(.d | .[] | try (if . == 3 then error(.) else . end) catch .)` and `path(.s | try error catch .)` refused with `Invalid path expression with result 3` where jq 1.7.1 answers `["d",0]`, `["d",1]` and `["s"]`, and `path(try (error(.)|error("x")) catch ((.a)? // 5))` on `{"a":{"b":1}}` refused where jq answers `["a"]`. A `try` entered on a path-tracked value whose body raises only its own input (`error`, `error(.)`, `error | error`, `error(.) | error("x")`, `select(c) | error`, an `if` over a total condition, a comma) now hands the handler the register's node, a number or string register included (it has no storage to compare), so `.`, `.a`, `.[0]`, `.[1:]` and `(.a)? // 5` reach it, through `path`, `del`, `=` and `|=`; the stage after such a `try` reads each handler output's own register, so `path(. as $x | try (error(.)|error("x")) catch ((.a)? // 5) | $x)` is `[]` on `{"d":[3,4]}` and still a path error on `{"a":{"b":1}}`, as in jq. A body that navigates first (`.[0] | error`), builds the payload by value (`error([.][0])`) or whose condition can raise still refuses, as in jq. Inside a `reduce`/`foreach` UPDATE or EXTRACT the handler is seeded as before, since a fold's source may have moved jq's register off the accumulator. Refuse-only before.
- **jq: a `foreach` UPDATE that is a bare register-neutral builtin, or a nested comma, pipe, `//` or `?` of them, no longer skips the write silently** (#4028, a #3960 residual). `del(foreach .a as $v (0; now; try ($v | .b?)))` on `{"a":{"b":1,"c":[1,2]},"z":0}` is `{"a":{"c":[1,2]},"z":0}` in jq and was the unchanged document (exit 0) here: `now`, `floor` and the other builtins #3960 lists navigate nothing, so jq's register is still on `.a` when EXTRACT runs, but only a flat comma sibling was read as leaving it, and the `try` swallowed the refusal into a skipped write. UPDATE is now read through the shapes that only fork or sequence such builtins (`now`, `((now,now),(now,now))`, `(now, now|tostring)`, `(now, first(floor))`, `(now, floor // 1)`, `(now, floor?)`, `(now)?`, `(($v|.b?), (now|floor))`), and `=`, `|=`, `del` and `path` follow jq. An 80,000-row seeded grid of UPDATE shapes against jq 1.7.1 fixes 1,783 rows with no regression and no new accepted-where-jq-refuses row. A pipe stage after a comma with a navigating sibling (`(($v|.b?), now) | floor`), a bare `abs`/`min`-class UPDATE and a neutral builtin inside an `if`, an array or a `catch` handler still skip the write silently, as before.
- **jq: `path(foreach (foreach (. as [$a] | .) as $k (.; .; .)) as $q (.; .; .))` now refuses as jq does** (#4031). A `foreach` whose source is a nested `foreach` over a destructuring bind of the register answered `[]` (and a write through it landed nowhere) where jq raises `Invalid path expression with result [[1]]`: the nested `foreach` does not backtrack its source, so the bind's tracked index step moves jq's register for the outer fold, whatever the nested loop pattern is. Only a nested `foreach` whose own *loop pattern* destructured (#3853) was routed through the resolver before; the nested source is now read too. A nested `reduce` backtracks and is unchanged.
- **jq: a `foreach` UPDATE that is a pipe stage after a comma with a navigating sibling, a bare `abs`, or a neutral builtin inside an `if`, an array or a `catch` handler no longer skips the write silently** (#4041, a #4028 residual). `del(foreach .a as $v (0; (($v|.b?), now) | floor; try ($v | .b?)))` on `{"a":{"b":1,"c":[1,2]},"z":0}` is `{"a":{"c":[1,2]},"z":0}` in jq and was the unchanged document (exit 0) here: the builtins navigate nothing, so jq's register is still on `.a` when EXTRACT runs, but the pipe stage after the comma was resolved without the comma's per-sibling register statement, and `abs`, `if`, `[...]` and `try ... catch` were not read at all, so the `try` swallowed the refusal into a skipped write. A neutral tail is now pushed into the siblings of the comma it follows (`(A, B) | F` is `(A | F), (B | F)` in jq's own evaluation order), `abs` joins the register-neutral builtins, and an `if` (its branches), an array (its contents) and a `try ... catch` (its body and handler) are neutral when what runs in them is; `=`, `|=`, `del` and `path` follow jq. Not changed: a navigating element inside an array (`[$v|.b?]`) and `min`/`max`/`ltrimstr`/`rtrimstr` still refuse or skip as before.
- **jq: a `reduce` with a destructuring loop pattern leaves jq's path register where it entered** (#4048, a #3999 residual). `path(. as $x | {a:{b:1}} | ((reduce . as {a:$a} ?// $a (0; .)) or true) | $x)` on `{"a":[true]}` is `[]` in jq and was exit 5 here (so were `reduce .[] as [$a] (0; .)` before a frozen `$x`, the same fold under unary minus, and the `del`/`=` rows built on them): the pattern's steps run inside the loop jq backtracks, but the fold handed back no register, so the next stage could not tell `$x` was still the register. A destructuring `reduce` now states the register unmoved, from the stage's frame on an untracked entry. Over the 20 `reduce`/`foreach ... ?//` operands of `scripts/jq-path-register-sweep.py` (6,027 sampled rows) 375 refusals became 155, no row worse and no new wrong answer. `foreach`, a `try`-wrapped fold and a fold entered under a `?//` bind still refuse where jq answers.
- **jq: a fold on an untracked stage steps from the register it carries** (#4049, a #3999 residual). `del(try (.a and (reduce . as {a:$a} ?// $a (0; .))))` on `{"a":true}` is `{}` in jq: the first alternative fails `path_intact`, `?//` retries to `$a`, and the `and` result `true` is `jv_identical` to the register's `true`, so `.a` is deleted. #3999 retried correctly but the fold could not *step* from a register whose position it did not know, and a destructuring `reduce` handed the stage no register, so the result refused ("with result true"). A fold entered on an untracked stage whose register the stage still carries now seeds its pattern walk from that register (it sits at the fold's root), so jq's `path_intact` decides each step -- a `null` or boolean element is the register's node by kind (`path(.a | 5 | reduce null as {a:$q} (null; .))` on `{"a":null}` is `["a"]`, a `foreach` over it extends the register's own path, `["a","a"]`) -- and a `reduce` over it leaves the register where it entered, as jq's backtracked loop does. A `foreach` still states no register at its emissions, so `del(.a and (foreach . as {a:$a} ?// $a (0; .; .)))` still refuses where jq answers (recorded in `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`). Over the 9 fold-pattern operands of the path-register sweep (119,907 rows, `/usr/bin/jq` 1.7.1), ACCEPT_WRONG stayed 0, DIFF stayed 8, REFUSE_WRONG fell from 7,745 to 7,285 and MATCH rose from 112,154 to 112,614, with no regression.
- **`sort_by`, `unique_by` and `group_by` read an absent key as no output, as yq does** (#4054, #4387). yq evaluates the key filter read-only, so an element lacking the key has a shorter key list instead of one holding `null`: `[{"k":3},{"k":null},{}] | sort_by(.k)` now puts `{}` before the explicit `null` rather than tying with it, and `sort_by(.x, .y)` over `[{"x":2},{"x":1},{"y":9}]` is `[{"x":1},{"x":2},{"y":9}]` (it was `{"y":9}` first). Mappings sort the same way.
- **yq: `min` and `max` of an array follow yq's comparator instead of jq's total order** (#4055, #4236).
  `[2, "10", 3] | min` printed `2` and yq stops with `!!str not yet supported for comparison`; the same for booleans (`[true, false] | min`), containers (`arrays`/`maps not yet supported for comparison`, `!!seq ([0]) cannot be subtracted from !!int`) and any two scalars of different kinds. A `null` element never takes part (`[null, 1] | min` is `null`, `[1, null]` is `1`, where jq sorts `null` first) and a tie keeps the first element for `max` as well (`[1, 1.0] | max` is `1`). The route over a document's own array and the one over a computed array agree. The values of a mapping (`{a: true, b: false} | min`) and `min_by`/`max_by` keep jq's ordering.
- **jq: a `foreach` UPDATE that is a pipe into a comma with a navigating sibling, or a sibling that navigates and then computes, no longer drops a path or writes where jq raises** (#4059, #4063; a #4041 residual). `(foreach .a as $v (0; 1 | (not, ($v|.b?)); try ($v|.b?))) = 9` on `{"a":null,"z":{"b":1}}` raises `Cannot index number with string "b"` in jq (it names `["a","b"]` and `["a","b","b"]`, and the second write meets the number the first one wrote) and was `{"a":{"b":{"b":9}},"z":{"b":1}}` here, with `path(...)` answering only `[["a","b","b"]]`. Two causes. The comma states jq's register per sibling, but only a comma at the head of UPDATE had that statement read, so behind a stage that cannot move the register (`1 | ...`, `length | ...`) the first sibling's register was lost; a pipe is now read through its last stage when every stage ahead of it cannot move the register. And a sibling that navigated and then computed (`$v|.b?|tostring`, `$v|.b?|not`) leaves jq's register on what it navigated to, which the fold took for its own register whenever the two values were equal (`null`, `true`, `false`) and so ran EXTRACT from the wrong node (`path(...)` answered `[["a","b"],["a","b"]]` where jq has `[["a","b"],["a","b","b"]]`); EXTRACT now runs from the node the register moved to. A seeded grid of UPDATE shapes against jq 1.7.1 fixes rows with no regression, and a sample of the register sweep over all 565 operands is identical to `main`.
- **jq: a `foreach` UPDATE comma with a pipe on the accumulator, or a trailing `| .`, no longer drops a path or writes where jq raises over a `null` source** (#4063, a #4059 residual). `(foreach .a as $v (null; (now, (. | .b?)); try ($v|.b?))) = 9` on `{"a":null,"z":{"b":1}}` raises `Cannot index number with string "b"` in jq (it names `["a","b"]` and `["a","b","b"]`) and was `{"a":{"b":{"b":9}},"z":{"b":1}}` here, with `path(...)` answering only `[["a","b","b"]]`; `(foreach .a as $v (.; ((1,2), ($v|.b?)) | .; try ($v|.b?))) = 9` did the same. Over a `null` source the accumulator is identical to jq's register, so the sibling `. | .b?` navigates and the neutral builtin beside it is a by-value leaf on a *trackable* entry, which stated the register lost; and a trailing `| .` made the pipe read as opaque, so the comma's per-sibling statements went unread. A bare register-neutral builtin now states the register unmoved on a trackable entry too, a comma sibling that leaves the register alone states the entry value there, and a trailing `| .` forwards the statement of the stage before it. The same change lets eight refusals of the register sweep (`del(try (any(now; .a) and .a))`, ...) match jq. A 2,592-row matrix (INIT x sibling pair x trailing `.`, two documents) against jq 1.7.1 fixes 528 rows with no regression; the 48 rows left all hold a sibling that navigates through the accumulator and then computes (`. | .b? | tostring`).
- **yq: `style = "tagged"` writes the value's type tag** (#4066, the last piece of #2707). It exited
  with `not yet supported`; `.a style = "tagged"` now prints `a: !!int 1`, `!!str x`, `!!float 1.5`,
  `!!bool true`, `!!null null`, and `!!seq`/`!!map` on the header line of a block container
  (`a: &an !!map`, before a flow or empty one), derived from the value as it is at write time. A
  string is not quoted for reading back as another type (`!!str 1`, `!!str null`), only for what
  the syntax needs (`!!str 'x: y'`), a multi-line one is `!!str |-`, and the empty string is the tag
  alone. Checked against yq v4.53.3 on about 2,000 random strings and the triage matrix. Not
  matched: a non-decimal integer's spelling (`!!int 31` for `0x1F`, #2802), `!!timestamp`, an
  explicit source tag (#1416).
- **jq: a `foreach` UPDATE the resolver cannot prove leaves jq's register where the step entered (a `try` whose handler navigates a frozen `$v`, `select(true)`, a `def` call), followed by an EXTRACT `try ($v|.b?)`, no longer drops a path or skips a write; it refuses loudly where jq answers** (#4071, a #4063 follow-up). `[path(foreach .a as $v (0; try (length|.) catch ($v|.b) | .; try ($v|.b?)))]` on `{"a":{"b":{"b":3}},"z":1}` is `[["a","b"]]` in jq and was `[]` here, and `(foreach ...) = 9` and `del(foreach ...)` wrote nothing and exited 0 where jq writes `{"a":{"b":9},"z":1}` and `{"a":{},"z":1}`; `select(true)` and a `def f: .+1; f` UPDATE did the same. The resolver left the register unrecorded as lost there, so EXTRACT's refusal of `$v` read as jq's verdict and the `try` around it swallowed it. The register is now recorded lost at the step's entry (jq mode, a live register only, and not when UPDATE's output itself navigated), which makes the refusal the resolver's guess and uncatchable (#3267). A handler that cannot move the register, and a `try` with no stage after it, still answer as jq does. Over the 11 register-sweep operands added for the `try` shape (146,547 rows), the 2,773 rows that accepted a wrong answer and the 45 that answered wrongly are gone; 652 rows that matched jq now refuse (480 on a `null` input, where the dropped write was a no-op anyway), because a body that did not raise cannot be told from one that did. The 12 operands for `select`, a `def` call and the issue's own shapes (159,867 rows) go from 1,511 wrong accepts and 27 wrong answers to 377 and 5 (the rest is #4252, identical on `main`), and lose 396 matches.
- **yq: a write keeps the document's explicit tags** (#4078). Any DOM write (`=`, `|=`, `del()`, `-P`,
  `-i`, `--arg`) re-emitted the document without them, so `yq -i '.Resources.B.Properties.Other = 1'`
  turned `Name: !Ref Param` into `Name: Param`, `!GetAtt [Q, Arn]` into `[Q, Arn]` and an application
  tag on a mapping into a plain one: a CloudFormation template was silently a different document after
  any edit. Tags on scalars, mappings and sequences are now kept (`!Foo` on a block mapping goes on
  its header line, behind any anchor; before a flow or empty collection), along with `!!str 1`,
  `!!float 1` and `!!int "2"`. A written node keeps a custom tag and loses a core tag its new value no
  longer has, `-P` drops the core tags that only restate a type, as yq does. Checked against yq v4.53.3
  on about 1,900 random tagged documents. A node a write copies from elsewhere (`.b = .a`) still loses
  its tag.
- **yq: a numeric, boolean or `null` index on a mapping finds the member by its key text, for reads and writes** (#4079). yq's `matchKey` compares texts, so on `abc: 1 / 1: y / true: t / null: n / 1.5: w` `.[1]` is `"y"`, `.[true]` is `"t"`, `.[null]` is `"n"` and `.[1.5]` is `"w"` (all were `null`, or `Cannot index object with boolean/null`), `.[1] | key` is `1`, `.[1] | path` is `[1]`, and `.[1] = "z"`, `.[1] |= . + "!"`, `.[true] = "z"` and a computed `1 as $k | .[$k] = "z"` update the member, while `.[2] = "z"` creates the key `2` and `.a[0][].b = 9` on `a: {}` is `{"a":{"0":[]}}` (they raised `Cannot index object with number`). A miss is still `null` (#2459) and an array keeps its positions; `del(.[null])` and friends on a mapping are now yq's no-op instead of an error. Reads work on the cursor and eager evaluators; single-target writes (`=`, `|=`, `+=`, `style=`/`anchor=`/`line_comment=`, a computed key) work on both. 53 rows captured from yq v4.53.3 and a unit test of the eager route pin it. Grouped and multi-target writes follow in #4085. Not changed: `.[01]` is read as the integer `1` where yq finds the `01:` key, and names with other punctuation (`.a+1`).
- **yaml: a node tag in front of a flow collection inside a flow sequence now parses** (#4081). `a: [!Foo {a: 1}]`, `[x, !Foo {a: 1}]`, `[!!str null, !Foo {a: 1}]` and `a: !!seq [!!str null, !Foo {a: !x.y 1, c: 2.5}]` were rejected (`Error: YAML parse error: unexpected character ']' at offset 15: expected ':' in implicit flow mapping entry`, exit 1, no output) where yq accepts them. The lookahead that decides whether a flow-sequence entry is an implicit single-pair mapping (`[k: v]`) skipped a leading anchor or alias but not a tag, so it scanned `!Foo {a` up to the `: ` inside the braces and took the tagged mapping for a pair whose key is `!Foo {a`. It now skips node properties (an anchor, an alias, a tag, in either order, a verbatim `!<tag:x,y>` included) and decides on what follows, as the real parse does. The same lookahead required the `:` after a flow-collection key to touch the closing bracket, so `[!Foo {a: 1} : v]` only parsed by accident (through the `: ` inside the braces) and the fix above would have rejected it; spaces and tabs before the `:` are now allowed after a flow collection as they already were after a quoted key, which also makes `[{a: 1} : v]` and `[[1] : v]` parse as yq reads them. `[!Foo k: v]`, `[!Foo "k": v]`, `[&x !Foo {a: 1}, *x]`, `[!Foo {a: 1}: v]` and `[!Foo [1], 2]` match yq. In a one-off sweep (not a committed test), output was identical to yq's across 2,400 tag/anchor/collection/context combinations on the default, JSON, `.a` and `-P`/write routes except two tag-rendering gaps that parsed before this change (a tag on an empty flow collection or on an implicit-pair key is dropped on YAML output, #4088).
- **yq: a numeric index on a mapping also works inside a grouped or multi-target write and a `del()` continuation** (#4085). After #4079 a write whose targets were enumerated first still raised `Cannot index object with number` where yq updates the member: on `a: {1: y, 2: z, x: 1}`, `(.a[1], .a[2]) = 7`, `(.a[1], .a.x) |= "q"`, `(.a[1] // .z) = 3`, `(.a | select(.[1] == "y") | .[1]) = 1` and `(.a[1], .l[0]) = 3` now update the `1:`/`2:` members. `del()` follows yq's two-sided rule: `del(.a[1], .l[0])` leaves the mapping's `1:` member alone (a terminal index on a mapping deletes nothing) while `del(.a[1].b)` and `del(.a[1].b, .l[0])` delete `b` from it. Pinned by 23 rows captured from yq v4.53.3; a 1,760-row differential of write, `|=`, `del` and grouped shapes over four documents against yq changed 747 rows to yq's answer and none away from it.
- **yq: a write keeps the first document's `---` marker** (#4086). Any DOM write (`=`, `|=`, `del()`,
  `-P`, `-i`) dropped a leading `---`, so editing a Kubernetes manifest, an Ansible playbook or a
  generated file that opens with it changed the first line (about 220 of the file/filter pairs that
  differed from yq in a sweep of 2,178 real YAML files). The text before the first document's content
  is now printed back when it holds a `---` on a line of its own: the comments and blank lines above
  it, verbatim, and the marker. Only the first document of a file gets it, `-N` drops the marker lines
  and keeps the comments, and a root that a write replaces keeps it too. Content on the marker's own
  line (`--- 5`) and `%YAML` directives are not handled.
- **yq: a boolean or `null` index into an absent container reads as `null` and a write builds a mapping keyed by its text** (#4087). On a document with no `a`, `.a[true]`, `.a[null]`, `.a[true].b` and `[.a[true]]` are `null` and `.a[true] = 1`, `.a[null] |= 5`, `.a[true][0] = 1`, `(.a[true], .x) = 1` and a computed `true as $k | .a[$k] = 1` build `a: {true: 1}`, `a: {null: 5}`, `a: {true: [1]}` (they raised `Cannot index null with boolean`/`null`); `del(.a[true])` and `del(.a[true], .x)` are no-ops. jq mode still raises. A boolean or `null` key on a scalar target is yq's no-op, as a numeric key is. Pinned by 32 rows captured from yq v4.53.3 and an eager-route unit test; a 5,376-row differential of reads, `?`, `=`, `|=`, `+=`, `del`, chained and grouped shapes over six documents against yq changed 1,427 rows to yq's answer and none away from it. Not changed: a `del()` through such a key on an explicit `null` (`d: ~`) stays `null` where yq vivifies `{}`, and a computed key that is `null` only because its source field is absent (`.a[.b]`) is not told apart from a literal one (yq: `a: []`).
- **yq: a tag on a flow collection, an empty flow collection or a mapping key is kept on YAML output** (#4088). `a: !!seq [1, 2]` printed `a: [1, 2]` (and `.a` printed `[1, 2]`) on the cursor-streaming route, because only a block container's tag was written there; `a: !Foo {x: 1}`, `- !Foo [1]` and a tagged root collection lost theirs the same way. On the DOM routes (`-P`, `=`, `|=`, `del()`) a tag on a mapping key (`!Foo k: v`, `!!str 1: v`, the key of an implicit pair `[!Foo k: v]`) was dropped outright, and `-P` also dropped a core tag on a container it does not restate (`!!str []`, `!!seq {}`, `!!int {a: 1}`), keeping only `!!seq` on a sequence and `!!map` on a mapping as yq does. Output now matches yq v4.53.3 on all of these; a core `!!null` on a container is still dropped by `-P` (#4111).
- **yaml: a flow collection, alias or tagged value in a flow-sequence pair entry is no longer wrapped or emptied** (#4091). `a: [k: [c]]` answered `{"a":[{"k":[["c"]]}]}` (one sequence level too deep), `a: [k: {x: 1}]` answered `{"k":{}}`, `a: [&x 1, k: *x]` answered `{"k": null}`, and `[? k : [c]]` shared the first, silently and with exit 0, where yq answers `{"k":["c"]}`, `{"k":{"x":1}}` and `{"k":1}`. The single-pair forms of a flow sequence (`[k: v]` and `[? k : v]`) opened a BP node for the value and then called `parse_flow_sequence`/`parse_flow_mapping`, which open a node of their own, so a sequence value was a one-element sequence holding it and a mapping value's members landed outside it; and they read an alias value as a plain scalar. They now share one value parser with the flow mapping (properties, then an alias, a collection with its own node, or a wrapped scalar). A one-off sweep of 7 key forms x 17 value forms x 5 contexts x 4 routes against yq v4.53.3 found no row that matched before and differs now; plain, quoted, explicit and anchored keys now match yq on every route. Still different from yq, unchanged by this fix: a complex key (`[{a: 1}: v]`) renders as `{"": v}` / `{"": v}` in YAML where yq writes `? {a: 1} : v`, an empty value (`[k:]`) is a pair where yq reads the plain scalar `k:`, and a tag on a pair's key is dropped on YAML output (#4088).
- **yq: a write keeps the blank lines between a head-comment block and the node below it** (#4093).
  `# lead` / blank / `version: 2` lost the blank line on any DOM write (`=`, `|=`, `del()`, `-P`, `-i`):
  the single most common divergence from yq in a sweep of 2,178 real YAML files (any file that opens
  with a comment header and a blank line). They are kept, one entry per blank line, for a node at
  column 0; yq drops them for an indented node and for a block that itself follows a blank line (it
  reads that as the previous node's foot), and so does this.
- **yq: `recurse(.[]?; cond)` stops at an alias and gives `key`, `path`, `parent`, `line` and `column` a position** (#4095). The owned walk it replaced expanded every alias (a 29-node document counted 51) and read no position, so `[recurse(.[]?; true) | path]` was a list of `[]`. It now answers what `..` does for `cond` = `true` with a single-output tail, node for node, and what `path(recurse(.[]?; cond))` does for a pruning `cond` that reads no `type` tag on a document without aliases. The walk asks `cond` as it reaches each node in the shapes it streams, so `limit` stops it where jq stops (`[limit(3; recurse(.[]?; debug | true) | path)]` asks `cond` twice), and a bare `recurse(.[]?; cond)` prints what `..` prints, including a document's leading head comment, which the owned walk's output dropped. A write through it, `path(recurse(.[]?; cond))` over aliases, and a `cond` the walk cannot ask at a position (one that reads `key`, `path` or `tag`) are unchanged ([#4223](https://github.com/rust-works/succinctly/issues/4223)).
- **yq: an input with no bytes at all is one empty document, not an error** (#4099). `printf '' | yq '.a'` is `null`, `.a = 1` is `a: 1`, `length` is `0` and `.` prints a blank line; `succinctly yq` stopped with `YAML parse error: empty input` (exit 1) for empty stdin and for an empty file, in the pipelines where an empty config is routine. It reads as the document `yq` reads it as (`null` for a `.json` input). With several inputs an empty one reads no document and the others are read, and a run of empty files reads one empty document, as in yq (`file_index` stays the file's place on the command line). `--front-matter` on an empty input, and the few outputs an empty document prints differently from a line-break one, are recorded in the yq limitations. The other items of the #4099 sweep stay open.
- **jq: `first`/`limit`/`nth` over `to_entries`, `sort`, `add`, `map(f)` (for an `f` that navigates nothing), `reverse` or `input_line_number` keep jq's path register, so a write is no longer silently skipped under a `try`** (#4108). `del(.a? as $y | try ((.a)? and first(to_entries)) | try ($y | .b))` on `{"a":{"b":1},"k":2}` printed the document unchanged, exit 0, where jq 1.7.1 deletes `.a.b` (`{"a":{},"k":2}`): the wrapper was refused where the bare stage was answered, and the `try` swallowed the refusal as though it were jq's own path error. `stage_is_register_keeping` now reads the leaf verdict for the peeled stage, and `input_line_number` joins the by-value stages that verdict lists. Checked against jq 1.7.1 on 44 rows through `path`, `del`, `|=` and the `-n` route. `first(path(f))` is still refused: admitting `path(f)` to the leaf verdict turned a loud refusal into a silent skipped write on a shape `test_transparent_bind_source_matches_identity_bind_3402` pins, so it needs its own fix (#4118).
- **jq: a `def` call over a register-keeping body keeps the path register, as in jq** (#4109). `succinctly jq 'path(. as $x | def g: last(.a); g | $x)'` on `{"a":{"b":1},"k":2}` raised `Invalid path expression with result {...}` where jq 1.7.1 prints `[]`, and the same held for a body of `select(f)`, a type filter, a `try` over one, a comma of them, a call of a call and a call inside `first(g)`, through `del`, `=` and `|=`. A zero-argument call is now read as its body is (the resolver already resolves the bound body against the call's own input), within the one shared budget of 16 bodies that #4124's literal-body rule uses. A body that navigates (`def g: .a`, `first(.a)`, `last(.a) | .b`) still moves the register and raises, and a call with an argument stays refused.
- **yq: a key deleted and written again keeps nothing of the old key** (#4113). `del(.k) | .k = 1` on `&a k: v` printed `&a k: 1` (and `!Foo k: 1` for a tagged key, and the old key's quoting and comment), where yq gives the new key none of them; a closed literal written there also no longer inherits the old value's comment. `.a |= {"k": 3}` is now the same write as `.a = {"k": 3}` (it kept the old key's `!Foo`). Swept 352 delete-and-write shapes (literal, compound, nested and `|=` writes over anchored, tagged, quoted, commented and `? `-keyed keys) and 968 `=`/`|=` literal shapes against yq v4.53.3: 0 rows moved from matching to differing in either, and the first went from 155 differing to 33 (`.k = .j` and `.k as $x | del(.k) | .k = $x` still take the deleted key's value comment/anchor, recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`; the rest are unrelated to recreation).
- **jq: `path(isempty(g))` answers through a `?//` that swallows its `first`'s break** (#4114). jq defines `isempty(g)` as `first((g | false), true)`, so a `?//` inside `g` catches the break after the first `false` (or the path error the consumer raises on it) and retries its next alternative; a retry that comes up dry leaves `g` running to its end and fires the trailing `true`. The resolver stopped at `g`'s first output, so `path(.x | isempty(. as $q ?// $z | if $q then true else empty end))` on `{"x":true}` was refused with `Invalid path expression with result false` where jq prints `["x"]`, and `del`/`|=` of it exited 5 where jq writes. `isempty` now hands each answer to the consumer from inside the drain, as `any`/`all` do (#3827, #3899): one `false` per answering alternative, the consumer's side effects ahead of the retry's, and the identity `true` once `g` ran to its end. yq mode is unchanged.
- **jq: a `?//` bind whose destructure succeeds now retries the next alternative when the body leads with a navigation step** (#4115).
  `path(.x | (. as [$q] ?// $z | (.[0]?, true)))` on `{"x":[true]}` refused without printing anything where jq prints `["x",0]`
  and then raises `with result true`, and `. as [$q] ?// $z | .[0]` refused where jq answers `["x",0]` (`del`/`=` likewise). The
  destructure moves jq's register onto the bound node, so the body's first step on the ambient fails jq's own `path_intact`
  check, which is what sends jq to the next alternative; the resolver now retries on that refusal when the body leads with the
  navigation and the ambient is not equal to the moved register's value. Other body shapes keep their refusal. Applies to `succinctly jq` outside a `reduce`/`foreach` body, where the fold keeps its refusal.
- **jq: `path(f)` as a pipe stage leaves the path register where it entered, so `first(path(f))`, `limit(n; path(f))`, `nth(n; path(f))` and a bare `path(f)` stage answer as jq does** (#4118). `path(. as $x | first(path(.a)) | $x)` on `{"a":{"b":1},"k":2}` raised `Invalid path expression` where jq answers `[]`, and under a `try` the refusal skipped a write: `del(.a? as $y | try ((.a)? and first(path(.a))) | try ($y | .b))` echoed the document where jq deletes `.a.b`. Over the three `path(f)` operands of the path-register sweep (39,987 rows, whole grid) 795 rows changed with none moving the other way: `MATCH` 38,406 to 39,201, `REFUSE_WRONG` 1,578 to 786, `DIFF` 3 to 0.
- **jq: an `as` bind whose source mixes a bare `.` with a `$var` marker, on a stage that computed a value, no longer lets a `try` skip the write** (#4118). `del(. as $v0 | length | (if true then $v0 else . end) as $v1 | try (($v1 | .[]?) | .b?))` (also with `keys` and `to_entries`) printed the document unchanged where jq deletes `.b` under each key: on a stage that is not the register, `.` is the computed value while `$v0` still names the register's node, so the source is no passthrough of either, yet it was bound as an exact marker and the `try` swallowed the refusal. It is now a loud `Invalid path expression` (jq answers; the safe direction). A `.` only in a condition (`if (.>0) then $v0 else $v0 end`), a bare `$v0` and a bare `.` source are unchanged.
- **jq: a recursion or other register producer inside a pipe nested in `if`, `first`, `try`, `limit`, a comma or a `def` now states the path register** (#4123).
  `path(. as $x | 1 | first(.. | select(true)) | $x)` is `[]` in jq and was a refusal here; `(.. | .)` and `(.. | select(f))`
  behind any of those forwarders now answer, and so do the `del`/`=`/`|=` forms. Over the 55 sweep operands that generate the shapes
  (46,563 `--stage-only` rows) 562 refusals and 80 wrong answers became matches, no regression.
- **jq: a call to a zero-arity `def` whose body is a literal keeps the path register, so `try path(...)` over it answers as jq does** (#4124).
  `try path(. as $x | def f: 1; f | $x)` printed nothing at exit 0 (and the bare `path` refused) where jq
  prints `[]`: the call read as a stage that may have moved the register, although `1 | $x` already did not.
  A call now leaves the register where its body does (looking through at most 16 nested calls), and an
  `if` with a literal condition reads only the branch it runs (`if false then .. else 1 end`). A body that
  navigates (`def f: .a`) still refuses, as jq's does.
- **jq: a `try ... catch` operand of `and`/`or` or unary minus that reads the register is refused in path position, as jq refuses it** (#4125).
  `del((.a)? or try (.a | error) catch .)` removed `.a`, `path(try (select(. // 1) | error) catch (.a)? and .[0])`
  printed nothing and `del(-(try (if true then error(. // 5) else . end) catch (.a)?))` was a silent no-op, where jq
  raises `Invalid path expression ...` (exit 5). The right operand now runs from the register the left operand left
  (a body that navigates before it always raises is no longer evaluated from the entry), and a handler whose payload
  may be the register's own node no longer has its `(.a)?` quietly pruned. Over a seeded 12,000-row sample of the
  path-register sweep's `try`/`catch` operands the build writes where jq refuses on 0 rows (18 on `main`) and
  refuses where jq answers on 13 more (219 against 206), all of them under an outer `try` that jq uses to swallow
  the path error.
- **jq: a `reduce` whose UPDATE is a `try ... catch` handler that navigates is refused in path position, as jq refuses it** (#4126).
  `del(reduce 1 as $k (.; try (., error) catch (.a)?))` wrote `null` over the whole document, and
  `path(reduce (1,2) as $k (.; try (., error) catch (.a)?))` printed `[]`, where jq raises
  `Invalid path expression with result ...` (exit 5). Over a source and INIT that cannot move jq's register,
  the handler now runs with `.` on the register, so its `.a` moves it off the accumulator and the final path
  check refuses. A navigating source (`reduce .[]? as $k (...)`) still answers `[]`, as jq does.
- **jq: a `catch` handler that navigates a `$x` the `try` body raised is a path when `$x` is the node the `try` stood on** (#4127). `path(.s | try (. as $y | .[0] | error($y)) catch .[0])` on `{"s":[1]}` refused with `Invalid path expression near attempt to access element 0 of [1]` where jq 1.7.1 answers `["s",0]`: `error`'s argument is evaluated with path tracking suspended and the handler runs against the register the `try`'s fork restored, so a variable frozen at the `try`'s own node is that node however the body stepped off it first. A `try` entered on a path-tracked value whose body can raise only a message string or such a `$x` (`.[0] | error($y)`, `.[] | error($y)`, `if .[0] == 1 then error($y) else . end`, `(., error($y))`, with `$y` bound inside the body or before the `try` at the same position) now hands the handler that node, an empty array and a scalar register included, through `path`, `del`, `=` and `|=`, and the stage after it (`| first(.)`, `| .a?`). A `$x` frozen at another position (the root, `.[0]`, a navigated bind when the `try` stood elsewhere), a rebound variable, a body that can raise anything else (`error({"a":1})`, `error($y|tojson)`) or a string register still refuses, as in jq or as before. Refuse-only before.
- **jq: a `reduce`/`foreach` whose source destructures the register, or is a fold that does, no longer answers where jq raises a path error, so `del` can no longer wipe the document through it** (#4128). `del(reduce .[]? as $k (.; foreach ((.|.) | reduce . as {a:$a} (0; .)) as $x (.; .; .)))` on `{"a":false,"b":null}` printed `null` (exit 0, the document deleted) where jq 1.7.1 raises `Invalid path expression near attempt to access element "a"`. The destructure `. as {a:$a}` is a tracked `INDEX` step run against the value in hand, which raises when that value is not the register (an untracked entry such as `{a:{b:1}} | ...`, or the accumulator of an enclosing fold whose source navigated); the by-value drive of a fold source ran it unchecked. A source that destructures `.` anywhere in its spine, a nested `reduce` and a `select(true) as {...}` bind included, is now resolved when the register is not known to be at `.`. Over the 95 destructuring-fold operands of the path-register sweep (40,000 sampled rows, seed 21) `ACCEPT_WRONG` went from 42 to 11 and `DIFF` from 10 to 9 with no row moving toward a wrong answer; 13 rows jq answers (contrived `?//`/nested-fold shapes) are now refused, in the safe direction.
- **jq: a `foreach` with a destructuring pattern states jq's path register per step** (#4129, first part).
  `del(. as $x | (foreach . as {("a"):$a} ?// $a (0; .; .)) | $x)` on `[true]` refused ("Invalid path expression with
  result") where jq answers `null`, and `=`/`|=` through such a `$x` refused the same way. A step that took no walk step
  (the bare `$var` alternative reached after a destructure failed) emits at the register the fold entered with, so a `$x`
  frozen before the fold is that register; a step that walked still states nothing and keeps refusing. Over the 185,211
  `--stage-only` sweep rows of every `foreach` operand: REFUSE_WRONG 4,464 -> 4,424, no regression, wrong accepts and wrong
  answers unchanged. A `try`-wrapped destructuring `reduce` and a fold entered under a `?//` bind are still refused (#4129).
- **jq: a `try ... catch` over a destructuring bind or fold no longer hides the register from the stage after it** (#4129, second part).
  `path(. as $x | {a:1} | (try (. as [$a] | $a) catch 7) | $x)` on `[{"a":1}]` and
  `path(. as $x | {a:{b:1}} | (try (reduce . as [$a] ?// $a (0; .)) catch 7) | $x)` raised `Invalid path expression with
  result` where jq answers `[]`, and `del`/`=` through such a `$x` refused the same way. A destructuring bind is now read
  from its body alone (its source is a subexpression and states nothing), and a `reduce`/`foreach` that destructures is
  read per result under a handler that navigates nothing. Over 13 new sweep operands (a seeded 15,000-row sample of the
  full grid, plus their 11,571 `--stage-only` rows) and a seeded 40,000-row `--stage-only` sample over the 506
  bind/fold/`catch` operands: REFUSE_WRONG 327 -> 233, 940 -> 888 and 648 -> 252, none lost, wrong accepts and wrong
  answers unchanged. A `try` handler that navigates, a body that holds a `.`, a fold entered under a `?//` bind (#4129
  item 3, which is a `?//` retry rule rather than a fold one) and a `foreach` UPDATE under a `?//` bind are still refused.
- **jq: a `foreach` on an untracked stage states its register at the emissions that navigated nothing** (#4130). A `foreach` emits from inside the loop, so the register an emission carries is where the pattern walk and `UPDATE` left it; on an untracked entry it stated none, so a result jq answers was refused at the result. The register the fold entered with is now stated on an emission whose step took no walk step (a bare `$var`, or the bare alternative a failed destructure's restored fork reached) and whose source, `INIT`, `UPDATE` and `EXTRACT` cannot move it, and a loss on every other one: `del(.a and (foreach . as {a:$a} ?// $a (0; .; .)))` on `{"a":true}` is jq's `{}` (it exited 5 with `Invalid path expression with result true`), and `path(. as $x | 5 | (foreach . as {a:$q} ?// $a (0; .; .)) | $x)` is `[]`. A navigating source, `UPDATE` or `EXTRACT`, a destructure that succeeds and a register an earlier `.a` moved still refuse, as in jq.
- **jq: a `reduce` on an untracked entry follows an `UPDATE` that navigates a `null`/boolean accumulator** (#4131).
  `path(.a | 5 | reduce null as {a:$q} (null; .b))` on `{"a":null}` refused at `.b` ("of null") where jq answers `["a"]`.
  `null` and the booleans are `jv_identical` to an equal one by kind, so an accumulator holding one is on the register the
  stage carries (#4049) and the step passes `path_intact`; a boolean accumulator now raises jq's own `Cannot index boolean`,
  and `del`/`=` through the fold land on `.a`. A register that is not `null`/boolean, a fold that mentions a frozen `$var`, and an `UPDATE` that nests a fold or a
  `try ... catch` around the navigation still refuse where jq answers (the safe direction).
- **yq: array subtraction compares numbers by their spelling, as yq does** (#4136). `[1.50] - [1.5]` removed the element because the two are equal by value, where yq's `subtractArray` pairs scalars by tag and text (`recursiveNodeEqual`) and answers `[1.50]`; the same held for `1.0 - 1.00`, `1e3 - 1E3`, `-0.0 - 0.0`, a long float against its computed value, and inside a nested array or object. A computed number is spelled the way yq formats it (`[5.0] - [2.5 * 2]` keeps the `5.0`), an int and a float still never match, and the rule is yq-only (`jq`'s `-` still compares by value). Not part of this change: `contains` compares the same way in yq (`[1.50] | contains([1.5])` is `false`) and a computed string key that reads as a number (`{(.a | tostring): 1}`) is still written unquoted.
- **yq: an empty `as` source runs its body once, and an empty index operand stands for every child** (#4139).
  `select(false) as $z | .a` is `.a` in yq (the variable stays unset); it printed nothing here. `.[E]` with no output
  is `.[]`, so `.b[$typo] = 1` sets every element, `.b[$typo] += 1` and `.[$typo] |= f` update them, `del(.[$typo])`
  deletes them all and `.b[$typo]` prints them, while here the same filters left the document unchanged and exited 0.
  `has(E)` with no output is `false`. A scalar operand has no children, so those writes stay no-ops. jq mode is
  unchanged.
- **jq: an `error(msg)` whose message navigates an input the path register is not on raises jq's path error, in path position** (#4146).
  jq defines `error(msg)` as `msg | error`, so the message is path-checked and a `try` catches the path-error
  string. The message was evaluated by value, so the payload was the value it read: `path(.a? or try error(.c) catch .)`
  on `{"a":false,"c":null}` printed `["a"]` where jq exits 5 with `Invalid path expression with result true`,
  and a stage over a constructed value (`path({"c":false} | try error(.c) catch .)`) refused with the wrong text.
- **jq: a `?//` destructuring bind or a `foreach` whose INIT moved the register no longer answers where jq raises a path error, so `|=` and `del` can no longer write through it** (#4150). `(try (((foreach ((., .) as {a:$a} | .) as $x (.; .; .)))) catch .) |= 9` on `{"a":[true]}` printed `9` (the root overwritten) and `del(try ((. as [$q] ?// $z | (.a?, null)) or .[0]))` on `[{"a":1}]` echoed the document, where jq 1.7.1 raises `Invalid path expression` (exit 5). Four causes. A non-last `?//` alternative whose body refused was not retried, and the refusal came back as an ordinary error that an enclosing `try`/`?` swallowed, though jq retries the next alternative and checks what it yields outside the `try`; it is now the uncatchable guess when a later alternative would yield a value, so `try (. as [$q] ?// $z | .a)`, which jq answers `[]`, still does. A pattern that fails by value (`0 as [$q]`) is a certain retry in jq, and now counts as one. A `foreach` whose INIT navigated and then computed ran its SOURCE as if the register were still at the entry. A `(., .) as {..}` source was not routed to the resolver. On the path-register sweep the targeted sample went from 75 wrong accepts to 8 and the whole-grid sample from 14 to 0, none moving toward a wrong answer; 20 contrived `?//` binds under `try`/`?` that jq answers are now refused, in the safe direction. A plain-bind prefix, a bare-`.` `?//` chain and a `(.|.) as {..}` source are still accepted (#4187).
