A backslash and a letter that means nothing there is the letter (`"h" | test("\\h")` was an error, and `"A" | test("\\u0041")` was `true` where jq, which reads `\u0041` as the text `u0041`, says `false`), `\N`, `\O` and `\Q…\E` work, `\101` and `\0` are octal, `\cA` is control-A, `\xc3\xa9` is `é`, and `(*FAIL)` never matches. An interval with nothing to repeat (`{1}`), a group name that starts with a digit or is empty, a short multibyte escape and a backreference or conditional on a group the pattern lacks are errors, as in jq: `"a" | test("(?(2)a|b)")` panicked inside `fancy-regex` and now fails cleanly. `\X`, `\y`, `\Y`, `\g<n>` and octal escapes of 0x80 or more stay refused. Every row was captured from jq 1.7.1.
- **yq: a single-quoted scalar with an empty line is written across lines when it sits in a nested flow collection or is a mapping key** (#6075). `printf "a: [['x\n\n  y']]\n" | yq .` keeps the quotes and indents the continuation by the scalar's depth (`a: [['x`, an empty line, `      y']]`); `succinctly yq` wrote `y']]` at the start of its line, which a reader folds to a space. A mapping key holding the break is `? 'k`, an empty line, `  z'` with the `:` on a line of its own, where `succinctly yq` wrote `'k` and `z': 1` on two lines. Both the streaming and the write route now match yq v4.53.3 on the documents pinned in `tests/yq_cli/i6075.rs`.
- **jq: a regex `{n}+` is the fixed count `{n}`, not a repeat of it** (#6079). `"aaaa" | match("a{2}+")` is `aa` in jq (a fixed count has nothing to give back) and was `aaaa` here, and `.{1}+` matched two characters where jq matches one, with no error. The `+` is dropped, and a quantifier after it applies to the `{n}` (`{n}++` repeats it, `{n}+?` makes it optional), as in jq. Of 3,360 pattern, text and flag rows, those with a fixed `{n}+` now all agree with jq 1.7.1; possessive `{n,m}+` and `*+` are still refused where they are not last.
- **jq: a `$` that something follows, and an escaped letter jq does not define, match as Oniguruma matches** (#6080). `"ab\n" | match("b$\\n")` is `[1,2]` in jq 1.7.1, because `$` matches before a final newline and leaves it for the next token; it found nothing here, and so did `$\n`, `b$\s` and `(?:b$|x)\n`. A pattern with a `$` that is not the last token of its branch or pattern is now read by the exact engine, as one with `\z` already was. `\g`, `\h`, `\i`, `\j`, `\k`, `\l`, `\m`, `\o`, `\q`, `\v` and the capitals `\C`, `\E`, `\F`, `\H`, `\I`, `\J`, `\L`, `\M`, `\T`, `\V` are the letter itself in jq (`"v" | test("\\v")` is `true`): they were a parse error here, and `\v` a vertical tab. `\g<n>` and `\k<n>` keep their meaning.
- **`succinctly jq` finds the empty match a `\K` leaves under the `n` flag** (#6083). `"a1" | [match("1\\K";"n")|[.offset,.length]]` is `[[2,0]]` in jq and was `[]`: the `fancy-regex` route already refuses a match that ends where the attempt began, as Oniguruma's `ONIG_OPTION_FIND_NOT_EMPTY` does, and then a second test measured the span `\K` keeps and refused it again. That second test now runs only on the routes whose engine does not enforce `n`. Every row was captured from jq 1.7.1; `l` with `\K` still differs (`"a1" | match("a\\K1";"l")`, #6085).
- **`succinctly jq` finds the match for the `l` flag with `\K`** (#6085). `"a1" | match("a\\K1";"l")` is `[[1,1]]` in jq and was empty, `"a1b" | match("1\\K|b";"l")` is `[[2,0]]` and was `[[2,1]]`: the longest-match search recorded each candidate by the start `\K` had moved, then searched again from there and found nothing, and compared lengths from that start. A pattern with `\K` under `l` is now searched one start at a time with the pattern anchored there (`\G(?:...)`), and a match is measured from the start of its attempt, as Oniguruma's `ONIG_OPTION_FIND_LONGEST` does. Still different: a pattern whose ways to match at one start keep different spans (`"baa" | match("b?\\K[ab]a*";"l")` is `[[1,2]]` in jq, `[[0,3]]` here), and `l` with an inline `(?x)`. The search tries one start at a time and each search reads the rest of the text, as Oniguruma's does, so `g` with `\K` under `l` is quadratic in the matches (12.8 KB holding 6,400 matches: 6.3 s, M4 Pro).
- **yq: a descent's `|=` updates every level, not only the outer one** (#6087). yq's own recipe for renaming keys everywhere, `(.. | select(tag == "!!map")) |= with_entries(.key |= "KEY_" + .)`, renamed the top-level keys, left the nested ones and added a `b: null` entry that is in neither the input nor yq's answer; `(.. | select(tag == "!!map")) |= keys` raised `Cannot index array with string "b"` where yq answers the keys. The updates address nodes by path, and an outer rename invalidated the path an inner update was recorded under, so a path set from a descent (`..`, `recurse`) is now written deepest first, which keeps a parent's paths intact; equal depths keep their order and any other path set keeps the order it was named in. Ten live yq captures, including `|= {"w": .}`, `|= (. * {"z": 1})`, a second rename pass over the first, and sequences, now match.
- **yq: `$i | path`, `key`, `parent`, `line`, `column` and the other node reads of a `SRC as $i ireduce (INIT; UPDATE)` loop variable answer from the node `$i` is bound to** (#6088). The fold bound the element's value, so `$i | path` was `[]` and yq's documented prune example, `(.b.c2, .c.c1) as $i ireduce({}; setpath($i | path; $i))`, printed the last value (`z`) instead of the pruned document; `$i | key` printed nothing and `$i | line` printed `0`. They now print what yq does, as do `tag`, `style`, `anchor`, the comment readers and `document_index`. A read followed by more stages (`$i | path | length`) is covered; a node reached through a step first (`$i | parent | key`) still sees a value.
- **yq: `(PATH | key) = value` and `(PATH | key) |= filter` rename the key** (#6089). `printf 'a:\n  x: 3\n  y: 4\n' | yq '(.a.x | key) = "meow"'` prints `meow: 3` in place of `x: 3`; `succinctly yq` accepted it and printed the document unchanged with exit 0. The new name keeps the key's quoting, anchor and comments, `|=` binds `.` to the key's text, and a later pipe stage sees the new name (`(.a.x | key) = "z" | .a | keys` is `z`, `y`). A name that is already a member (yq keeps both entries), a mapping or sequence, or a text with a line break is refused with an error, and `+=`, `-=`, `*=` and `//=` on a key target are a parse error where they used to do nothing; the remaining gaps are in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: `upcase` and `downcase` map the Unicode simple case mapping, as yq does** (#6091). They were jq's `ascii_upcase`/`ascii_downcase` under yq's names, so `ágUA | upcase` was `áGUA` where yq prints `ÁGUA`, and `ΑΣ | downcase` stayed as it was where yq prints `ασ`. They now map each character as Go's `strings.ToUpper`/`ToLower` do: `ß` has no single-character uppercase and stays, `İ` lowercases to `i`, the Greek letters with an iota subscript (`ᾀ`) uppercase to their titlecase letter (`ᾈ`), and a case pair Unicode 16 added (`ɤ`/`Ɤ`, `ƛ`/`Ƛ`, the Garay letters) maps neither way, as Go's tables are Unicode 15. Compared with yq v4.53.3 over every printable code point of the basic and supplementary planes, in both directions: identical. jq's `ascii_upcase`/`ascii_downcase`, and `succinctly yq --jq-extensions` `ascii_upcase`, stay ASCII.
- **yq: a mapping or sequence in a string interpolation is its YAML text, not JSON** (#6092). `"I \(.m)"` over `m: {an: apple}` printed `I {"an":"apple"}`; it now prints `I {an: apple}`, as yq does, and a block mapping interpolates as its block text (`I a: 1` / `b: two` over two lines). Each `\(...)` slot is now a `to_string` stage, so a container reads as `to_string` makes it, and a node written in flow style stays flow for a slot of plain navigation or `//` of it (`"\(.m)"`, `"\(.a // "d")"`). A slot that is a call, `..` or a write's right-hand side is read from an owned copy and prints a flow container as block (`.x = "got \(.m)"` writes `got an: apple`; yq `got {an: apple}`). jq mode keeps `tostring`'s JSON text, as jq does.
- **jq: a regex with two greedy `X+` repeats and one optional repeat between them, on the second engine, is refused instead of answered wrongly** (#6096). `"a" | test("(?=a)a+a*a+")` was `true` (upstream `fancy-regex` 0.20.0) where jq and the `regex` crate say `false`, and `a+b*a+`, `.+.*.+`, `a+a?a+` and `(?:ab)+c*(?:ab)+` behind a lookahead, a backreference or `\K` did the same. Such a pattern now gives `invalid regex` for any text; the same shape with nothing that needs the second engine, and with `l` or `n`, keeps its normal route and answers as jq does. Two repeats between the plusses, a mandatory item, another atom and bounded repeats are not affected.
- **yq: `sort_by(key)` on a mapping sorts by the key** (#6099). yq sorts a mapping's entries by the key filter with `key` naming the entry's key node (its "Sort a map by keys" example, `sort_by(key | downcase)` too). `succinctly yq` ran the filter on the entry's value, where `key` names nothing, so the mapping came back in its input order. `key` at the head of the filter (`key`, `key | f`, a comma of those) now reads the entry's key, which sorts by the kind the text resolves to (`null`, then booleans, numbers, strings), so `10` follows `9`. A `key` below another step (`.a | key`) is unchanged. A quoted key that reads as a number or boolean sorts as one: the mapping reaches the sort as JSON text, which no longer says it was quoted.
- **yq: `pivot` pads a short row with an empty node, as yq does** (#6102). `printf -- '- [foo, bar]\n- [sis]\n' | yq pivot` prints `-` with no value for the cell the short row lacks; `succinctly yq` printed `null`. A `pivot` that is the whole filter now also moves every cell with its own comment, quoting, anchor, alias and tag (`"c"`, `&x d` and `# cc` used to come out plain) and quotes a mapping key that reads as another type (`"1":`). `-o=json` still prints `null`. A `pivot` inside a larger filter (`[pivot]`, `.x |= pivot`, `pivot | .[1][1]`) still pads with `null`; the gaps are listed in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: `unique` keeps `~`, `null`, `Null` and an empty value apart, as yq does** (#6103). yq keys an element on its text, so `- ~` / `- null` / `- ~` / `- 1` / `- null` gives `~`, `null`, `1`; `succinctly yq` keyed a `null` by its decoded value and kept only the first (`~`, `1`). `unique` and `unique_by(.)` over a document's elements now key a `null` by the way the source spells it, and a container that holds one by the spellings of its nulls too (`[~]` and `[null]` are two elements). `unique_by(.a)`, `group_by`, an array the filter builds and an anchored or aliased element still read a decoded `null`; they are listed in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **jq: a greedy regex loop ends at an iteration that matches nothing, as Oniguruma's does** (#6106). A loop body whose empty way came before a consuming one matched longer than jq: `"ba" | sub("(?:b*|a)+"; "X")` was `"X"` and is now jq's `"Xa"`, and `"foo-bar" | gsub("(?:\\w*|-)+"; "X")` was `"XX"` and is now `"XX-XX"`. A bounded repeat ends at its empty way the same way. A body with a capture group, a zero-width assertion or a flag switch, and a pattern that goes to `fancy-regex`, keep the longer match (recorded in `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **jq: a group repeated `{0}` keeps its capture entry** (#6108). `"ab" | match("(a){0}b")` had no capture where jq reports one (offset `-1`, string `null`; an empty string at the match offset when the whole match is empty), so `.captures` was one entry short whenever no later group followed the `{0}` group, `capture` dropped the named key and `scan` returned the match instead of the capture array. `{0}`, `{0,0}`, `{00}`, a lazy or stacked repeat and groups nested inside one are all counted, as in jq.
- **jq: `strftime(f)` and `strflocaltime(f)` with a format that is not a string report the input's fault first, as jq does** (#6111). They raised `expected string, got strftime format` for every input. jq tests the input before the format: `null | strftime(1)` is `strftime/1 requires parsed datetime inputs`, a broken-down-time array is `strftime/1 requires a string format`, and a number outside the range is `error converting number of seconds since epoch to datetime` (`strflocaltime/1` in the local-zone builtin's wording). A number that converts still raises succinctly's own error, since jq aborts there (#3046).
- **jq: `--seq` with `--stream` or `--stream-errors` feeds the filter the events of each record** (#6115). The flags were ignored under `--seq`, so `printf '\x1e[1]\n\x1e{"a":2}\n' | succinctly jq -c --seq --stream .` printed the two records where jq prints `[[0],1]`, `[[0]]`, `[["a"],2]` and `[["a"]]`, and `--seq --stream-errors` never turned a fault into the `[message, path]` event jq prints.
  Both now read with the port of jq's streaming parser (`jq_stream_errors.rs`) in its record-sequence mode, so a record cut short still yields the events before the cut, and the fault is jq's own warning (`jq: ignoring parse error: Truncated value at line 2, column 1`), or under `--stream-errors` an event.
  `input`/`inputs` raise a fault as an error, `-s` closes its array where jq does, and `input_line_number`/`input_filename` follow jq's reader; 15,500 random record sequences over stdin and up to three files, with long lines across jq's 4,095-byte read, matched `/usr/bin/jq` 1.7.1 on stdout, status and the set of stderr lines.
- **jq: a module name that starts with `/` is joined onto each search directory** (#6120). `import "/a" as a` with `-L lib` found no module (`module not found: /a`) where jq reads `lib//a.jq`, i.e. `lib/a.jq`, and `import "<abs path>/a"` found one jq reports as not found; `include`, a data import (`import "/d" as $d`) and `modulemeta` followed. The name is now joined onto every search directory the way jq does, with `-L /` the one way to reach an absolute path.
- **jq: a regex group option other than `i`, `m`, `x`, `s` is an error, as in jq** (#6126). `"a" | test("(?U)a")` printed `true` and `"aa" | [match("(?U)a+") | .string]` swapped greedy and lazy quantifiers, where jq 1.7.1 answers `undefined group option`; so do `(?u)`, `(?R:a)` and every other letter, in `(?X)`, `(?X:...)`, `(?-X)` and `(?iX)` spellings, which the `regex` crate used to reject with its own parse-error wording (`(?)` and `(?Ra)` too). `(?R)` is `unmatched close parenthesis`, as in jq. Checked against jq 1.7.1 over 364 option spellings.
- **jq: a repeated group that Oniguruma reads as an assertion is refused** (#6127). `"ab" | test("(?:a|\\b|b)*")`, `(?:\\b)+`, `(?:a|$)?` and `(?=a)*` answered `true`; jq refuses them with `target of repeat operator is invalid` (here with the `invalid regex:` prefix), as it already did for `\\b*` (#5535). The rule jq applies (an assertion is an invalid target, a sequence of several nodes is not, an alternation is when any alternative is, a plain `(?:...)` group is its body) was captured over 75,780 generated groups and the scan agrees on all of them.
- **jq: a lazy repeat that must run twice or more ends at its body's empty way, as Oniguruma's does** (#6128). `"bab" | [match("(?:(?:b|c)||[ab]){2,3}?"; "gn") | .string]` is `["b","ab"]` in jq and was `["b","a","b"]`. A differential of 2,435 generated lazy patterns over fifteen strings under `g` and `gn` differed on 386; it differs on 4 of 3,866 now, all unbounded `{n,}?` with a consuming way before the empty one (listed in `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **jq: a loop beside a lookaround, backreference or `\K` ends at its empty iteration, as Oniguruma's does** (#6128). A pattern with syntax only `fancy-regex` reads used to keep its loops as written: `"ba" | match("(?:b*|a)+(?=)")` was `"ba"` and is now jq's `"b"`. The same holds for a loop inside a lookaround or atomic group, and next to `\G`, `\K` or a `(?#...)` comment, and for a loop whose body holds a comment with no quantifier after it. A differential of 70,000 generated patterns with such syntax beside, around or inside a loop found 277 cases fixed and none broken (the cases left are listed in `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **jq: a repeat operator after a comment repeats the item before the comment, so a loop over one ends at its empty iteration** (#6128). `"bab" | [match("(?:b(?#)*|a)+"; "g") | .string]` printed `["bab",""]`; jq 1.7.1 reads `b(?#)*` as `b*` and answers `["b","","b",""]`. The comment is left out of what the regex engines read when a repeat operator follows it and an item precedes it. Over 68,970 generated cases, 588 are fixed and none broken; a comment right after a quantifier (`b*(?#)*`) keeps its earlier answer.
- **jq: a lazy `{n,}?` repeat over a body with a consuming way after its empty one is read as Oniguruma reads it, by the body's size** (#6128). Oniguruma writes `X{n,}?` out as `n` plain copies when the body's compiled length times `n` is at most ten, and as a counted loop that leaves at the body's empty way otherwise. The rewrite applied the counted-loop form to both, and gave up past a count of three when the body held a Unicode class, which `\w` is: `"ab" | [match("(?:b?|\\w){2,}?"; "gn") | .string]` printed `["ab"]` where jq 1.7.1 prints `["a","b"]`, and `"ab" | [match("(?:b?|\\w){4,}?"; "gn") | .string]` printed `["a","b"]` where jq prints `["ab"]`. Over 7,098 generated `{2,}?`, `{3,}?` and `{4,}?` patterns, the 259 that differed now agree, and 20,328 patterns across the repeat kinds, with 1,500 random bodies beside them, agree with jq; a count of seven or more over a body of a few operations is still given up (`docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **yq: `map_values(f)` leaves a value whose `f` yields nothing, as yq's `.[] |= f` does** (#6129). `[1, 2, 3] | map_values(select(. > 1))` printed `[2, 3]` and `a: 1` / `b: 2` lost `a`; yq keeps every value (`[1, 2, 3]`), as it does for `map_values(.[])` over a sequence with an empty member (`[1, [], 3]`) and for a repeated key (`a: 1` / `a: 2` stay). `succinctly jq` still deletes the entry, as jq does.
- **yq: a pipe from an absent key in a `select` condition is empty, as yq reads it** (#6130). `select(.zz | not)` kept every item, `select(.zz | contains([1]))` raised a type error and `.[] | select(.t[-1] == 1)` over a list with an item that has no `t` stopped with `index [-1] out of range, array size is 0`; yq keeps nothing for the item in each case, in `select`, `map(select(...))`, `with_entries(select(...))`, `del(...)` and the left side of `=`/`|=`. A key that exists and holds an empty sequence still raises.
- **yq: `@csv` and `@tsv` encode as Go's `encoding/csv` does, as yq's do** (#6131). `[1, a, b] | @csv` printed `1,"a","b"` and yq prints `1,a,b` (a field is quoted only where it holds the separator, a double quote, a line break or a leading space); an array of arrays is one record each (`cat,thing1,thing2` / `dog,"thing,3",thing4`), an array of flat objects is the first object's keys then one record each, a scalar input is its own text, and `@tsv` quotes rather than backslash-escapes. Both raise yq's own errors for what they cannot encode. A `null` element is spelled `null` where yq keeps the source spelling (`~`). `succinctly jq` is unchanged.
- **jq: a regex option run that repeats `-` or ends on one is read as in jq** (#6133). `"a" | test("(?-)a")`, `test("(?--i)a")`, `test("(?i-m-s)a")` and `test("(?i-:a)")` failed with the `regex` crate's parse error, where Oniguruma turns options off from the first `-` and takes a later `-` as a no-op (so `(?i-m-s)` is `i` on, `m` and `s` off). The run is rewritten to its single-`-` equivalent before the crate sees it, and the extended-mode tracking follows the rewritten run. Checked against jq 1.7.1 over every option run of up to four of `i`, `m`, `s`, `x`, `-` in four pattern shapes on five inputs (15,620 runs, 2,560 of them differing before). A blank inside a character class under the extended mode (`(?x:[a b])+`, `(?x)[a b]+`, `(?x-:[a b])+`) is now kept literal as in Oniguruma, where the `regex` crate dropped it, and a letter repeated in a rewritten run is applied once, in order.
- **jq/yq: an alternation whose branches start with the same repeat takes its first branch's match** (#6134). `regex-syntax` factors a shared prefix out of an alternation (`a*a|a*b` became `a*[ab]`, rust-lang/regex#1400), which changes the leftmost-first match when the prefix can match more than one way: `"aab" | match("a*a|a*b")` was `"aab"` and is now jq's and yq's `"aa"`, and `"abbc" | sub("ab*b|ab*c"; "X")` was `"X"` and is now `"Xc"`. A lazy repeat of such an alternation (`(?:a*a|a*b)+?`) now leaves after the first branch's match. Patterns with lookaround, backreferences, `\K`, an atomic group or a `(?#...)` comment are covered too. On a generated-pattern differential against jq 1.7.1, 882 of 80,000 cases were fixed; the 11 that changed from matching jq to differing are loops whose body can match nothing and holds a capture group, the shape #6106 leaves alone, which matched before only because the factoring cancelled that difference out (recorded in `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **jq: `--seq` without `-n` lets `input`/`inputs` raise a malformed record's error, as jq does** (#6137). A program that read `input` printed every `jq: ignoring parse error: ...` before it ran, so the records after a fault paired differently with the main loop: `[., input]` over `1`, `[1,]`, `2`, `3` printed `[1,2]` and a `break` error where jq prints `[2,3]` after `jq: error (at <stdin>:2): Expected another array element ...`. The fault is now the error the next `input` raises; one the program does not read is printed as ignored when the main loop reaches it, after the values before it, and the reader's message-less return ends the main loop there, as in jq. `-s` and programs that never read `input` are unchanged.
- **jq: `--seq --stream` goes on reading past jq's end-of-stream stop, so a later `input` still meets what follows** (#6141). The first call after the read that hit the end of the file returns nothing at an empty record, and that ends only the call that met it: `input` raises `break`, `inputs` ends there, and the main loop ends only if it is the one that pops it. The reader ended the whole stream, so `printf ',"a"nultrue}-\x1e[1]\n\x1e[]\\' | jq -c -e --seq --stream 'limit(2;inputs)'` printed `[[0]]` and exited 0 where jq also prints `Invalid numeric literal at EOF` and exits 5. Random record sequences over 16 programs (`--stream`, `--stream-errors`, `-n`, `input`, `inputs`, `-e`) went from 13 differences in 4,000 runs against jq 1.7.1 to none.
- **jq: `input_line_number` is 0 after a read past a slurped value, as in jq** (#6145). Under `-s`, `printf '1\n2\n3\n' | jq -c -s '[input_line_number, (try input catch .), input_line_number]'` is `[3,"break",0]` in jq and was `[3,"break",3]` here; so is `-n -s '[inputs] | [input_line_number]'` (`[0]`, was `[3]`), and the same holds over `--seq` and `-R`. The slurp had read the stream to its end to build its one value, so the first read past it is already one past the end. Checked against jq 1.7.1 over 182 rows of `-s`, `-n -s`, `-R`, `--seq` and `--stream` with one to two files and empty files: 54 differed before, none after.
- **jq: `input` past the end of a `--seq` stream names the position jq names** (#6146). `printf '\x1e1 \x1e' | jq -c --seq '[.,input]'` says `(at <unknown>): break` in jq and said `(at <stdin>:0)` here; a stream with no value at all (`\n\n\n\x1e` under `-n`) names its newline count (`<stdin>:3`) where it said `<stdin>:0`. The rule is the plain-JSON one (#4303), applied to the values the `--seq` reader yields: the position is lost when the read that reached the end of input completed the last value. A sweep of 4,662 runs (1,554 streams, each through `[.,input]`, `-n [.,input]` and `-n [.,input,input]`) against jq 1.7.1 went from 533 differences to the 30 that end in a fault after the last value (#6137's family).
- **jq: `--seq` prints each ignored parse error when the main loop reaches it, for every program** (#6147). A program that never reads `input`/`inputs` printed every `jq: ignoring parse error: ...` up front; jq prints each after the values before it, so `halt` on an earlier value suppressed it and a runtime error on an earlier value came ahead of it. A differential of 1,500 random `--seq` streams over eleven programs and five flag sets against jq 1.7.1 differed on 103 before and on none now.
- **jq: an alternation beside a `(?#...)` comment that spans a line takes its first branch's match too** (#6149). The guard #6134 put in front of an alternation whose branches share a prefix that can match more than one way could not read such a pattern, so `"aab" | match("(?#a\nb)a*a|a*b")` still took the second branch's `"aab"` where jq 1.7.1 gives `"aa"`; so did a pattern whose guarded form the `regex` crate refused for its size. `succinctly` now requires `regex-syntax` 0.8.12 and `regex` 1.13.2, which keep such a prefix in each branch (rust-lang/regex#1400), and the guard is gone, so every pattern gets the first branch's match without a rewrite.
- **yq: an integer index that misses a mapping finds no node when it is read as an operand, an assignment's right side or a `select` condition** (#6155). `.a + .[0]` over `a: 1` / `b: 2` raised `number (1) and null (null) cannot be added`, and `select(.[0] | not)` kept the mapping; yq answers `1` and keeps nothing, as it does for `.a + .zz`. An index past the end of a sequence is still a `null` read.
- **jq: a repeated group whose body is `\K` is refused** (#6157). `"a" | test("(?:a|\\K)*")`, `(?:\\K|a)+`, `(?:\\K)?` and `(?:a|(?:\\K))*` answered `true`; jq refuses them with `target of repeat operator is invalid` (here with the `invalid regex:` prefix), as #6127 made it for `\b`, `\G` and a look-around. Oniguruma reads `\K` as an assertion like `\G`, so a `\K` among several nodes (the regexes `(?:a\K|b)*`, `(\K)*` and `(?:\K\K)*`) still repeats. A sweep of 7,392 generated `\K`, `\G` and `\b` groups agrees with jq 1.7.1 on every verdict except the two shapes recorded as #6164 and #6165.
- **yq: `tojson` is `to_json`, as yq spells it** (#6158). `{a: 1} | tojson` printed the compact `{"a":1}` and yq prints the indented text with a line break of its own; `tojson(0)` was a parse error. `succinctly jq` keeps jq's compact `tojson`.
- **yq: `min` and `max` of a mapping refuse a string, boolean, array or map among its values, as they do for a sequence** (#6162). `{a: 1, b: x} | max` printed `"x"` and `{a: 1, b: [2]} | min` printed `1`; yq raises `!!str not yet supported for comparison` and `arrays not yet supported for comparison`.
- **jq: a repeated option group of a zero-width body, a stacked repeat of a group holding `\K`, and a repeated empty group answer as jq does** (#6164, #6165). `"ab" | test("(?i:\\K)*")`, `(?i:\\G)+` and `(?i:(?=a))*` answered `invalid regex: regex parse error` where jq compiles them (an option group is a valid repeat target in Oniguruma, whatever its body); `(?:\\Ka)**` was refused where `(?:ab)**` and jq answer; and a repeat of an empty group (`(?:)+`) now takes the `fancy-regex` route under `l`, `n` and a `$` tie (`"abc \n" | match("(?:)+\\s+$")` is `[3,2]`, as in jq, where it was `[3,1]`). Over 28,908 generated groups, jq 1.7.1 vs main, 9,947 more agree and none that agreed now differ except 14 repeats of `\K|a`, which answer where jq refuses them (#6157 tracks the single repeat). A repeat with only a comment before it stays refused.
- **jq: a lazy repeat of a group holding `\G` finds the match after it, as jq does** (#6166). `"cab" | match("(?:\\K\\G)*?b"; "g")` answered `[]` where jq finds the `b` at 2, and so did `(?>\\G)*?b`, `(?:\\G\\K)??b`, `(?i:\\K\\G){0,2}?b` and `(?:\\K\\Ga?)*?b`: `fancy-regex` 0.20.0 ends the whole search where a `\\G` outside every capture group and alternation fails away from the search start, which is wrong once a lazy repeat that may stop at once makes the `\\G` optional. The group's body now gets a way that never matches (`|(?!)`), which takes the `\\G` out of that early exit and changes no match. Over 3,000 generated patterns whose repeated body holds a `\\G` and may match text (seven subjects each), the patterns that differ from jq 1.7.1 fell from 203 to 40, none new; the 40 repeat lazily with a minimum of one or more, which is a separate difference. Over 4,000 patterns with a `\\G`/`\\K`-only body, none differ.
- **jq: a global regex search over a `\K` in a look-behind ends** (#6169). `"cab" | [match("(?<=a\\Kb)";"g")]` never answered and grew without bound (1.4 GB in 20 s): the match begins before the offset the search resumed from, so resuming at its end found it again. A match that begins before that offset and ends at it was found by the search before and is skipped, so the answer is `["b"]`. jq 1.7.1 loops on this shape too; every pattern it answers is unchanged here (1,969 of 2,538 generated cases agree, none differs).
- **jq: a repeat interval after only comments is refused** (#6170). `"cab" | test("(?#){0,1}a")`, `(?:(?#c){2}|b)`, `x|(?#){1}a` and `(?#)(?#){1}a` answered where jq refuses them with `target of repeat operator is not specified`, as it does `{0,1}a` (#6070). A comment is invisible to jq; the scan for an interval with nothing before it forgot what stood before one.
- **jq: a possessive quantifier that something follows is answered as jq answers it, not refused** (#6172). `"aaa" | test("a*+a")` is `false` in jq, and #5524 refused it because the `regex` crate has no atomic group. The quantifier is now written as the atomic group of its atom and quantifier (`(?>a*)a`), which the second engine reads, so `a*+a`, `(ab)*+ab`, `[a]{1,2}+b`, `a?+*`, `a*+*` and `a?+{2}` (which `fancy-regex` cannot read written out) give jq's answer. An atom the scan cannot place (a quoted run, an unsized escape, a group of flags), an inline `(?x)`, and a pattern with a lazy quantifier followed by `+` keep the refusal. 30,000 generated patterns against jq 1.7.1 (three flag sets) went from about 2,900 differences per 8,000 patterns, nearly all refusals, to 640, none new.
- **jq: a repeat operator after a bare option group is refused, as jq refuses it** (#6181). `"caab" | test("(?i)*a")`, `test("a(?i)+")` and `test("(?i){1}a")` printed `true`; jq 1.7.1 has nothing to repeat there and answers `Regex failure: target of repeat operator is not specified`, at the start of a pattern, after an item and past comments alike. `(?i:a)*`, `((?i))*` and `(?i){,2}a` (a literal run) still answer. Over a 1,350-pattern sweep of option groups, operators and positions, 1,048 refusals now match jq; the rest are patterns with an inline `(?x)` and possessive operators, which keep their earlier answers.
- **jq: an inline option in a lookaround or atomic group ends with the group, and a repeated run letter counts once** (#6183). `"aAbB" | [match("(?=(?i)a)a";"g")]` also matched `A`, and `(?<=(?i)a)B`, `(?>(?i)a)B` and `(?i)(?=(?-i)a)A` were wrong the same way, because `fancy-regex` keeps an option set inside such a group for the rest of the pattern where Oniguruma ends it at the `)`. A body that holds an inline option run is now wrapped in `(?:...)` before the engine sees it. A letter named twice in a run (`((?ii)a)B`) is applied once, as Oniguruma does. Checked against jq 1.7.1 over 7,560 lookaround, atomic and plain group shapes.
- **jq: a dash in a character class is read as Oniguruma reads it** (#6184). The `regex` crate takes `--` for set difference and a leading `]` for a literal that no range can start, so `"a-" | [match("[+--]";"g").offset]` and `[--{]` and `[]-b{]` came out as other sets, and the reversed `[?--]`, `[(?--)]` and `[]-(]`, errors in jq, were accepted. `[+--]` is now the range `+` to `-`, `[--{]` the range `-` to `{`, `[]-b{]` the range `]` to `b`, and the reversed ranges are errors. A range that starts or ends on a set (`[[:alpha:]-a]`, `[a-[:alpha:]]`) is an error too. Generated classes against jq 1.7.1 went from 40-65 differences per 8,000 to none.
- **jq: a plain group holding only an option group of a zero-width body is no longer refused** (#6187). `"cab" | match("(?:(?i:\\K))*"; "g")`, `(?:(?i:\\K))+b`, `(?:(?i:(?=a)))*b` and `(?:(?:(?i:\\G)))*` failed with the `regex` crate's parse error where jq answers. #6164 made a repeated option group a valid target by making it atomic; the same group one or more plain `(?:...)` groups down is now rewritten the same way. `(?:\\K)*` and `(?:(?:\\G))*`, which hold no option group, stay refused, as in jq.
- **jq: only the first `^` after a class's `[` negates it** (#6193). The scan kept the class at its start through every `^`, so in `[^^]z[]` the `]` after the second `^` was read as a literal and the class ran on, and an unterminated class after a `[^^]` was accepted where jq refuses it (`"aab" | test("[^^]z[")` was `false` and is an error). Generated classes with leading carets against jq 1.7.1 went from about 80 differences per 8,000 to none.
- **jq: a backreference compares under the case mode in force where it stands** (#6196). `"aA" | [match("((?i)a)\\1";"g")|.string]` printed `["aA"]` (the `(?i)` ended with its group, so jq 1.7.1 answers `[]`), and `[match("(?i)((?-i)a)\\1";"g")|.string]` printed `[]` where jq answers `["aA"]`. A pattern with a backreference and an inline `i` option now writes each backreference as `(?i:\1)` or `(?-i:\1)` for the mode at its position. Over 2,598 generated patterns and strings, jq and `succinctly jq` agree on all (94 differed).
- **jq: a capture or lookahead inside a negative look-behind, and a lookahead or negative look-behind inside a positive one, are refused as in jq** (#6197). `"cb" | test("(?<!(a))b")`, `test("(?<!(?=a)b)c")` and `test("(?<=(?<!a)b)")` answered, where Oniguruma fails with `invalid pattern in look-behind`, at any depth (`(?<!(?:(a)))b`, `(?<=(?<=(?<!a)))z`). A capture or a lookahead in a positive look-behind and a look-behind in a negative one are still accepted, as in jq.
- **jq: a look-behind with alternatives of different widths is refused as jq refuses it** (#6201). Oniguruma, in the Perl syntax jq uses, rejects `(?<=a|bc)d`, `(?<!a(?:b|cd))e` and `(?<=(?:a|bc){2})d` (`invalid pattern in look-behind`), and the `regex` crate answered them (`(?<!a|bc)d` returned `[]` where jq errors). A look-behind whose body holds an alternation of branches of fixed, differing widths, none written as empty, is now an error when the body has no repeat of a varying count, and when the alternation is the body or an item of it under a repeat that must run at least once (`(?<=(?:a|bc)+)`). Alternatives of one width (`ab|cd`), a branch written empty (`a|`) and a body that repeats a varying number of times that may be zero (`(?<=a?)`, `(?<=(?:a|bc)*)`) stay accepted, as in jq. 8,000 generated look-behinds without a varying repeat matched jq 1.7.1 in what they accept, and none that jq accepts was refused over 32,000 more with one.
- **yq: `pivot` of an alias row raises, as yq does, and every `pivot` refusal is in yq's words** (#6202). `.l | pivot` over `[*row, [c]]` transposed the anchor's value (`[[a, c], [b, null]]`) where yq raises `sequence contains elements of  and !!seq types` (an alias node has no tag), and over `[*row, *row]` `can only pivot elements of !!seq or !!map types, received `. The rows are now compared by tag as yq does, on the document route and on a computed array alike, so `[1, 2.5]`, `[[a], 1]` and `[!foo [a], [b]]` give yq's `sequence contains elements of ... types`, scalar rows `can only pivot elements of !!seq or !!map types, received !!str`, a non-array `cannot pivot node of type !!int`, and an empty array (which yq refuses and `pivot` used to answer `[]`) the same `received ` error. Collection rows pivot as before. An array the filter builds (`[.l[]] | pivot`) still resolves its aliases, and a row with a `<<` merge key is still merged first (both recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`).
- **yq: a `select` over `key` in the target of a write** (#6206). `(.. | select(key == "x")) = 5`, `|=`, `+=` and `del(.. | select(key == "x"))` resolved to no target, so the write did nothing and exited 0, where yq writes to every node whose key matches. The `select` condition is now judged against the key of the node it stands at, so `(.. | select(key == "x") | key) = "q"` renames too. `succinctly jq`'s own `key` takes the same path. A `key` that names another node's key (after the head of a pipe) and a negative index in the path are evaluated as before and recorded in the yq limitations page.
- **yq: a flow mapping key that continues on the next line, `{x⏎ y: 1}`, is refused as in yq** (#6208). `printf '{x\n y: 1}\n' | succinctly yq -o json .` printed `{"x y":1}`, where yq stops with `did not find expected ',' or '}'`: a simple key has no line break between its first character and its `:`. The same holds for `{x⏎: 1}`, `{"x"⏎ : 1}`, a quoted key that spans lines, a nested-collection key (`{[a,⏎ b]: 1}`, which was `{"": 1}`) and a key with an anchor, also as the single pair of a flow sequence (`["x⏎ y": 1]`, `[{x⏎}: 1]`). Text across a break that has no `:` is still a multi-line plain entry (`{x⏎ y}` is `x y: null`), and an explicit `? key` may span lines, as in yq. JSON documents read as JSON (`.json` files, `-p=json`) are unaffected.
- **yq: a plain scalar's continuation line drops every blank in front of its text** (#6209).
  `a: [x⏎ ⇥ y]` (a space, a tab, a space) folded to `x  y` with two spaces; go-yaml drops all the blanks of a continuation line, spaces after a tab included, and reads `x y`.
  The same held for `[x⏎⇥ y]`, a tab and spaces in block context, and a blank line followed by such a line (`x⏎⏎ ⇥ y` kept a space).
  A scalar that starts on a `---` line folds differently in yq (the first break is dropped); that is #6276 and not changed here.
- **jq: an inline option switch inside a capture group ends at the group's `)`** (#6212). `"xA" | match("(?i)(x(?-i))a(?=)")` is `xA` in jq, because Oniguruma ends `(?-i)` at the `)` of the group it is in and the `a` after the group is still case-insensitive; `succinctly jq` found nothing, since the second regex engine (any pattern with a look-around or a back-reference) let the switch run on past the group. The body of a plain or named capture group (`(?<n>`, `(?'n'`) that holds an option run is now wrapped in a non-capturing group, as #6183 did for a look-around and an atomic group; group numbers do not move.
- **yq: a tab after U+2028, U+2029 or U+0085 is refused below the block indent, in a flow collection and in block context, as after a newline** (#6214).
  `a: [x⏎⇥y]`, `a: x⏎⇥y` and `- x⏎⇥y` with a Unicode line break were read as the text `x y`; go-yaml ends a line at those characters as at `\n`, so the tab at the start of the next line violates indentation (`found a tab character that violates indentation`), as #6059 made it after `\n`.
  The break stays scalar content that folds as before.
  The column rule is the one #6059 applies: a tab after enough spaces, a scalar or collection at the document root and a quoted scalar are still read, as in yq.
  The empty-key host (`: [x⏎⇥y]`) is not changed: yq refuses every `: value` with no `?` before it, tab or not (#6288).
- **jq: the `x` flag no longer hides a quantifier on an assertion** (#6215). `"cab" | match("\\b*"; "gx")` is an error in jq (`target of repeat operator is invalid`) and was an answer here, because the blanks and comments the flag ignores kept the repeat-target checks from seeing what the quantifier follows; `^+`, `a$?`, `(?:\\B){1,2}`, `(?:a|\\b)*` and `(?i)*a` were accepted the same way. The checks now read the pattern without the blanks and comments, so `\\b *` and `(?: \\B ){1,2}` are refused as well. A pattern with an inline `(?x)` and a quantifier right after a `(?#...)` comment still stand down; `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md` lists them.
- **jq: `\p{XDigit}` is the ASCII hex digits, and `\p{Age=1.1}` and the properties newer than jq's Unicode tables are refused, as in jq** (#6217). `"a5" | test("\\p{XDigit}")` was `invalid regex: regex parse error`; jq 1.7.1 answers `true`. `test("\\p{Age=1.1}")`, `\p{Script=Latin}`, `\p{gc=L}` and `\p{Bidi_Mirrored}` printed an answer; jq says `invalid character property name {NAME}`, and so does `succinctly jq` now. Over every name in the `regex` crate's property table in seven spellings (3,052 cases) the answers match jq; the `In_*` block names are still refused here.
- **jq: under the `n` flag a trailing possessive quantifier over a lazy atom answers as jq does** (#6218). `"cabb" | [match("(?:a??)*+"; "gn")]` printed the `a`; jq 1.7.1 finds nothing, because the possessive quantifier is the atomic group, which takes its empty way and fails the `n` flag's empty-match rejection (`a??+` is the reverse: jq finds `a`). A trailing possessive quantifier over an atom that can match nothing first (a lazy quantifier or an alternation inside it) keeps its atomic group under `n`, and an ungrouped `a??+` is written as `(?:a??)+`. Over a 14,280-case matrix the `n` answers match jq except `X?++`.
- **jq: `\X`, the extended grapheme cluster escape, is read as in jq** (#6220). `"éa" | match("\\X";"g")` failed with the `regex` crate's `unrecognized escape sequence`. It now matches one cluster as Unicode UAX #29 defines it (CR LF, a lone control, a prepend run, a regional-indicator pair, a Hangul syllable, an emoji joined by ZWJ, then the extending marks), as an atomic group, so a cluster is never given back in part, and is refused inside a look-behind as in jq. Checked against jq 1.7.1 over 85,259 strings drawn from every break class and 800,000 random strings; the differences left are characters whose break class changed after jq's Unicode tables (U+1B44 and U+A9C0 in Unicode 15.1, and the Unicode 16 additions), and a pattern that retries `\X` from inside a cluster (`\X\X`, `\Xa`), where jq's `\X` reads the characters to its left; both are listed in `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`.
- **jq: a repeated group of a zero-width item and a bare option group is read as jq reads it** (#6221). `"cab" | match("(?:\\G(?m))*";"g")` is four empty matches in jq and was `invalid regex` here, as were `(?:\\K(?m))*`, `(?:\\Z(?m))*b`, `(?:(?=a)(?i))*` and `(?:\\G(?:(?m)))*`: Oniguruma reads the body as a sequence of two nodes, a valid target, where `fancy-regex` refuses a repeat of a body that is only zero-width. Such a group is now rewritten as the atomic group of its body, as #6164 and #6187 did for an option group; `(?:\\K)*` and `(?:(?m)\\Z)*` (an option group first encloses the rest) stay refused, as jq refuses them. A pattern with an inline `(?x)` or an alternation in the body keeps its old answer.
- **jq: Oniguruma's multi-character case folding is read under the `i` flag** (#6225). `"SS" | test("ß";"i")`, `"STRASSE" | test("straße";"i")` and `"ﬁ" | test("fi";"i")` were `false`: the `regex` crate folds one character to one, where Oniguruma folds with the whole of `CaseFolding.txt` (`ß` is `ss`, `ﬁ` is `fi`, `ﬃ` is `ffi`, `ŉ` is `ʼn`, the Greek iota subscripts). The pattern is now rewritten to the expansion Oniguruma makes of it, a port of `unravel_case_fold_string` over the library's own fold tables (v6.9.8, Unicode 14): a run of literals is walked from the left, the longest fold found there (three characters, then two, then one) becomes an alternation, and the walk goes on after the characters it covered, so `sss` finds `ßs` and not `sß`, as in jq. A bracketed class holding a character that folds to several (`[ß]`, `[ß-ÿ]`, `[\w]`) gains the alternative that spells it; a negated class and a look-behind do not. Checked against jq 1.7.1 over 60,000 random patterns and subjects. Limits are listed in `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`.
- **jq: `\p{Word}` is the class `\w` is** (#6227). `"²" | test("\\p{Word}")` is `true` in jq, whose word class has the Latin-1 `No` characters (U+00B2, U+00B3, U+00B9, U+00BC-U+00BE) outside a class and lacks the joiners U+200C and U+200D, and was `false` here, where the `regex` crate's property has the reverse. `\p{Word}`, `\P{Word}` and `\p{^Word}` now read as `\w` and `\W` do, inside a class and out. `\b` and `\B` keep the crate's definition, a recorded divergence on those six characters.
- **jq: a Unicode block name, `\p{In_Basic_Latin}`, is read as jq reads it** (#6228). `"a" | test("\\p{In_Basic_Latin}")` was `invalid regex: regex parse error`; jq 1.7.1 answers `true`. All 328 block names Oniguruma knows are read, in any spelling (`\p{In basic-latin}`), also as `\P{..}`, `\p{^..}` and inside a class, and under the `i` flag as jq folds them. The table is read from the pinned jq by `scripts/jq-regex-block-table.py`. Over every block in three spellings, nine forms and both flag settings (17,712 cases) the answers match jq.
- **jq: a malformed character class is refused with jq's message** (#6229). `"a" | test("[]")` and `test("[a")` reported the `regex` crate's multi-line `regex parse error`. They now say `empty char-class` (a class that opens with `]` and has no other `]` to close it: `[]`, `[^]`, `a[]`, `[]a`), `premature end of char-class` (any other class the pattern ends inside) and `end pattern at escape` (a trailing backslash), as jq 1.7.1 does. Both tools exit 5; only the wording changed. A `]` first in a class stays a member when a later `]` follows, escaped or not, as in jq. A pattern with two errors reports the class error when the earlier one is found only by the crate (see `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **yq: `-P` writes a mapping key that holds a line break as a literal block, as yq does** (#6230). `printf "? 'k\n\nz'\n: 1\n" | yq -P .` prints `? |-` with `k` and `z` indented under it and the `:` on a line of its own; `succinctly yq -P` printed `? "k\nz"`. The same holds for a double-quoted source key, a plain multi-line one and a key over 128 bytes with a break. A quoted key `-P` strips is a known string with no style left, which the explicit-key branch now takes as it does a plain one. Pinned over 19 rows captured from yq v4.53.3 in `tests/yq_cli/i6230.rs`.
- **jq: a `\x` inside a character class that is not followed by two hex digits is read as Oniguruma reads it** (#6234).
  `[a\x]`, `[\x]`, `[\xg]` and `[\x1]` were refused with `invalid regex: regex parse error`; `\x` followed by something that is not a hex digit
  (or a brace) is NUL and `\x` followed by one hex digit is that digit's value, as outside a class (#6070), so they match what jq 1.7.1
  matches.
- **jq: a `\xHH` at 0x80 or above inside a character class is a byte of a UTF-8 sequence, as it is outside one** (#6240).
  `[\xC3\xA9]` was read as the two characters U+00C3 and U+00A9 and matched neither `é` nor anything jq matches, and `[\x80]` as U+0080; jq decodes the bytes, so `[\xC3\xA9]` matches `é` and `[\x80]` matches nothing.
  A sequence that stops short is `too short multibyte code string`, a bad tail byte is `invalid code point value`, and a range between a decoded character and a character or another byte run (`[\xC3\xA9-\xC3\xAB]`, `[a-\xC3\xA9]`) holds what jq holds, including the one-sided reading of a stray byte (`[\x80-\x90]` matches nothing, `[\x80-\xC3\xA9]` is U+0080 to U+00E9).
- **jq: a lazy counted repeat over a body that holds an option group, a bare `\p{L}` among them, is written out as jq writes it** (#6241). `"ca" | [match("(?:a?|\\p{L}){2,}?"; "gn") | .string]` was `["ca"]`; jq 1.7.1 answers `["c","a"]`, as it does for `(?:a?|\\w){2,}?`. The length of a body that held an option group was not worked out, so it was taken for a long one and given the counted-loop rewrite, where Oniguruma writes `n` plain copies; `succinctly jq` puts such a group around every bare `\p{..}`, which is how `\p{L}` differed from `[\p{L}]`. An option group (`(?s:\w)`, `(?-i:\p{L})`, `(?i:b)?`) now counts as its body. Over 28,728 body shapes, counts and texts the answers match jq except one pattern, `\w` under an inline `i` (#6263).
- **jq: a dash after a range that ends in `\x42`, `\102` or `\cB` is a member of the class, as in Oniguruma** (#6244). `"aA1-" | match("[\\x41-\\x42-\\d]"; "g")` was refused as `char-class value at end of range`; jq 1.7.1 answers `"A"`, `"1"`, `"-"`. The scan of a class's dashes took the digits of an unbraced `\x` or octal escape, and the letter of `\c`, for items of their own, so a range just ended could start another. Over 2,835 generated classes (a range ending in a letter, a hex, octal, braced or control escape, then a dash and a class escape, a letter or an escape), 328 differed from jq before and none now.
- **jq: a negated class of bytes alone whose range holds the lead bytes matches no multibyte character** (#6246). `"aé€" | [match("[^\\x80-\\xFF]";"g").string]` is `["a"]` in jq 1.7.1 and was `["a","é","€"]`; `[^\x41-\xFF]` matches nothing, and `[^\x80-\xBF]` still matches all three. Oniguruma keeps single bytes in a bitset and tests a negated class with no code point against the first byte of a multibyte character, so a range that holds `C2`..`F4` excludes every one of them. The class is now written with the non-ASCII range added; a member that is a code point or a Unicode class (`é`, `\x{E9}`, `\w`, `\p{L}`, `[:alpha:]`) keeps the negation of characters, as in jq. Under `i` (the modifier, or any inline option that sets it) a class holding `k`, `s`, `[:ascii:]` or a range over them is left as it was, since their folds to the Kelvin sign and the long s are code points, which is a gap where `i` is not really in force at that class; the others are written with the character checked after the class (a look-behind, so they run on the backtracking engine). The grid of `[^\xLO-\xHI]` over seven starts and four ends, and 60 further shapes, agree with jq.
- **jq: Oniguruma's `\o{...}` octal escape is read, in a character class and out of one** (#6248).
  `"aA" | [match("\\o{101}"; "g").string]` and `[\o{101}-\o{102}]` were refused with `invalid regex: regex parse error`; the escape is now the code point it names, as in jq 1.7.1.
  The edge cases follow jq: a value past U+10FFFF or a surrogate matches nothing, `\o{8}` and a twelfth digit are `too long wide-char value`, a value past 32 bits is `too big number`, and a missing brace is `invalid code point value`.
  A surrogate or a value past U+10FFFF as the end of a range in a class (`[a-\o{154000}]`, which jq clamps) stays refused.
- **jq: under the `x` flag a repeat operator with nothing to repeat is refused** (#6249). `"x0" | match("*0";"x")`, `match("a| *b";"x")` and `match("(?: *a)";"x")` answered as if the operator were not there, where jq 1.7.1 refuses them with `target of repeat operator is not specified` (without `x` both already refused). The flag's `(?x)` prefix is a group that the `fancy-regex` fallback repeats; the pattern scan now refuses `*`, `+` and `?` at the start of a branch as it did `{2}`, on the pattern without the blanks and comments `x` ignores, and no longer skips patterns made of nothing but such a branch start. A `(?x)` written in the pattern itself still stands down.
- **jq: a braced hex escape `\x{...}` is read as Oniguruma reads it** (#6251).
  `\x{110000}`, `\x{D800}` and `[\x{110000}]` were refused with `invalid regex: regex parse error` and now match nothing, as in jq 1.7.1.
  A ninth digit (`\x{000000041}`, which matched `A`) is `too long wide-char value`, a missing brace (`\x{101`) is `invalid code point value`, and `\x{}` or `\x{ 1}` is the letter `x` followed by an ordinary brace.
  A surrogate or past-U+10FFFF value as the end of a range in a class (`[a-\x{D800}]`, which jq clamps) stays refused.
- **jq: `\k<name>` for a name several groups share tries each of them, as Oniguruma does** (#6254).
  `"aba" | test("(?<n>a)(?<n>b)\\k<n>")` was `false`: the reference read the last group of that name only. It compares the last group that is set, then the one before it, and so on, and does not give the match back once one fits.
  A reference to a name defined twice or more is now the atomic alternation of the numbered groups before it, so it composes with the case pin of #6196, and a name defined again after its reference no longer makes the crate refuse the pattern.
- **jq: a computed-bound slice of a malformed array is an error, as the literal spelling is** (#6257). `printf '[1 2 3]' | jq '.[0+0:0+2]'` answered `[1,2]` (and `[1,,2]` with `.[1+0:]` answered `[2]`, `[,]` answered `[]`) where jq 1.7.1 refuses the document at parse time and `.[0:2]` has exited 5 since #6231. The computed spelling swallowed the structural error its own walk found (#4287); it now raises it, and checks an array with no element for a stray comma. The text inside an element the slice drops is still unread (see `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`), and a computed index of such an array (`.[0+0]` on `[,]`) still answers `null`.
- **jq: a repeat operator after a comment with nothing before it is refused under the `i` and `x` flags too** (#6261). `"aab" | match("(?#c)*"; "gi")` answered four empty matches where jq 1.7.1 refuses it (`target of repeat operator is not specified`), as it does without a flag: the `(?i)` put before the pattern made the `regex` crate read the operator as repeating the comment. The refusal is now made on the pattern as written, for a comment at the start of a group or after a `|`.
- **jq: a backreference to a group that is still open, under a repeat that can run twice, is refused on the second engine instead of answered wrongly** (#6262). `"ab" | [match("(\\1|\\w)+";"g")|.string]` was `["a","b"]` (the group `[1,""]`) where jq 1.7.1 answers `["ab"]` with the group at `[1,"b"]`, and `(a|\1)+`, `(a|\1){2}` and `((?!\1)){2,}` did the same: `fancy-regex` reads such a reference from the group's new start to its old end, empty for contiguous passes, where Oniguruma reads the group's last completed value. Such a pattern now gives `invalid regex` for any text. A reference to a group that is open under no repeat (`(a|\1)`, `(a|\1)?`) and one to a group that has closed (`(a)\1+`) keep their route and answer as jq does. Over a grid of 468 such patterns, 185 differed from jq before; 283 agreed and are refused with them, since a pattern cannot tell which texts reach the reference.
- **jq: `\w`, `\W` and `\p{Word}` under the `i` flag are one operation in a lazy counted repeat's body, as in Oniguruma** (#6263).
  The translation writes them as a bracketed class, and the count of the body took any bracketed class under case folding for a long one, so with the `n` flag `"ca" | [match("(?i)(?:a?|\\w){2,}?"; "gn") | .string]` was `["ca"]` where jq answers `["c","a"]`. The translated word class is now recognised and counted as one operation, also inside an option group (`(?i-s:\w)`, which #6241 counts as its body).
- **jq: a computed index of an array with no element but a comma is an error** (#6270). `printf '[,]' | jq '.[0+0]'` answered `null` (and `.a[1-1]` the same inside an object) where jq 1.7.1 refuses the document at parse time, as the literal `.[0]`, `length` and `.[]` do here (exit 5). The walk of an array sees no gap when it has no element, so the check is made where the target's cursor is held, as #6257 did for the computed slice.
- **jq: a range whose start is above its end inside a character class is `empty range in char class`, as in jq** (#6273).
  `"a" | test("[z-a]")` reported the `regex` crate's own parse error (exit 5 either way); the class is now read the way Oniguruma reads it, and a descending range between two characters, control or octal escapes below 0x80 (`\n`, `\101`, `\cA`), `\x{..}` or `\xHH` bytes is jq's refusal. A class longer than 2,048 characters before the `-` is left to the crate.
- **jq: a computed integer compares as a double against a decimal literal, as in jq** (#6275).
  `jq_numeric_cmp` read a bare `Int` as a literal, so the result of `1+1`, `length` or `floor` was compared by its exact decimal digits: `(1+1) == 2.00000000000000000001` and `(0+0) == 1e-400` were `false` where jq answers `true`, and `(9007199254740992+0) == 9007199254740993` likewise.
  A bare `Int` is now a computed double, and the reindex bridge carries one within `2^53` as a token that reads back bare, so `[2.00000000000000000001,(1+1)] | unique` and `[1e-400,(0+0)] | sort` answer as jq does. Two literals still compare exactly. The first value of a `range` still reads as a computed one; the entry is in `docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: a scalar that starts on the `---` line runs on into the next line, as yq reads it** (#6276). yq's header slurp pushes the text after a leading `--- ` back without the marker line's own line break, so `--- x` / `y` is `"xy"` where `succinctly yq` read `"x y"`, and `--- x` / `y: 1` is `{"xy": 1}` where it was a parse error. The same lost break applies to a flow collection (`--- [a, x` / `y]` is `["a","xy"]`), a quoted scalar, a comment (`--- # c` / `x` / `y` is the comment `# cx` and the document `"y"`) and a following marker (`--- x` / `--- y` is the one scalar `x--- y`), and `a: 1` / `b: 2` after `--- ` is refused as yq refuses it. A marker on a line of its own, a marker after the first content line, a lone CR break and `load()` are unchanged, and under `--eval-all` only the first file's marker line is glued, as in yq.
- **yq: a line holding only a tab after a plain scalar is refused when the tab is no deeper than the block that owns the scalar** (#6286).
  `a: x⏎⇥` (and one level down, after a sequence item, with spaces before the tab) was read as an empty line; go-yaml stops with `found a tab character that violates indentation` when the tab's column is at most the block's indent, and reads the line as empty when it is deeper.
  A document-root scalar has no block to violate and is unchanged.
  The same line after a flow collection, a quoted scalar, a comment or a key with no value is refused at any column by yq and is still read at a deeper column here (#6295).
- **yq: a tab after a U+2028, U+2029 or U+0085 break in a block scalar is refused below the scalar's indent** (#6287). go-yaml ends a block scalar's line at those three breaks as at `\n`, so `a: |` over `  x<U+2028><tab>y` is `found a tab character where an indentation space is expected`, as is a tab after fewer spaces than the indent (`<U+2029>` + one space + tab under an indent of 2); `succinctly yq` read all of them as scalar content. A tab after at least the indent's worth of spaces, or one that does not follow such a break, is still content. Checked against yq v4.53.3 on a grid of 4,608 documents (four hosts, `|`/`>`/`|-`/`>+`, three breaks, 0-5 spaces), 1,344 of them refused, with no difference in which. The same breaks still do not end the line for dedent, indent detection or the strip of the spaces after them (#4913). The check rides on the walk over a block scalar's lines, which now goes eight bytes at a time and notes a tab on the way, so a scalar without a tab costs nothing extra and the walk itself is faster: a 24 MB document made entirely of block scalars indexes 1.02-1.03x faster on an AMD Ryzen 9 7950X and 1.10-1.12x faster on an Apple M4, and 0.93x / 0.99x when every scalar also holds tabs and U+2014 (min of 9, interleaved).
- **yq: a block-mapping `:` with no `?` before it is `did not find expected key`, as in yq** (#6288).
  `: a`, `a: 1` then `: b`, a second `:` after an explicit key's value and `- : b` were read as an entry with an empty key, and the value was dropped after a mapping entry (`a: 1⏎: b` answered `{"a":1}`); yq refuses all of them. A `:` is now only the value of a `?` key that is waiting for one, and a tag or an anchor before it (`!!str : 1`) stays an empty key. Six YAML test-suite cases that are valid YAML 1.2 but refused by yq (`2JQS`, `6M2F`, `NHX8`, `S3PD`, `SM9W/01`, `UKK6/00`) join the known-failures manifest.
- **yq: a node with an explicit tag and no value is the empty string whatever the tag, as in yq** (#6291).
  `k: !!seq`, `- !custom` and `--- !!str` read as `null` in `-o json` output and in a comparison with `""`, where yq answers `""` (`false` for `!!bool`; only `!!null` is `null`). `!!str` and `!!bool` already agreed, and `!!int`/`!!float` with no value stay the empty string where yq's JSON encoder fails (`docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`).
- **yq: a flow indicator right after a tag is refused, as yq does** (#6293). `[!!str]`, `{a: !!str}`, `[!!str, 1]`, `[!foo]`, `[!]`, `[!<tag:x>]` and `a: !!str]` printed `[""]`, `{"a":""}`, `["",1]`, `[null]` and the like, where yq takes the `,`, `[`, `]`, `{` or `}` as part of the tag's run of characters and refuses it with `found character ']' that is not allowed in a YAML tag`. The tag is refused in flow and block context, with or without a value, for a core, custom, named-handle and verbatim tag; a space first (`[!!str ]`, `[!!str ,1]`) and a value after the tag are unchanged. Twenty-nine refused and thirteen unchanged documents are pinned against yq v4.53.3's answers.
- **yq: a line holding only a tab is refused after every completed node, as yq refuses it** (#6295). go-yaml skips a tab only where a simple key is not allowed, which is never at the start of a block-context line, so ` ⇥` after a flow collection (`a: [x]`), a quoted scalar, a comment (`a: x # c`), a key with no value (`a:`), a property (`a: &x`) or an anchored flow collection, in a sequence, after a later document's `---` and after a `...` end marker is `found a tab character that violates indentation` at any column where `succinctly yq` read an empty line (#6286 did the plain-scalar case). The same line before the first content line of a block scalar (`a: |` / ` ⇥` / `  x`) is refused as well. A plain scalar before it (`a: x`), a block scalar's content, a flow collection's own lines and the head of the first document (`---` / `⇥` / `a: 1`, which read as yq's header) are unchanged, or newly read in the last case.
- **yq: a verbatim tag followed directly by a non-space is refused, as yq does** (#6298). `a: !<tag:x>x`, `[!<tag:x>x]`, `!<tag:x>"q"`, `a: !<tag:x>#c` and `!<tag:x>[a]` read the text after the closing `>` as the tagged value (`{"a":"x"}`, `["x"]`, `"q"`, ...) where yq's scanner needs whitespace, a line break or the end of the input there and stops with `did not find expected whitespace or line break`. A verbatim tag followed by a space, a tab, a line break or the end of the input is unchanged. Twenty refused and fourteen unchanged documents are pinned against yq v4.53.3's answers.
- **yq: a plain scalar under an unknown `!!` tag is its text, as in yq** (#6299).
  `a: !!str: 1`, `[!!int: 1]` and `a: !!foo 1` read the number `1` where yq answers the string `"1"`: the `:` of `!!str:` belongs to the tag, and a tag of the secondary handle that names no core type (`!!binary`, `!!set`, `!!foo`) makes the scalar its text. A custom `!foo 1` still resolves like the untagged text, and the core tags force their own kind.
- **jq: a loop body whose consuming way holds an assertion ends at the body's empty way, as Oniguruma's loop does** (#6300). `"ba" | [match("(?:b*|\\Ba)+") | .string]` printed `["ba",""]` and `"ba" | [match("(?:b*|a\\z)+") | .string]` printed `["ba",""]`; jq 1.7.1 answers `["b","",""]` for both. An assertion beside an item that consumes text (`\Ba`, `a\z`, `^a`, `a$`) only decides whether that way matches, so it is copied with the other ways and no longer keeps the loop as written; a way that matches nothing only where an assertion holds (`(?:b*|\b)+`) still does. Over 20,000 generated loops with one way that can match nothing and one or two ways holding an assertion, on 13 strings under `g`, the 362 that differed from jq now agree and none changed the other way (`docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **jq: a loop whose body holds an inline flag switch ends at its empty iteration as Oniguruma's does** (#6301).
  `"ba" | [match("(?:(?i)b*|a)+"; "g") | .string]` is `["b","",""]` in jq and was `["ba",""]` here: the loop keeps the `regex` crate's longer match when its body holds `(?i)`, `(?s)`, `(?m)` or the like, and the rewrite for #6106 had left such a body alone.
  The switch reaches the rest of its group, later ways included, so it is now written as a flag group over what it reaches (`x(?i)y|z` is `x(?i:y)|(?i:z)`) before the loop is rewritten.
  Over 13,056 generated cases (16 body shapes, 7 switches, 6 loop forms, 17 strings) 885 differed from jq before and none after.
  A switch that names `x` or `U`, and a lazy repeat over such a body, keep their loop as written.
- **jq: a comment after a quantifier, then a second repeat operator, repeats the quantified item inside a loop body, as in Oniguruma** (#6303).
  `b*(?#)*` is `(?:b*)*` and `b+(?#)?` is `(?:b+)?`, not the lazy `b+?`, but the comment was kept for the engines to repeat, so `"bab" | [match("(?:b*(?#)*|a)+"; "g") | .string]` was `["bab",""]` where jq answers `["b","","b",""]`. A greedy `*`, `+` or `?` followed past the comments by another is now the one quantifier with the same language and the comment is left out. Over 68,970 generated cases 544 were fixed and none broken; a capture group, an interval or a lazy `*?` as the second repeat still differs (`docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **jq: a loop over a capture group ends at the body's empty way, as Oniguruma's does** (#6305). `"ba" | [match("(b*|a)+") | .string]` printed `["ba"]`; jq 1.7.1 answers `["b"]`, as it does for the same loop without the group, and `sub`, `gsub`, `scan` and `splits` followed. The capture rewrite of #6069 leaves the repeated group's own loop as a plain `(?:X)*`, and the empty-iteration rewrite of #6106 now reads that loop. Over 3,346 generated patterns (a repeated capture group with `*`, `+`, `{0,}` or `{1,}`, on 19 strings under `g`), the 117 that differed from jq now agree and none changed the other way; a capture group nested inside the repeated group, or a repeat with a count of two or more, keeps its earlier answer (`docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **jq: a `{n,}` repeat (n of 2 or more) of a capture group ends at the body's empty way and reports its empty iteration, as Oniguruma's does** (#6309). `"abb" | [match("(b|){2,}$";"g") | .captures[0].string]` printed `["b",""]`; jq 1.7.1 answers `["",""]`, and `"ba" | [match("(b*|a){2,}";"g") | .string]` printed `["ba",""]` where jq answers `["b","",""]`. The capture rewrite (#6069) now takes such a repeat as its `*` loop, and the loop rewrite (#6106, #6305) reads that. Over 2,498 generated `{2,}`, `{3,}` and `{4,}` patterns the 519 that differed from jq now agree, and none changed the other way; a counted repeat over a body with a group inside it, and a bounded one, keep their earlier answer (`docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **jq: a loop whose body has a capture group after its empty way ends at that empty way, as Oniguruma's does** (#6310). `"ba" | [match("(?:b*|(a))+") | .string]` printed `["ba"]`; jq 1.7.1 answers `["b"]`, as it does for the same loop without the group, and `sub`, `gsub`, `scan` and `splits` followed, as did `(b*|(a))+`. The loop rewrite of #6106 now lists a capture group's ways and writes the group once, in the iteration, so the pattern's groups keep their number and order; a group it would copy or drop (in a way before the empty one, in the empty way itself, or in the body of a counted repeat) keeps the loop as written (`docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`). Over two draws of 5,000 generated loops (`scripts/jq-regex-capture-loop-sweep.py`), 51 and 68 patterns that differed from jq now agree and none changed the other way.
- **yq: a write keeps a `<<` merge key that names nothing to merge** (#6318).
  `- <<: *seq`, where the alias is a sequence of scalars (five CI files of one crate in a sweep of 2,057 real YAML files), came back `- {}` from any write such as `.zzkey = 1`, losing the key and its alias; so did `<<: 5`, `<<:` and `<<: hello`. The entry stays now, written plain where yq writes `!!merge <<`, which reads back the same. A merge of a mapping is still expanded by a write, as before.
- **jq: a number literal past the double range prints as jq prints it when the answer is an owned value** (#6319). `[1e1000] | map(.)?`, `map(.) | sort`, `min`, `max`, `reverse`, `sort_by(.)` and `unique_by(.)` printed `[null]` (and `null`) where jq 1.7.1 keeps the literal as `[1E+1000]`; `-1e1000`, `1e309` and `1.7976931348623157e309` did the same, and `[1e1000, 1, -1e400] | map(.) | sort` lost both ends. The library's jq output streamer carried yq's rule for an infinite number (`null`); it now prints a literal in its canonical spelling and a computed infinity as the `DBL_MAX` text (`1.7976931348623157e+308`), which is what the CLI's own printer already wrote. `--preserve-input` echoes the literal as written. The yq output is unchanged. A literal that fits a double, and one that underflows, were not affected. Found by a randomized differential of options, documents and filters.
- **yq: a bare `:` after an explicit key is a null value, not a missing one** (#6321). `printf '? a\n:\n'` printed `{}` where yq has `{"a":null}`, and with another entry after it the key was paired with that entry's key: `? a⏎:⏎? b⏎: 1` was `{"a":"b"}` (yq `{"a":null,"b":1}`), `x: 1⏎? a⏎:⏎y: 2` was `{"x":1,"a":"y"}`, `- ? a⏎  :⏎- 2` lost its key, and `m:⏎  ? a⏎  :⏎  b: 1` was `{"m":{"a":"b"}}`. The colon with a property on it (`: &y`, `: !!str`) already wrote its null node; the bare one now does too. A value on the next lines, a sequence at the colon's indent, a comment line between, and a `:` followed by text are unchanged. 40 documents are pinned against yq v4.53.3.
- **yq: an explicit key whose own content is an explicit key (`? ? a⏎  : b⏎: c`) is read as the mapping-as-key it is** (#6322). `succinctly yq -o json .` stopped at the inner `:` with `inconsistent indentation`, and read `? ? a⏎: c` as the plain-scalar key `? a` (`{"? a":"c"}`, silently); yq answers `{"":"c"}` for both. The inner key now waits for its value in front of the outer one, and the outer one takes the next shallower `:`; a tag or an anchor before the nested `?` (`? !!str ? a`) and a `:` that lands between the two stay refused, as yq refuses them. Over 4,200 generated explicit-key documents, 1,608 that differed from yq now agree and none changed the other way.
- **jq: `strptime` and `fromdate` read the date string and the format as C strings, so a NUL byte ends each, as jq's do** (#6324). `"2015-03-05T23:51:47Z\u0000junk" | fromdate` is `1425599507` in jq 1.7.1 and was an error here; `"\u0000" | try fromdate catch .` now says `date "" does not match format ...` and `"2015-03-05" | strptime("%Y-%m-%d\u0000junk")` parses. Found by a differential of every zero-arity builtin against 80 edge-case inputs, where these two were the only builtins that differed.
- **yq: a bare `: ` entry inside an explicit key is `did not find expected key`, as in yq** (#6325).
  `? : x`, `- ? : x`, `? - : x`, `? - - : x`, `a:⏎  ? : x` and the key content on the next line (`?⏎  : x`) were read as an empty key with a null value; yq refuses them, as it does the keyless `:` of #6288. A tag or an anchor before the `:` (`? !!str : x`) stays an empty key. `M2N8/00` joins the YAML test-suite known failures.
- **jq: a global regex search steps one byte after an empty match, so a multibyte character gives an empty match per continuation byte, as jq 1.7.1's does** (#6326). `"ß" | [match("";"g") | .offset]` printed `[0,1]`; jq answers `[0,1,1]`, and `"ß" | gsub("";"X")` is `"XßXX"` in jq and was `"XßX"`, `"ß" | [splits("")]` is `["","ß","",""]`. The extra matches are empty, at the next character's offset, with the same empty captures; they follow a pattern with no assertion (`""`, `x*`, `\s*`, `a?`, groups and alternations of them), and the `n` flag still drops them. Over 1,854 generated patterns on strings of one- to four-byte characters, 1,114 differed from jq before and 3 do now; a pattern with `\b`, `^`, `$` or a look-around keeps the character step (`docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **jq: `strftime`'s `%I`, `%l` and `%r` print the hour modulo 12 for an hour outside 0-23, as jq's libc does** (#6331). `[2015,2,5,25,0,0,4,63] | strftime("%I %r")` is `01 01:00:00 PM` in jq 1.7.1 and printed `13 13:00:00 PM`; an hour of 100 printed `88` where jq prints `04`, and a negative hour keeps C's sign (`-13` is `-1`). Hours 0-23 are unchanged; a sweep of 93 hours from -30 to 59 plus 100, -100 and 1000 agrees with jq.
- **jq: a loop whose body has a capture group before its empty way, in it, or with its own empty way first ends at the empty iteration and sets its groups, as Oniguruma's does** (#6332). `"abca" | [match("(?:(a)|b*|c)+";"g") | .string]` printed `["abca",""]`; jq 1.7.1 answers `["ab","","a",""]`, and `"ba" | [match("(?:b*|()|a)+";"g") | .captures[0].string]` left the group unset where jq has `""` at the exit. The loop is now written with the group copied (the ways before the empty one are written twice, a counted repeat writes its body again for each count) and ended with the body's empty way, and each copy is read back into its group as the one the match set last (the greatest start, then end, then number). A capture group counts as two operations in the count that decides whether Oniguruma writes a lazy `{n,}?` out as copies. A loop inside another repeat that can run its body more than once, and a counted repeat over a body with a loop of its own, are left as written; the switch that the `i` and `s` flags put in front of a pattern stays there. Over two draws of 5,000 generated loops (`scripts/jq-regex-capture-loop-sweep.py`), 236 and 236 patterns that differed from jq now agree and none changed the other way, and six draws with the loops nested inside repeats fixed 108 to 160 and broke none; about 50 in each plain draw still differ, mostly in a counted `{n,}` of a capture group with a group inside it, or beside a flag switch or an assertion (`docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`).
- **yq: a comment written inside a flow collection is kept** (#6334). `printf 'v: ["a", # c1⏎  "b", # c2⏎  "c"]⏎' | succinctly yq .` printed `v: ["a", "b", "c"]`, dropping both comments from the file; yq prints the collection across lines with each comment after its element's comma (`v: ["a", # c1⏎  "b", # c2⏎  "c"]`), and the closing bracket on a line of its own when the last element is commented. The same holds for a comment on a line of its own (`[` / `# head` / `x,` / `y` / `# foot` / `]`), which yq reads as the head of the element after it and the foot of the last one (`.v[0] | head_comment` answers `head`), lays out on lines of their own at the collection's indent, and keeps under `-P`; in a mapping the comment belongs to the entry's key. The parser records a comment for the element it follows or precedes (a sequence element, a mapping entry, nested collections included), and the cursor and document routes lay the collection out with the layout they share (`yaml::flow_layout`). Over 600 generated documents (541 holding a comment: flow sequences and mappings, nested, in a mapping value, a nested mapping and a sequence item, checked under `.`, a write, a navigation, `-P` and `-I4`), the ones that differ from yq under `.` fell from 454 to 159, and those that differ under some filter from 454 to 244, none changed the other way. A comment before a comma that precedes the closing bracket, some blank lines yq writes beside a footed collection, and `-P` with a collection that ends a sequence still differ (`docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`).
- **yq: `-P` holds the comment of a flow element that is a collection** (#6334, part of it). `printf 'v: [[1], # a⏎  2]⏎' | succinctly yq -P .` printed `- 2` with no comment, losing `# a` from the file; yq writes a flow collection it turns into a block without the line its comment sat on, holds that comment (as it already did one after the whole collection, #4377) and writes it at the end of the next line without a comment of its own (`- 2 # a`; `- # a` above the members of a collection; `b: 2 # a` in a mapping). Between the elements of a flow sequence an element with a comment of its own (an alias too, which takes the held one when it has none) overwrites the held comment instead of letting it wait, and the held comment is one slot that the next held comment overwrites. Over 500 generated documents with same-line comments, the ones that differed from yq under `-P` fell from 45 to 15, none changed the other way; the 15 left are an empty `[]`/`{}` after a held comment, a second comment on a comma's line and the foot of a footed collection that a key follows (all in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`).
- **`succinctly yq` prints an earlier entry of a repeated key as it was spelled** (#6335). A mapping with a repeated key keeps every entry, but the by-key presentation tree described only the last one, so a write printed `a:` (an empty value) as `a: null`, and `~`, `Null` and `True` as `null`, `null` and `true`, for every entry before the last (`printf 'a:\na: 2\n' | succinctly yq '.zzkey = 1'` now prints `a:` / `a: 2` / `zzkey: 1`, as yq does). The spelling is kept per earlier entry, in the key's metadata, through `=`, `|=`, `del`, `*`, `with_entries(.)` and a `to_entries | from_entries` with nothing between the two; of 570 rows (30 documents, 19 programs) compared with yq v4.53.3, 206 that differed now agree and none regressed. A filter between `to_entries` and `from_entries`, `*+`/`*d`/`*n`/`*?` and `pick` still lose it. A tag, quotes, a comment or an anchor on an earlier entry are still written plain (recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`).
- **yq: an explicit key inside an explicit key's value is read as the mapping it opens** (#6340). The node after an explicit key's `: ` can be a compact mapping whose first entry is an explicit key (`? a` / `: ? x` / `  : y` is `{"a": {"x": "y"}}`); `succinctly yq` read `? x` there as a plain scalar (`{"a": "? x"}`) and refused the `: y` after it, in a mapping, a sequence item and a nested mapping, with any depth of nesting (`: ? x` / `  : ? p` / `    : q`). A key sequence whose first item opens one (`? - ? x` / `    : y` / `: v` is `{"": "v"}`) was `inconsistent indentation`. A property before the inner `?` (`: &t ? x`) is refused, as yq refuses it.
- **yq: a stream with no content reads as yq reads it: a tab-led comment or a `%YAML` directive alone is a null document, a `...` met before any content is refused** (#6342). yq's header slurp sets aside every leading blank, comment, `%YAML` directive and `---` line before go-yaml sees the rest, so `⇥ # c` and `%YAML 1.2` are one null document that print back as written, where `succinctly yq` read no document and printed nothing; and `...`, `---` / `...`, `# c` / `...` and `%YAML 1.2` / `...` hand go-yaml a `...` as the first token of an implicit document, which it refuses with `did not find expected node content` where `succinctly yq` read nothing or a null document. A `%TAG` (or any directive other than `%YAML`) with no `---` after it is refused too (`did not find expected <document start>`). A `---` that is not in the head still starts an empty document a `...` can close (`a: 1` / `---` / `...` is `{"a":1}` then `null`). Every stream is pinned against yq v4.53.3 in `tests/yq_cli/i6342.rs`; the library loader keeps the YAML test suite's reading (`HWV9`, `QT73`: zero documents).
- **yq: a scalar, alias or flow line level with a mapping's keys or a sequence's `-` markers, with no value waiting for it, is refused as yq refuses it** (#6343).
  `a: |⏎  x⏎stray` kept `{"a":"x\n"}` and dropped `stray`; `k: &a⏎q` dropped `q`; `? k⏎q` and `a:⏎"q"` read the line as a value; `a: |⏎"q"⏎b: 1` read a key and a value that are in no document; yq stops with `while scanning a simple key` for all of them. A block scalar header at that indent (`- &x⏎|`) stays a node of the entry above it, as in yq.
