- **`succinctly jq --seq -s --stream` and `--seq -s --stream-errors` meet the fault of a record left open across files at the read jq does, when one file after it did not open** (#6730, family 1, the `--seq` form). `jq -c --seq -s --stream . trunc pa missing` (`trunc` = `\x1e[1,`, `pa` = `[1]`) printed nothing and said `ignoring parse error: Unfinished JSON term`; it now prints the array and says only `Could not open file missing`, as jq does, because the read of the failed file brings out the closing event `pa` held back and the fault waits for a read the main loop never makes. A directory last is the same single read, for both flags: `--seq -s --stream . trunc pa dir` prints the array, and `--seq -s --stream-errors . trunc pa dir` no longer prints the fault as a second output. A second read behind `pa` (another file that did not open, an empty file or a directory) is where the fault is met, as before: `--seq -s --stream . trunc pa missing empty` still loses the array and says the warning.
- **`succinctly jq --stream-errors` stops at the first failure when a file of several values follows a directory behind a bare number** (#6732). `jq -c --stream-errors halt_error p.json dir r2.json gone.json` (`p.json` = `1` with no newline, `r2.json` = `1 2`) prints `Is a directory` and `[[],11]`: the number goes on into `r2.json`, where the first event is whole at the space, so the main loop stops there and `gone.json` is never opened. succinctly judged `r2.json` by its last token (`2`, a bare number), sent the run up front, and said `Could not open file gone.json` too. A file that is all number or letters (`2`, `ab`) still continues the token into the next read, and a number that ends inside a string is judged as before. 20 of the 180 rows of #6683's 35,090-row differential against jq 1.7.1 were of this shape; they are fixed and none changed for the worse. The other 160 (a first file that ends in a container, `{"a":1}` or `[1,2]`, with a program that reads `input` under plain `--stream-errors`) are the closing-event shape of #6646 and stay with #6732.
- **`succinctly jq --stream-errors` counts the directory behind a closing event the program's own `input` reads, and stops where a first event spanning two files is whole** (#6732). A container that ends its file with no newline (`{"a":1}`, `[1]`) holds its closing event back until the next read, which is the open of the directory behind it: `jq -c --stream-errors 'input,halt_error' obj.json dir gone.json` read it and exited 2 with nothing said, where succinctly exited 5 with the halt's status, and `jq -c --stream-errors input arr.json dir p.json gone.json` printed `Is a directory` and `Could not open file gone.json` where jq prints neither (the bare number in `p.json` had sent the run up front). A first event that two files make (`1` in `p.json`, then `1\n` in `pn.json`) is whole in the second, so `jq -c --stream-errors halt_error p.json pn.json gone.json` no longer says `Could not open file gone.json` and exits 5 with the halt's status. A 12,000-row differential against jq 1.7.1 (three seeds, 11 programs, lists of up to four files with a directory and missing files, `-n` rows alongside) left 107 rows fixed and none changed for the worse; 21 rows are still apart, all with a token left open across files (`[`, `[1,`).
- **`succinctly jq --stream-errors` stops printing a spurious `Unfinished JSON term at EOF` event when a directory is the last file** (#6732). When an earlier file leaves a token open (`[`, `[1,`) and the file before the directory finishes a container (`{"a":1}`, `1]`), `jq -c --stream-errors . open.json obj.json dir` printed an extra `[\"Unfinished JSON term at EOF at line 1, column 8\",[0]]` after the two events; jq prints the two events and exits 2, and so does succinctly now (the same for `first` and `halt_error`). A program that reads `input` still sees that event, as in jq (`[inputs]` prints it inside the array and says `Is a directory`). A newline after the closing bracket, or an empty file before the directory, keeps the event, as before.
- **`succinctly jq --stream-errors` counts every file that did not open when a token left open across files ends in a fault** (#6732). A bare number completes only when jq's reader asks for more, so after `[` and a missing file, the `2` of `1 2` is read together with the end of the text: jq opens, and reports, every file that did not open before it raises `Expected separator between values at EOF`. `jq -c --stream-errors . open.json gone r2.json gone` (`open.json` = `[`, `r2.json` = `1 2`) reported `gone` once where jq reports it twice, and so did `halt_error` and a program that reads `input` (the same for a directory: `open.json dir r2.json gone`). The same holds when the fault is raised in a file after the second failure (`open.json gone r2.json gone open.json`, `Expected separator between values at line 1, column 5`), and a fault met mid-text in the file before the failures (`[1,2` then `{"a":1}`) is no longer taken for a closing event held back for the failure's read (`open3.json obj.json gone gone` stopped after the first). Differential grids against jq 1.7.1 (`-c --stream-errors`, up to six programs, lists of 3-5 files with a directory and missing files, 9-11 fixtures, `-n`, `-e`, `-s`, `--seq` alongside) cover about 120,000 rows (they overlap): 150 rows were apart, and after the change none is, with no row changed for the worse.
- **yq: `map(.)`, `sort`, `reverse`, `unique`, `select` over `.[]` and an array of nodes keep the comments between a sequence's items** (#6736).
  `printf -- '- a\n# c\n- b\n' | yq 'map(.)'` prints `- a` / `# c` / `- b`, where `succinctly yq` printed the items without
  the `# c`: the cursor streamers wrote only each item's own trailing comment, so only a query that built an owned value
  kept the others. They now write each item's head and foot comments, the blank line after a foot when another item
  follows, and the comment on a bare `-`, as the sequence arm of `.` does. Over 14,768 document x filter x option rows
  (comment placements above, between and after items, blank lines, nested sequences, anchors, tags, multiple documents,
  CRLF) against yq v4.53.3, 619 rows that differed now match and none that matched changed. Still not written: a document's
  own foot comment after a reordered root sequence, the trailing foot after `reverse` or `sort_by` of mappings, the
  comments of a chain of two reordering stages (`sort_by(.id) | reverse`), and the comment on a bare `-` that holds a
  nested sequence when `.[0][]` streams the inner elements (the owned route wrote that one for an array).
- **yq: the cursor streamers quote a plain scalar that starts like a document marker, a lone `-` in flow context, and write a folded multi-line one as a block** (#6737).
  A source plain scalar was written back as spelled, which yq's emitter does not do when it cannot stay plain. `a: ---`, `b: ...`, `x: --- y` and `z: ...x` print as `a: '---'`, `b: '...'`, `x: '--- y'` and `z: '...x'` now (single quotes, in a mapping, a sequence and flow collections), a lone `-` inside `[...]` or `{...}` as `'-'` (it was `"-"`), and a plain scalar the source folded across blank lines (`a:\n  x\n\n  y`) as a literal block, `a: |-\n  x\n  y`, where it was one double-quoted line with `\n` (`a: "x\ny"`). All of it agrees with yq v4.53.3 on a 44-row matrix of contexts and spellings and on about 5,000 random plain scalars in seven contexts (no row that matched before differs now, 700 that differed match). A document with a trailing comment keeps the quoted spelling for a multi-line plain scalar, because the streamers write that comment after the value, which a literal block would read as text (yq puts it on the block's header, `|- # c`).
- **`succinctly yq` writes the block value and block key of an explicit key at the column their continuation lines stand at, inside a compact sequence entry** (#6738). `printf -- '- ? [a, b]\n  :\n    - 1\n    - 2\n' | succinctly yq -I=4 .` printed `:   - 1` over `    - 2`, which neither succinctly nor yq reads back (`inconsistent indentation`); the first entry was padded by a fixed `-I - 1` blanks after the `:`, where the continuation lines step by `deeper_yaml_indent`. It now prints yq's `: - 1` / `    - 2`, and under `-I=3`, where there is no room for a blank, starts the value (and a block key, `?` / `   - a`) on a line of its own, as yq does. 266 rows of documents (explicit keys at the root, in a compact entry, nested twice, with block and flow values, keys that are collections) over `-I=1` to `-I=8` against yq v4.53.3: 52 fixed, none changed for the worse.
- **jq: `--stream`, `--stream-errors` and `--seq --stream` read the extra empty read jq makes of a file whose last read fills its 4,095-byte buffer** (#6760). jq reads a file a line at a time into 4,096 bytes; when the last read of a file fills the buffer with no newline, EOF has not been seen and jq reads that file once more, getting nothing, and a closing event the file held back comes out of that read, in that file. succinctly made no such read, so the event came out of the next file's read instead. `--seq --stream . full.seq arr` printed `arr`'s events where jq stops, `--seq --stream '[., input_filename]' full.seq arr` named `arr` for `full.seq`'s closing event, `--seq --stream '[., input]' full.seq arr` exited 5 where jq exits 0, and `--seq --stream . full.seq dir arr` lost `jq: error: Is a directory`. A closing event held back at a file whose last read filled the buffer is also no longer put at the next failed file's read, so `--stream-errors . full.json gone gone2` says both failures. Rows around the boundary (4,094, 4,096 and 8,190 bytes, a last line of 4,095 bytes after an earlier newline) were already right and still are; 125 of 3,408 rows of a sweep over those shapes moved to jq's answer and none moved away.
- **jq: `--seq --stream` and `--seq --stream-errors` stop at a directory given last that delivers a held-back closing event** (#6761). When the file before a last directory ends in a container whose closer waits for the next read (`[1]` with no record separator and no newline) and an unfinished record runs on into it, jq's reader reads the closer at the directory and its main loop ends there, so it never reaches the `Unfinished JSON term at EOF` fault. succinctly went on and said it (`--seq --stream`) or printed it as an event (`--seq --stream-errors`): `jq -c --seq --stream . trunc nors dir` now prints the three events, says nothing and exits 2, as jq 1.7.1 does. A directory in the middle of the list (#6646) and a missing file last already did.
- **yq: the routes that gather a source before indexing it read a BOM-prefixed file with no header too** (#6762). #5357 did it for the streaming routes (stdin and files with `.`, `-N`, `-I=0`, `-o=json`); `-P`, a write (`.a = 5`, `del(.a)`), `-i`, `--eval-all` and `--slurp` still echoed the first document's leading `---`. `printf '\xef\xbb\xbf---\na: 1\n' | yq '.a = 5'` printed `---` / `a: 5` where yq prints `a: 5`. Now such a source has no preamble to print back, `line` and `column` count every line of the text (`---` / `a: 1` is line 2, as in yq, where it was 1), the blank lines or the marker between a first document's head comment and its content are no part of the comment (`# c` / blank / `a: 1` with `.a = 5` prints `# c` / `a: 5`), and a run of leading `---` is a null document and then the next one for `--eval-all`/`--slurp` too. Measured against yq v4.53.3 over three seeds of 1,800 random BOM rows on the DOM routes, 0 rows got worse and 145, 176 and 163 got right.
- **yq: `sub(re, s)` and `with_dtf(layout, expr)` take a comma, as in yq** (#6769). yq reads the arguments of both as the left and
  right child of whatever node holds them, so a comma spells them as well as `;` does, and yq's own string-operators and datetime
  pages write `sub("dogs", "cats")` and `with_dtf("Monday, 02-Jan-06 at 3:04PM MST", .a += "3h1m")`. `succinctly yq` accepted only
  the `;` spelling and refused the comma one as a parse error. The first item is the pattern (the layout), the rest is the
  replacement (the body), and the first output of a replacement list is the one read (`sub("dogs", "X", "Y")` is `X are great`,
  as in yq); parentheses only group, so `sub(("a", "X"))` is the same call. `succinctly jq` keeps refusing the comma spelling, as jq does.
- **yq: `map(f)` with a union body runs each branch over every member, as in yq** (#6770). yq's `map` runs its body once over the
  whole list of members, so `map(. + 1, . + 2)` over `[1, 2, 3]` is `[2, 3, 4, 3, 4, 5]` (the first branch over every member, then the
  second), `map(.n, .m)` over a list of mappings is every `.n`, then every `.m`, and `map(select(. > 1), 9)` is `[2, 3, 9, 9, 9]`.
  `succinctly yq` ran the body per member and interleaved the branches (`[2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5]`). A union-bodied `map` over a sequence
  or a mapping with members now takes the walk `[.[] | f]` already took, and answers as a node of its own, as `map`'s result is; a scalar, `null` and an empty mapping keep their answers, and
  `succinctly jq` still interleaves, as jq does. Still different: a union-bodied `map` on the right of an assignment (`|=`, `=`, `with`) or on a value the
  program computed first (`[.[]] | map(., 0)`), and bodies that read their own path or key (`map(path, key)`); the plain pipe
  `[.[] | (a, b)]` shares each.
- **yq: `env(NAME)` reads the value as YAML, and an unset `strenv(NAME)` is the empty string, as in yq** (#6771). yq's `env(NAME)`
  decodes the variable's value and answers the first document, so `myenv=12` is the number `12`, `true` a boolean, `{b: fish}` a
  mapping and `~` a null (`.replicas = env(REPLICAS)` puts a number into the document); an empty value is `not provided`. `succinctly yq`
  answered the text for every value, so it was `strenv`'s twin and yq's own environment-variable examples failed. yq's `strenv(NAME)`
  never checks that the variable is set, so an unset one is `""` (`succinctly yq` raised `not provided`). `succinctly jq`'s own
  `env(NAME)` and `strenv(NAME)` extensions are unchanged. `env(NAME)` reads through `from_yaml`'s decoder, so a timestamp keeps the tag
  `!!str` and the YAML 1.1 spellings `0b11` and `1_000` stay strings (see `limitations.md`).
- **yq: `head_comment` keeps the blank lines of the comment block and joins a comment above a leading `---` to the one under it, as in yq** (#6772).
  yq's head comment is the text above the node with its blank lines kept: `# c` / blank / `a: 1` is `c` followed by a line feed (so yq's own
  comment-operators example prints `welcome!` and then a blank line), a blank line inside the block stays (`# c` / blank / `# d` is `c`, a blank line, `d`),
  and a first document's `# c` / `---` / `# d` is one text, `c` and `d` on two lines, where the first key the comment under the marker
  was indexed on has none (`.a | key | head_comment` is empty). `succinctly yq` answered the comment lines alone, and
  left `d` on that key. An indented continuation (`# c` / `  # d`) is still answered as `c` and `d`, where yq keeps the indentation and the `#`.
- **jq: `--seq -s --stream-errors` puts the fault a record left open ends in inside the slurped array when two reads follow the last file with bytes** (#6773). A `--seq` record left open (`\x1e[1,`) that runs on into a file meets its fault at the read of the last file, and the fault is an event of the stream, so jq has it in the array: `jq --seq -s --stream-errors . trunc pa missing missing2` printed the array without `["Unfinished JSON term at EOF at line 1, column 7",[1]]`, and so did `trunc pa missing empty` and `trunc pa missing dir`. One failed file after the last file with bytes, `--seq -s --stream`, and every other flag set are unchanged.
- **jq: `--seq -s --stream` no longer says a parse warning to a program that only asks `input_line_number` where its read stands** (#6774). With a `--seq` record left open (`\x1e[1,`) running on into a file, then a directory last, `jq --seq -s --stream input_line_number trunc pa dir` printed `jq: ignoring parse error: Unfinished JSON term at EOF` where jq prints nothing: `input_line_number` reads no input, so the unfinished term is never handed to it, as it is not to `.` or `input_filename`. `[., input_line_number]` and `[., input_line_number, input_filename]` are the same. A program that calls `input` or `inputs` is handed the term and keeps its answer. 6 of 39,312 rows of a sweep over eight programs, six flag sets and every list of up to three files moved to jq's answer and none moved away.
- **`succinctly jq -n -s --stream-errors` says `Is a directory` where the fault event at the end of the text is read** (#6775). `jq -c -n -s --stream-errors '[., (try input catch .), (try input catch .)]' ptr pa dir` (`ptr` = `[1,`, `pa` = `[1]`, `dir` a directory) prints the slurped array, then the event `["Unfinished JSON term at EOF at line 1, column 6",[1]]`, and says `jq: error: Is a directory`: jq's reader finds the token still open only by going on past the last file, so the read that returns the event has been through the directory. succinctly read the event as a value of the first file, so nothing reached the directory and a program that stopped after the event never said it (exit status was already 2). The event now carries the directory's own position, which is also what `input_filename` names after it for a last file that did not open (`"missing"`, where this said `null`). A program that stops after the array still says nothing, as in jq. Measured against jq 1.7.1 over 4,389 rows (every file list up to three of seven fixtures, eleven programs): 6 got right, 0 got worse, and 0 differ; random lists of up to four over five flag sets, 4,500 rows, 0 got worse.
- **jq: `--seq --stream` and `--seq --stream-errors` stop at a failed file after a program that reads `input`** (#6781). A program that reads `input` without `-n` and stops before the end of the stream (`first(inputs)`, `[limit(2;inputs)]`, `try input` twice) ended jq's main loop at the file that did not open or the directory it reached, so the fault at the end of the text was never popped. succinctly read on: it said `Unfinished JSON term at EOF` under `--stream` and ran the program once more for the fault event under `--stream-errors` (`jq -c --seq --stream 'first(inputs)' rend gone obj` now says only `Could not open file gone`, as jq 1.7.1 does). The loop now also stops as soon as a read has reported a failure, as jq's `while (jq_util_input_errors(...) == 0 ...)` does; the earlier sign, a last value read that names a source past the failure, stays, and the held-back closing event the program's `input` read is the one it misses.
- **yq: a write through a member a `<<` merge brought in changes the source's node, as in yq** (#6785). With `a: &a {x: 1, z: 9}`, `b: &b {y: 2, z: 8}` and `item: {<<: [*a, *b], k: 0}`, `.item.x = 5` set only `item`'s copy of `x` and left `a.x` at `1`; yq sets `a.x`, so every mapping that merges `a` shows `5`. `.item.x |= . + 1`, `del(.item.x)`, `.item[] |= 7` and `setpath` do the same, a key two sources hold is written in the last one (`.item.z = 7` sets `b.z`) while the mapping keeps showing the first (`item.z` stays `9`), and the reverse direction now holds too: `.a.x = 5` and `del(.a.x)` change `item`. Writes through an own key (`.item.k = 7`) and a mapping a write replaced (`.item = {"q": 1} | .item.x = 5`) are unchanged. A write whose body runs on the merging mapping with a path of its own (`.list[] |= (.x = 7)`, `with(.item; .x = 4)`) still changes only the mapping's copy. A source removed whole (`del(.a)`) leaves the members it merged, a key the first of three sources loses shows through from the second, and a mapping that is itself aliased passes the new value on to its alias slots. Checked against yq v4.53.3 over 44 rows in five documents, every one a match (`tests/yq_cli/i6785.rs`), and a write that changes all 4,000 members of a document takes 0.4s in a debug build, linear in the number of merges.
- **jq: `--seq -s --stream` and `-n -s` put the fault a record left open ends in at the last file that did not open** (#6788). A program that reads `input` raises that fault, and jq has it standing at the missing file, line 0: `jq --seq -s --stream input trunc pa missing` says `jq: error (at missing:0): Unfinished JSON term at EOF ...` where succinctly said `(at <unknown>)`, and `input_filename` after the fault is `"missing"`, not `null`. `'[., input]'`, `'[inputs]'` and `-n -s --stream '[inputs]'` are the same. A directory last, a plain `.` and `--seq -s --stream-errors` are unchanged.
- **jq: `--seq -s --stream-errors` says `Is a directory` for a last directory after a program's `input`** (#6789). Under `--seq -s --stream-errors`, a program that reads one `input` over an unfinished record and a last directory printed the fault as an event but never said `jq: error: Is a directory`; jq says it on that read, since the slurp's own read went through the directory and the program's read after it is the next one the reader is asked for. A slurp's last directory is now said by the first read the program makes after the slurp's own, wherever that read comes from, as well as by the read that finds the stream at its end (`jq -c --seq -s --stream-errors input trunc pa dir` now exits 2 with `Is a directory`, as jq 1.7.1 does).
- **yq: a `(PATH | key)` target inside a union is no longer dropped, and several key-node targets are written** (#6792). `((.a | key), .b) head_comment = "x"` wrote only `.b`'s text and printed the document with exit 0, because a union of targets was not read as holding a key target: the key's text was lost without a word, as were `line_comment` and `style`. Each branch of a union is now resolved on its own. A key node among value targets is refused (the head of a value is the next key's, which interact in an order yq's emitter decides and that is not modelled), and `(.[] | key) head_comment = "x"`, `((.a | key), (.c | key)) comments = "x"` and the `|=` forms, several key nodes and nothing else, are written, as yq writes them. Measured against yq v4.53.3 over a 224-row matrix of key targets (4 setters x 2 texts x `=`/`|=` x 14 target shapes): 116 rows match yq, the rest are refused, none exits 0 with a different result (before: 120 did, and 12 matched by accident because the key was dropped); 9 goldens pin it.
- **jq: `--seq -s --stream` and `--seq -s --stream-errors` run the main loop once past a failed file** (#6796). A program that reads one `input` (`input`, `[., input]`, `first(inputs)`) over a file that did not open, or a directory, in the middle of the list ran the loop a second time: jq's slurp read every file in its first call and counted the failure there, so its loop ended after that call, but succinctly popped what the stream still held and said the fault at the end of the text (`Unfinished JSON term at EOF` under `--stream`, an uncaught `break` under `--stream-errors`). A slurp's loop now ends after its first call once a failure has been counted, for every slurp; the sweeps of `-s`, `-s --stream`, `-s --stream-errors` and `--seq -s` found no other row that differed before or after (`jq -c --seq -s --stream input trunc gone obj` says only `Could not open file gone`, as jq 1.7.1 does).
- **yq: an empty `{}` after a fan-out is one mapping, as in yq** (#6801). `.x[] | {}` over `x: [1, 2, 3]` printed three `{}`; yq builds the empty mapping once however many nodes reach it (a `[]` and every other literal are still one per node), so it now prints one, and so do `(.x[], .x[]) | {}`, `.x[] | ({}, {})` and `.x[] | select(. > 5) | {}` (an empty context). `map` follows the same rule, since yq's `map(f)` is `[.[] | f]`: `.x | map({})` is `[{}]` and `.x | map(select(. > 5) | {})` is `[{}]`, where `.x | map({} | length)` is `[0]` and `.x | map(. as $v | {})` stays one per element.
- **yq: an `ireduce` folds a list of accumulators, as yq's does** (#6802). An UPDATE with several outputs kept only its last (`. as $i ireduce (0; (. + $i, . * 10))` over `[1, 2]` printed `0`; yq prints `3 2 10 0`), an UPDATE with no output left `null` where yq prints nothing, and an INIT with several outputs (`ireduce ((0, 100); . + $i)`) folded the later ones over a `null` source (`3 100` for yq's `3 103`). Each output of UPDATE is now an accumulator of the next step, a union in it is branch-major over the list, an empty one drops its accumulator, and every INIT output folds the one source. A fold with one accumulator answering once is stepped as before. jq's `reduce` is unchanged. An absent key read through the loop variable in an arithmetic operand (`. + [$i.a]`) is no output, as in yq (`[]`, not `[null]`; `. + $i.a` leaves the accumulator alone), on the plain route and under `--eval-all`; an UPDATE that answers the loop variable still differs (limitations).
- **yq: a block scalar's header line ends at U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029, as in go-yaml** (#6820). `a: |<U+0085>  x` is `"x\n"` in yq and was `""` here: the header was read to the next `\n`, so the first content line was taken for its comment. The parser now walks the header line to the first break of any of the five spellings and lists the scalar like one that holds a Unicode break in its body (#6369), so the decoders end the header at the same byte. A header that ends at `\n` or `\r`, which is all of the usual ones, costs what it did. Checked against yq v4.53.3 on 60 pinned documents and on 6,000 random ones (ten headers, six owners, five breaks, four spacings and comments, twelve bodies): the new build agrees with yq on 2,453 documents it did not before, and on every document the old build already read as yq does. Still different, recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`: a plain scalar or key that spans a break, a comment line that ends at one, a document-root `--- |` whose first blank line is spaces and a NEL, a document-root `--- |<break>  x` whose text ends in one `\n` (yq loses that break), and a sequence item `- |<break>key: v` with the key on the header's physical line.
- **yq: a `$name` stage after a fan-out answers its value once** (#6821). yq's pipe evaluates its right side once over the whole list the left side produced, and `GET_VARIABLE` returns the variable's stored list, so `.n as $v | .x[] | $v` is one `7`, `.x | map($v)` is `[7]`, `.x[] | select(. > 5) | $v` is one `7` from an empty context, and every stage after the variable sees that one node; `succinctly yq` read the variable once per element (`7 7 7`, `[7,7,7]`, nothing). A `$name` that is not a stage (`[$v]`, `{"k": $v}`, `. + $v`, the body of an `as`) is read per node in yq too and is unchanged. 52 rows captured from yq v4.53.3, including `map` over a sequence, a mapping, a scalar, `null` and an empty collection, and `path`, `key`, `parent` and `tag` after the variable, which also match now. A `$name` as a branch of a `,` after a fan-out (`.x[] | (5, $v)`) is still read per node, and `line`/`column` of the bound node after a rewritten stage answer `0`. jq mode is unchanged.
- **yq: a write made inside an update body reaches a merged member's source** (#6827). `.list[] |= (.x = 7)`, `with(.item; .x = 4)` and `.item |= del(.x)` over mappings that merge `<<: *base` now change `base` and every mapping that merges it, as yq does; they changed only the mapping's own copy before. A body that reads the member it writes (`.x += 1`), one that deletes a key and then writes more, and the shapes of #6785 that stay (a source replaced with other keys, a chained merge) still differ and are recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: `with(PATH; del(...))` deletes** (#6840). `with(.a; del(.x))` left the document unchanged, and an assignment piped after the delete (`with(.a; del(.x) | .z = 1)`) was dropped with it, because the delete was taken for a value-producing stage whose result yq discards. A `del(...)` or `delpaths(...)` in the update is now an in-place write like an assignment, alone, in a comma or a pipe, behind a `select(...)` or a binding, as yq v4.53.3 does for the 22 captured rows pinned in `tests/yq_cli/i6840.rs`. `with(.b[]; del(.))` (which empties the array in yq) is still a no-op here.
- **yq: a comment at or left of the parent's indent, straight after a block scalar's header, ends the scalar empty, and the deeper text after it is refused** (#6843). `a: |` / `#x` / `  y` is an error in yq (the scalar is empty, the comment is a comment, `y` is a stray line) and was `a: ""` here with the `y` dropped without a word: the parser skipped the comment to find the content line, found `  y`, and the block-end kernel (which never looks at a scalar's first line) then took the comment line as the scalar's first line, so the scalar ran over `y` and the decoder, which reads `#x` as the first content line, answered empty. The same held for `>`, `|-`, `|+`, a sequence item (`- |`) and a nested key. A document's root block scalar is as it was: yq's first document reads past the comment on its own `--- |` line (`"y\n"`, as here), and refuses the other roots, which are still read as empty here (recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`). Checked against yq v4.53.3 on 41 pinned documents and on 4,000 random ones (eight owners, seven headers, four leading blank runs, eight comment shapes, nine bodies): 44 documents newly agree, none that agreed before differs, and none of the 4,000 differs from yq now.
- **yq and the YAML parser: a compact mapping after `? ` or `: ` takes a zero-indented block sequence as its key's value** (#6847). `? a` / `: k:` / `  - 1` is `{"a":{"k":[1]}}` in yq and was refused here with `a sequence cannot follow a completed mapping entry`, as were `? k:` / `  - 1`, `- ? k:` / `    - 1` and `a:` / `  ? k:` / `    - 1`: valid YAML, which the same shapes under a plain key (`a:` / `  b:` / `  - 1`) or a dash (`- k:` / `  - 1`) already read. The check that refuses a sequence after a completed `key: value` entry (#4530) read the previous line's key without walking past the `?` or `:`, so it took the marker's column for the key's and judged the entry complete. It now reads the key both ways, past the dashes only (a bare `:` line is the value indicator that leaves its value below it, YAML test suite 6PBE) and past the `?` and `:` as well. Checked against yq v4.53.3 on 42 pinned documents (spacings, a tab, CRLF, a quoted key and a comment included; the last eight are refusals that stand) and on 6,500 random explicit-key documents (five shapes, nested keys, dashes, properties, flow and block values): 2,006 newly agree, none that agreed before differs, none of the 6,500 differs from yq now. A key with node properties before it (`? &a k:`) is still refused; it is recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: a mapping that merges one source and then writes an own key the source also has lists that key where it was written, as yq's JSON rendering does** (#6851). With `x: &G {a: 1, b: 2, c: 3}`, `y:` / `<<: *G` / `a: 9` renders `{"b":2,"c":3,"a":9}` in yq (`-o=json`, `tojson`, `with_entries`, `map_values`, a value nested in a construction) and rendered `{"a":9,"b":2,"c":3}` here, with `a` at the merged position. Found by a differential sweep of 11,125 real YAML files, in a GitLab CI pipeline and gcloud's `delete.yaml`. The iteration (`.y[]`) already listed `a` first, as yq does, and a `<<` with several sources keeps its own order (#4983).
- **yq: a comma body of `|=` applies every assignment in it** (#6854). yq evaluates the body of `.a |= BODY` against the target node itself, so an assignment in it changes that node in place and the update, which takes the first output, ends with all of them: `.a |= (.x = 7, .y = 1)` sets both `x` and `y`. `succinctly yq` applied only the first. A comma whose first branch answers the node (an assignment, `del`, `.`, alone, piped, grouped or behind an `as` binding; a leading `select(..)` while every later branch is a write) is now read as `with(PATH; BODY)` reads its update: the writes run in order on the evolving node and any other branch is still evaluated for its errors, also when the comma sits in a group, a pipe or ahead of a `//`. A body that starts with a value (`5`, `.x`), or whose `select` may fail ahead of a value branch (`.a |= (select(.x == 2), 5)` is `5`), keeps its first output, and `succinctly jq` is unchanged. 33 rows in `tests/yq_cli/i6854.rs` match yq v4.53.3, among them the merged-member form `.list[] |= (.x = 7, .y = 1)` over mappings that merge one source, which #6827 had listed as still differing.
- **yq and the YAML parser: a plain scalar in a flow collection ends at its last character before a blank line** (#6855). `[42` / `` / `]` is `[42]` in yq and was `["42\n"]` here, so a number, boolean or null before a blank line in a multi-line flow sequence or mapping came out as a string that ends in a newline (`{a: true` / `` / `}` was `{"a":"true\n"}`, `{a: 42` / ` ` / `}` was `{"a":"42 "}`, `[1,` / ` 42` / `` / `]` was `[1,"42\n"]`). The flow plain scalar's scan steps over a blank line's two breaks at once and trimmed only spaces and tabs from its end, so the run of line breaks stayed in its text; it is trimmed now, a NEL, LS or PS among them (`[42<LS>` / `` / `]` kept the LS), in the value scanner and in the explicit-key scanner (`{ ? a` / `` / ` : b}` kept `"a\n"` as the key). The same step left a `#` that opens the line after a blank line behind a break, where the scan only looked for a space or a tab, so `[42` / `` / `# c` / `]` read `# c` as part of the scalar (`"42\n# c"`); a `#` after a line break starts a comment too. Checked against yq v4.53.3 on 56 pinned documents (seven more on the YAML output and write routes) and on 8,500 random flow collections (sequences and mappings, nested, as a value, an item and an explicit key; fourteen gap shapes of blank lines, spaces, CRLF and comments around each item and before the closer): 4,107 newly agree on the JSON value, none that agreed before differs, none of the 8,500 differs from yq now. The YAML text of a flow collection that holds comments still differs from yq's layout (recorded under #6334).
- **yq: an indented `---` in the head of a stream is a document marker** (#6859). yq's header slurp trims the lines of the head before go-yaml reads them, so a `---` with spaces or a tab before it, before any content, is its marker as the one at column 0 is: `  ---` / `a: 1` is `{"a":1}`. It was a plain scalar here: that stream was refused, `  ---` / `- x` was the string `"--- - x"`, and a lone `  ---` was `"---"` where yq reads a null document. The parser now reads the `---` of such a line as the marker when only yq's header lines (blank lines, comments, `%YAML`, other markers) come before it, with the same head as the indented `%YAML` of #6408; a `---` after content, inside a block, or indented behind `a: 1` stays content (`a: 1` / `  ---` / `b: 2` is `{"a":"1 ---","b":2}` in both). The marker is written back flush left (`  ---` prints `---`, as in yq), on the streaming and the write routes, and lines count from the first content line after it, as after a marker at column 0. A marker with only blanks after it no longer ends the header early, so `---  ` / `---` / `a: 1` keeps both markers as yq does (it printed one). Checked against yq v4.53.3 on 176 pinned rows (JSON, YAML, a write and `line`, over 40 head shapes) and on 4,500 random heads per output mode (fifteen head lines in runs of up to four, 23 bodies): over 2,000 newly agree in each of JSON and YAML, and none that agreed before differs; an indented marker behaves as the same marker at column 0 in all of 11,000 more document and filter pairs where yq reads them alike. Still different, as for a marker at column 0: a `%YAML` line before the marker on a write (`%YAML 1.2` / `---` / `a: 1` loses its marker), and the `---` yq prints between documents of a `.`-less query.
- **yq: an assignment after `..` updates every node it selects before the first result is printed** (#6860). yq's `|` runs its right side once over the whole list its left side produced, so `.. | select(tag == "!!int") |= . + 1` answers the document with every int incremented, then each node of it, itself updated; `succinctly yq` ran the assignment per node, so the first result (the document, which holds all the others) came out as it was read. The same holds for `=` and `+=` with a literal right side. `A | .. | select(...) |= f` (`A` navigation) is written `A | .. | select(...) | ((.. | select(...)) |= f)`, so a node the update moves is still listed where it was, as yq lists it. Found by a differential sweep of real YAML files, where the unparenthesised form differed on 411 of 819 files.
- **yq: `ALIAS |= (. = X)` rebinds the position, not the shared node** (#6861). `.b |= (. = {"p": 3})` over `b: *x` rewrote the anchor and every alias of it (`a`, `b`, `c` and a list element all became `{"p": 3}`); yq replaces the node at that position only, as `.b = {"p": 3}` always did here, and leaves the shared node alone. A write below the target (`.b |= (.p = 9)`) still reaches the shared node. `|=` now sends a body to the anchor only when it does not assign to its own target (`. = X`, `. |= f`, `del(.)`, `setpath([]; X)`, at the top of a pipe, group or `as` binding). A body that writes below the target and then replaces it (`.b |= (.p = 5 | . = {"p": 3})`, `del(.p) | . = X`) still writes only the position's copy, where yq's first write reaches the shared node; recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: a zero-padded decimal with an 8 or a 9 (`08`, `0018`, `-09`) is a float, as in yq** (#6866). go-yaml tries a leading `0` as octal, which an `8` or `9` breaks, and falls back to the float: `a: 08` is `!!float` and `8.0` in JSON, where it was `!!int` and `8` here; `007`, `0755` and `010` stay integers. The spelling is kept (`tostring`, copies, `==` against a number), as for `007.5`. `tojson` of such a scalar still prints `8` where yq prints `8.0`. Found by a differential sweep of real YAML files (a fixture holding `00000000000000000000000008`).
- **yq: `-o=json` of a float that is `+Inf`, `-Inf` or `NaN` fails as yq's encoder does instead of printing `null`** (#6867).
  `yq -n -o=json '1 / 0'` is `Error: json: error calling MarshalJSON for type *yqlib.CandidateNode: json: unsupported value: +Inf` and exit 1, and a document `.inf`/`.nan` scalar fails with `strconv.ParseFloat: parsing ".inf": invalid syntax`;
  the message carries yq's wrap once per node from the number up to the root, so `[1 / 0]` has it twice.
  `-r` on a bare scalar prints the number's own text (`+Inf`, `NaN`, `.inf`), as yq does.
  A result the streamed route has begun has its part before the number on stdout when the failure comes, where yq prints none of it (recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`);
  the results before it are whole and the exit code and error line are yq's.
- **`succinctly dev compare jq` and `bench run` name an aarch64 Linux CPU** (#6873). An Arm Linux kernel prints no `model name` in `/proc/cpuinfo`, so a run on an AWS Graviton recorded `Unknown CPU`, and `--write-docs` could never match it against the `**CPU**:` line of a section of `docs/benchmarks/jq.md`. The core is now named from the `CPU implementer` and `CPU part` fields (`ARM Neoverse-V2` for implementer `0x41`, part `0xd4f`, as read on a Graviton 4; Neoverse-N1, V1, N2, V3 and N3 by the part numbers of the kernel's `cputype.h`), and a core outside that list is named by the two fields. `docs/benchmarks/jq.md` gains the empty `jq-linux-aarch64` block of its Neoverse-V2 section for the run to fill.
- **DSV: a CRLF line ending is the record terminator** (#6874). A file written with `\r\n` line endings (Excel, Windows tools, RFC 4180) left the `\r` in the last field of every record, and a last field that was quoted ended in `\r` and not in `"`, so its quotes stayed in the value: `a,b` / `1,"x y"` with CRLF read as `["a","b\r"]` and `["1","\"x y\"\r"]` through `succinctly jq --input-dsv`, `sjq`, and the library's `Dsv::rows`, `DsvRow::fields` and `DsvRow::get`, with no error. `DsvCursor::current_field`, which every accessor goes through, now leaves a `\r` out of a field that ends at a `\n` or at the end of the text; a `\r` in front of a delimiter or inside a quoted field is content as before, and the index is unchanged. Checked against Python's `csv` module on 6,400 random tables written with LF and CRLF terminators, comma and tab, both quoting modes and fields holding quotes, newlines, CRLF and non-ASCII text: the old build differed on 1,368 of 2,988 and the new one on none, and the same tables read the same under LF. A lone `\r` is still content, so a file with `\r`-only line endings is one record (recorded in `docs/parsing/dsv.md`).
- **DSV: a delimiter that ends the text leaves an empty field after it** (#6875). `a,b,` read as `["a","b"]` and `1,` (the last row of a file with no final newline) as `["1"]` where Python's `csv` reads `['a','b','']` and `['1','']`, and the same text with a line break after it was right (`["a","b",""]`), so a file read differently with and without its final newline, with no error. The field iterator (`DsvRow::fields`) and `DsvRow::get` stopped at the end of the text after moving past the delimiter, so nothing was read there; they now read the empty field when the delimiter is the last byte, a marker (one inside a quote is not) and not a newline. Checked against Python's `csv` on 13,000 random tables (comma, tab, semicolon and pipe, LF and CRLF terminators, both quoting modes, with and without a final line break): the old build differed on 17 of 4,000 and the new one on none.
- **yq: `sort`, `sort_by`, `reverse`, `unique` and `unique_by` of a flow-style sequence keep its flow style and comments** (#6877). `.l | sort` over `l: [3, 1, 2, 3] # c` printed the items as a block sequence without the comment, where yq reorders the node in place and prints `[1, 2, 3, 3] # c`; the same held at the document root, behind any static path, and for the quoting of the items (`['a', "b", c]`) and an `&anchor`. The write form (`.l |= sort`) was already right. A read of this shape over a flow-style sequence is now answered through it, `(.l |= sort) | .l`, for YAML output (36 rows pinned against yq v4.53.3 in `tests/yq_cli/i6877.rs`, among them other documents, `. | sort`, `-N`, `-I=4`, `-r` and `-P`); a block-style sequence, a reorder that is only part of the read (`[.l | sort]`, `.a | sort, .b | sort`) and `-i` are unchanged. Any document of the input holding such a sequence sends the whole input to the DOM route.
- **yq: `style` of a node with an explicit tag is `"tagged"`, or `"<unknown>"` when something else styles it** (#6881). yq reports `"tagged"` for `a: !foo x`, `a: !!str x` and a tagged block collection, and `"<unknown>"` for a tag with quotes, a block scalar or a flow collection (`!foo "x"`, `!foo |-`, `!foo [x]`, a CloudFormation `!Sub "..."` or `!GetAtt [a, b]`); `succinctly yq` answered the style without the tag (`""`, `"double"`, `"flow"`). The non-specific `!`, an alias node and an untagged node are unchanged. Found by a differential sweep of real YAML files (15 `!string |-` scalars in Go's simdgen tables counted as `literal`).
- **yq: a document `.inf`/`.nan` used as an arithmetic or ordering operand, and `to_json`/`@json` of a non-finite float, fail as yq does** (#6887).
  yq reads each operand's text with Go's `strconv.ParseFloat`, which has no `.inf` spelling, so `printf 'a: .inf\n' | yq '.a + 1'` is
  `Error: strconv.ParseFloat: parsing ".inf": invalid syntax` in every output format, and so are `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`, the ordering
  operators `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` (in an assignment too) and `min`/`max` over two numbers one of which is such a scalar; `succinctly yq`
  printed `+Inf` (or `NaN`, `true`, `.inf`). It names the left operand when both fail, as yq does; `min`/`max` of a float and a hex or octal integer (`[1.5, 0x10] | max`) fails the same way. `to_json`, `to_json(N)`, `tojson` and
  `@json` printed `null` for a non-finite float and now raise the JSON encoder's marshal error with yq's wrap count (`.a | to_json` over
  `a: .inf` one, `[.a] | to_json` two, `[1 / 0] | @json` two). `==`, `!=`, `//`, `length`, a string or `null` on the other side and a
  computed infinity (`1 / 0`) are unchanged. Two corners stay recorded in `limitations.md`: yq names the last node when an update fails
  on several, and it panics on a `sort` over such a scalar.
- **yq: `style` of a block mapping whose first key is quoted is `""`, not `"single"` or `"double"`** (#6889). The mapping's text begins where its first key does, so the key's quote read as the mapping's own style: `a:` / `  'k': 1` answered `"single"` for `.a | style`, where yq answers `""`, and `select(style == "double")` over a document with quoted keys counted every such mapping. A quoted scalar value, a flow collection and a mapping inside a sequence item are unchanged. Found by a differential sweep of real YAML files (Playwright accessibility snapshots).
- **yq: `style` of the single `key: value` pair of a flow sequence is `"flow"`** (#6891). `[cron: "40 1 * * *"]` holds a mapping of its own that begins at its key, which carries no `{`, so `style` answered `""` where yq answers `"flow"` (`[.. | select(style == "flow")] | length` over a GitHub Actions `schedule: [cron: ...]` file was one short). A pair's value, a scalar element, a block sequence item and a block mapping are unchanged. Found by a differential sweep of real YAML files.
- **yq: `del(PATH[] | select(...))` over a document without `PATH` leaves it as it is** (#6892). `del(.spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.name == "sidecar"))` over a stream of Kubernetes manifests raised `Cannot iterate over null (null)` and exited 1 on every document that was not a Deployment, where yq deletes nothing and prints the document unchanged. The raise stays for any other target shape, a comma among them (`del(.zz[] | select(.n == 1), .kind)`), where a missing key's `null` can stand for a write yq vivifies, and for a field write through the same path (`(.zz[] | select(.n == 1)).x = 5`, which yq answers by adding `zz: []`); both are recorded in the yq limitations. A path that is there deletes as before.
- **yq: a write that selects by `tag` leaves custom-tagged nodes alone** (#6895). `(.. | select(tag == "!!str")) |= upcase` over `a: !Ref x` upcased the scalar, because a write resolved its left side on the owned document, where `!Ref x` is the string `x` (`!!str`); yq's `tag` is the node's own, `!Ref`, and it selects nothing. The left side is now resolved on the document's cursor first when it reads `tag`, as #5479 does for `style`, `anchor`, `kind` and the comments, so CloudFormation's `!Ref`, `!Sub` and `!GetAtt` scalars, gcloud's `!REF` and any other custom tag are skipped by `select(tag == "!!str")` and `"!!int"` as in yq, and `select(tag == "!Ref")` finds them. A comparison with `!!map` or `!!seq` keeps the owned route, which a custom-tagged collection (`!GetAtt [a, b]`) still passes as a plain sequence. Found by a differential sweep of real YAML files (182 of 399 gcloud files).
- **yq: a zero-padded decimal with an 8 or a 9 (`08`, `0018`, `-09`) prints as a float in JSON on every route** (#6899). #6866 made `a: 08` a `!!float` that is `8.0` in `-o=json`, but only where the document node itself is printed. A value that is bound, copied, merged, written through or rebuilt (`. as $x | $x`, `. * .`, `.zz = 1`, `with_entries(.)`, `to_entries | from_entries`, `{"k": .b}`) and `tojson`/`@json` of it still printed `8`, where yq prints `8.0`. The JSON writers asked for a literal's text from the text alone, which a decimal parse reads as the integer `8`; they now ask with the number the literal is of, so the `08` of a float is `8.0` and the `08` an explicit `!!int` tag forces stays `8`. Known residual (#6927): an explicit `!!int 08` loses its integer across the reindex bridge, so on the routes that write through it (`.zz = 1`, `with_entries(.)`) and in `tojson` it prints `8.0` (see `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`).
- **yq: a `*` with one merge flag keeps the document's comments, flow style and anchors** (#6900). `*+`, `*d`, `*?` and `*n` (and the same flags on a path, `.ports *+ [...]`) answered with the head comment, every line comment and every flow collection of the document gone, where the plain `*` and yq keep them: `. *+ {"env": ["y"]}` over `env: [x] # ev` printed `env:` / `- x` / `- y` with no comment instead of `env: [x, y] # ev`. The replay that carries the presentation now follows each flag's rule (the arrays append, merge by index, are kept or replaced as the flag says). An array a plain `*` or `*?` replaces now keeps the left node's flow style around the right items (`env: [y, z]`). A merge that rebuilds a container (`*d`, `*?`, `*`, an object merge) drops its `&anchor` as yq does, and `*+` keeps it; an empty left array takes the right one as it is. A combination of flags (`*+d`) and `*c` still print plain. 41 rows are pinned against yq v4.53.3 in `tests/yq_cli/i6900.rs`.
- **yq: `to_yaml`, `@yaml` and `tostring` of a document node keep how it was written** (#6901). yq encodes a node with its own presentation, and these printed the canonical block text of its value instead: `.o | to_yaml` over `o: {p: 1, q: {r: 2}}` is `{p: 1, q: {r: 2}}` in yq and was `p: 1` / `q:` / `  r: 2`. A container that is a document node (a navigated one, or one bound by `as $x`) is now encoded by the writer the CLI prints that node with: a flow collection stays flow, a flow collection nested in a block one too, a trailing comment (`[a, b] # c`) stays, a sequence item keeps its own head and foot comment lines, and an alias node is the reference `*x` (a scalar alias too). `to_yaml(N)` keeps the indent rule. Checked against yq v4.53.3 on 800 queries (`.. | select(kind == "map" or kind == "seq") | to_yaml` and `| tostring` over 400 YAML files in the repository): the old build agreed on 341, this one on 748, with no query that agreed before differing now; 37 rows are pinned in `tests/yq_cli/i6901.rs`. A value the filter builds (`[.a] | to_yaml`, `{"k": .a} | .k | to_yaml`, a node behind a write or `with_entries`) has no node to read, and still prints block; it is recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: a field write through `(PATH[] | select(...)).x` over a document without `PATH` adds `PATH: []` as yq does** (#6902). `(.spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.name == "web")).image |= "x"` over a stream of Kubernetes manifests raised `Cannot iterate over null (null)` and exited 1 on every document that was not a Deployment, where yq leaves the document with `containers: []` added. `=`, `|=` and the arithmetic assignments are covered.
  The raise stays for a comma among the targets and for an iteration after the select (`(PATH[] | select(...)).x[] = 5`), both recorded in the yq limitations.
- **yq: a write to the root's head comment replaces the first document's `---` marker and the comments around it** (#6903). yq's head comment of the first document's root is its whole preamble, so `... comments=""` (the usual way to strip comments), `. head_comment=""` and `. head_comment="hi"` over `---` / `# c` / `a: 1` print `a: 1` and `# hi` / `a: 1`, where `succinctly yq` kept the `---` and the comments before and after it (and added `# hi` after the marker). Later documents keep their `---` as separators. Found by a differential sweep of real YAML files (22 of 400, macOS `.dSYM` relocation files start with `---`).
- **yq: `omit([...])` keeps the presentation of what it keeps** (#6906). `omit(["a"])` printed the rest of the document as plain block YAML: every comment, flow style (`c: {k: v}`), quoting (`d: "q"`), block scalar and the document's head and foot comments were dropped, even when nothing was removed (`omit(["zz"])`), where yq keeps them. `pick` has kept them since #5003. `omit` now joins the same replay: the members (or sequence items) it keeps come through as the document's own nodes, key and all. An `omit` that runs on the document itself keeps it (the whole filter, or the first stage of its pipe; one below the root, or past the 1 MiB cap `pick` shares, prints plain block YAML as before). A key of the wrong kind for the node (`omit(["a"])` over a sequence, `omit([0])` over a mapping) matches nothing and the node comes through whole, as in yq. 25 rows in `tests/yq_cli/i6906.rs` match yq v4.53.3 over mappings, sequences and nodes below the root (two more pin a head comment after `---` that goes with an omitted first key); the shapes that still differ are the existing families (a `*x` whose anchor was omitted, which yq leaves dangling and this tool expands; a collection-keyed mapping, #6547; the `~` spelling, #2802).
- **yq: `style = ""` keeps the quotes of a quoted string that reads as another type** (#6909). go-yaml's encoder quotes a string whose plain spelling it reads as a timestamp or an underscored number, so `a: "2023-07-12"` stays `a: "2023-07-12"` after `.a style = ""` (and `'2023-07-12'` becomes double-quoted); `succinctly yq` wrote it plain, which changes the node's type for the next reader. Spellings the core schema already types, a plain scalar and `style = "single"` / `"double"` are unchanged. Found by a differential sweep of real YAML files (`CABAL_CACHE_VERSION: "2023-07-12"` under `.. style = ""`).
- **yq: `--front-matter` splits an input as yq does, and reads what yq reads** (#6910). yq's front matter is the text up to the first line that starts with `---` at column 0, after the input's own leading `---` line (blanks around it allowed); that line starts the body, which `process` writes back as it was. An input with no front matter (`a: 1`, `# c` / `---` / `a: 1` / `---` / `body`, a blank first line), an unterminated one (`---` / `a: 1`), an indented opening line, and a `...` (which closes nothing) were refused with `no front matter found` or `unterminated front matter`; they are read now, and a text that is not one YAML document is the YAML error yq raises. The opening `---` is the front matter's own line and goes through the stream like any header, so it is written back as the input had it, CRLF included (`---\r\n` stays), when the result is the front matter document; a closing line is written as it was (`---  `, `--- # c`, `----`); the last file's body keeps a missing final line break, as yq's does. Checked against yq v4.53.3 on 288 rows (32 inputs x `.a`, `.`, `.a = "N"`, `.b = 2`, `del(.a)` and `keys`, in `process` and `extract` where the filter reads): the old build agreed on 178, this one agrees on 273, and the 175 stdout rows and 50 `-i` file rows that agree are pinned in `tests/yq_cli/i6910.rs`. The four shapes that still differ (a scalar read of a front matter with an opening `---`, which prints one `---` more; a failing filter, after which the body is still written; a write over an empty input, which gains a blank line; a front matter that is not one YAML document, which fails before printing its first) are in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: `-o=csv|tsv|base64|uri|ini` print the results before one the encoder refuses, and `-e` reads the value** (#6923). `-o=csv '.[]'` over `x`, `[1]`, `{d: e}` printed nothing before `csv encoding only works for arrays, got: !!map`, where yq prints `x` and `1` first, because yq runs its encoder while it prints each result; and `-e -o=props '.zz'` exited 0 because it read the encoded text `null`, where yq reads the null and exits 1. A top-level comma (`.a, .b`) still prints nothing before the error (`docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`).
- **`succinctly yq`'s `@urid` quotes a bad escape as yq does** (#6925). `invalid URL escape` now writes a control character the way Go's `strconv.Quote` does (`"%\x01"`, `"%\x7f"`, `"%\u00ad"`), where it wrote Rust's `"%\u{1}"`; `@urid` and the new `-p uri` share one `url.QueryUnescape`.
- **yq: an explicit `!!int 08` keeps its integer across the reindex bridge** (#6927). A zero-padded decimal with an 8 or a 9 is the float `8.0` of a plain `08` and the integer `8` of an explicit `!!int 08`, and the bridge wrote both under the same spelling token, whose reader (rightly, since #6866) reads the text `08` as the float. So `k: !!int 08` printed `{"k":8.0}` under a write (`.zz = 1`), `.k = .k`, `with_entries(.)` and in `tojson`, and its `tag` still said `!!int`. The integer is now written under its own token (`5` where the spelling token has `6`), decoded back to the integer literal it was, so all four print `8` as yq does. Checked on 8 rows against yq v4.53.3 (every one of which agrees), pinned in `tests/yq_cli/i6899.rs`, with the entry in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` and the temporary pin test removed.
- **yq: a tab right after a quoted scalar or an alias in block context is read as separation** (#6937). `a: "b"⇥`, `"a"⇥`, `- 'x'⇥`, `a: &x "b"⇥` and `a: *x⇥` were a parse error ("tab character used for indentation"), where yq reads them: the scanners for a quoted scalar and an alias stop just past their closing delimiter, so the main loop was entered mid-line and took the tab at the cursor for indentation, or for a line of its own. A tab that starts a line, and content after the tab (`a: "b"⇥c`), are still refused, as in yq. Found by a mutation fuzz of the yaml-test-suite inputs against yq v4.53.3.
- **yq: a zero-padded `08` is a float after a write, and `!!int 1_000` is a number** (#6938). `tag` and `type` over `p: 08` after a write (`.zz = 1 | .p | tag`) said `!!int`, where yq says `!!float`; an explicit `!!int 08` stays an integer. A tag-forced number now drops its underscores as yq does: `!!int 1_000` is `1000`, `!!int 0_8` is `8`, `!!float 1_0.5` is `10.5` (a `_` that is not between two digits is still refused for a float); they were the string. A plain `1_000` is still the string.
- **yq: a flow mapping's key with no value ends before a blank line and a comment** (#6941). `{k` / `` / `}` read the key as `"k\n"`, and `{k # c` / `}` was a parse error (a `#` after a line break was key text), where yq reads the key `k` with a null. The key scanner trimmed spaces and tabs only, so the line break the scan had walked past stayed in the key; the value scanner had trimmed it since #6855. The key scanner, the explicit-key scanner and the value scanner now share one trim (`trim_flow_plain_end`), and a comment ends a key in both key scanners. A key that reaches a `:` on a later line, and a comment that swallows the closing brace, are still refused, as in yq. Flow-style YAML output does not print the comment back (the open "comment after an empty value" row of #6334); block style with `-P` does. Found by a mutation fuzz of the yaml-test-suite inputs against yq v4.53.3.
- **yq: a lone `!` on an empty node is `null`, as in yq** (#6942). `a: !`, `- !`, `{a: ! , b: 1}` and a document of `!` read as the empty string; the non-specific tag decides no kind, so they are `null` in JSON output, in `== null`, `tag` and `type`, and a write that selects the nulls reaches them. `! 12` and `! x` are unchanged. The YAML output still prints the `!` back, where yq drops it.
- **yq: a literal or constructor after a stage that matched nothing is emitted once** (#6943). yq's `valueOperator` re-emits a copy of its literal when its context holds no node, so `.a[] | 1` over `a: []` is `1`, and so is `select(false) | 1`, `.zz[] | "x"`, `.c.b | {"k": 1}`, `.a[] | 1 + 1` and `.a[] | -1`; `.a[] | [1]` is `[]`, `.a[] | (1, 2)` is `1`, `2`, and `[.a[] | 1]` is `[1]`. `succinctly yq` printed nothing for all of them, having modelled the rule for an operand of `and`/`or`, the right side of `=` and a few single stages only. It is the pipe's whole context list that is empty, not a node: `.d[] | select(false) | 1` is one `1` however many members `d` has, `.d[] | 1 | select(false)` stays empty, and `map(select(false) | 1)` is `[1]` as `[.[] | f]` is. The same holds over `--eval-all`'s list of documents (`select(fi == 9) | 0` is `0`). The pipe's outputs are counted and the stages before a re-emitting one are run a second time only when the whole pipe was empty, so a pipe with outputs keeps the lazy and cursor routes it had; jq mode is unchanged. 48 rows over a four-member document are pinned in `tests/yq_cli/i6943.rs`, all captured from yq v4.53.3; the old build agreed on 13 of them. What still differs (a write's right side, `map_values` and `|=` bodies, a computed source) is in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`.
- **yq: the non-specific tag `!` is dropped from the YAML output** (#6948). It names no kind, so yq reads the node it marks as untagged and prints it without the `!` (`a: ! x` is `a: x`, `a: !<!> x` is `a: x`, `a: !` is `a:`). `succinctly yq -o=yaml` printed it back on every route, and a write into the node made that visible: `.x = "12"` over `x: !` printed `x: ! 12`, which both tools read as the number `12`, and `.x = ""` over `x: ! a` printed `x: !`, which reads back as null. The cursor now reports a non-specific tag as no tag, which is how every reader and writer of a node's explicit tag asks, so the cursor writers and the tag of a written document agree. 43 rows over scalars, containers, keys, block scalars, anchors, comments, `-P`, bindings, numeric and boolean keys (`! 1: v` has the key `1` in `keys`, as in yq; it was the string `"1"`) and writes are pinned in `tests/yq_cli/i6948.rs`, all captured from yq v4.53.3; the old build agreed on 7 of them.
- **yq: a multi-line plain key-only entry of a flow mapping is read when a line of it ends in a blank** (#6949). `{a ` / ` b}`, `{ multi⇥` / `  line, a: b}` and `- {a ` / ` b}` were a parse error, where yq reads the key `"a b"` with a null: the implicit-key scanner ended the key at the blanks before the line break, and the loop that followed refused the continuation line. The explicit-key scanner had handed that decision to its line-break arm since #402; the implicit one does now. A key that reaches a `:` on a later line (`{a ` / ` b: 1}`), a comment between the lines and a quoted key with a continuation are still refused, as in yq. Found by a mutation fuzz of the yaml-test-suite inputs against yq v4.53.3. The blank arm of both key scanners (implicit and explicit) also re-scanned the rest of a blank run from each blank of it, so a key holding 320,000 consecutive blanks took 18 to 23 seconds; each now steps to the end of the run once and takes a few milliseconds.
- **yq: `document_index` after a write is the document's own number** (#6950). `.x = 5 | document_index` over a two-document stream printed `0`, `0` where yq prints `0`, `1`, so `.x = 5 | select(documentIndex == 1)` matched nothing; the same held for `|=`, `del`, `*`, `+`, `with`, and for an absent key (`.zz | document_index`) over several files. A node the filter builds (`[.x]`, a literal) now answers the document being evaluated too, where yq answers `0` (recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`).
- **yaml: a run of nested explicit keys (`? ? ? ? a`) is a clean error past 128 levels, not a stack overflow** (#6956). Each `?` whose key is another explicit key is a call of the parser, and no depth limit counted it: 160,000 indicators (320 KB) took 17 seconds, 640,000 did not finish in two minutes, and about 1.5 million (3 MB) aborted the process with a stack overflow, for output of a few bytes. The recursion is charged like a flow collection now, so past 128 levels the run stops with `nesting depth exceeds limit of 128` and exit status 1, at once, whatever its length. `- ? ` and `? ? - ` runs are covered the same way. yq reads up to 10,000 levels, so a document with 129 to 10,000 nested explicit keys is read by yq and refused here (recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`; no real document has them). Found by a scaling fuzz that repeats one unit in many parser contexts.
- **yq: an underscored `!!float` keeps its text** (#6958). `a: !!float 1_0.5` is the number 10.5 and, as yq prints it, the text `1_0.5` through `tostring`, `to_yaml`, YAML output and a copy, where `succinctly yq` printed `10.5`; and `!!float 1_000` is `1000.0` in JSON, not `1000`. An underscored float is now carried as its text, as an underscored `!!int` already was, across the evaluator and the reindex bridge (its own token family, because the text alone reads as an integer), and it carries the `!!float` tag where the text alone would not read as one (`a: !!float 1_0.5`). `-P` over one and `to_yaml` under YAML output are recorded residuals.
- **yq: a `#` directly after a closing quote starts a comment in block context** (#6968). `a: "x"#c`, `- 'x'#c`, `a: &x "v"#c` and `? "x"#c` were a parse error (`mapping values are not allowed in this context`), where yq reads the comment, and prints it back (`a: "x" #c`). The check that a value is the last thing on its line took a `#` for a comment only after a blank, and the quote that precedes it is not one. After a plain scalar the `#` is still content (`a: x#c` is `x#c`), and a comment between a quoted key and its colon is still refused. Found by a mutation fuzz of the yaml-test-suite inputs against yq v4.53.3.
- **yq: an arithmetic result keeps its left operand's `document_index`, `file_index` and `filename` under `--eval-all`** (#6969). `yq ea '. * {"z":1} | document_index' md.yaml` over two documents printed `0 0 0 0` (and `file_index` `0` for every file, `filename` empty); it now prints each result's own document, as yq does, for `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and `%`, the merge flags and a constructed left operand. A comparison's result has no origin, as before.
- **yq: an `--eval-all` arithmetic result keeps its left operand's `EvaluateTogether` flag** (#6973). yq's `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and `%` return a copy of their left node, so when that node is one of the list's own (`.`) the result is flagged too: `yq ea '. * {"z":1} | [.]' md.yaml` over two documents is one array of the four results (it was four arrays of one), `. + 1 | [.]` over `5` and `6` is `[6,6,7,7]`, and a following binary stage crosses the whole list (`(. * {"z":1}) | . + {"w":2}` is 16 results, it was 4). A left operand that navigated or built its node still has no flag (`.x + 1 | [.]` is one array per result), and a comparison's boolean is a node of its own. 27 rows are pinned against yq v4.53.3 in `tests/yq_cli/i6973.rs`; `line` of a computed result, an `as` binding over the list and the `document_index` of a comparison stay open in #6973.
- **yq: an `--eval-all` comparison's boolean keeps the origin of the left read** (#6973). yq makes the boolean from the left node (`createBooleanCandidate`), so `yq ea '.x == 1 | document_index' md.yaml` over two documents is `0 0 1 1` (it was `0 0 0 0`), `.x != 1`, `.x < 5` and `.x == .y` the same, and `file_index` follows; a left node that is one of the list's own gives it none (`. == . | document_index` is all `0`), and the boolean carries no `EvaluateTogether` flag. 28 rows over a two-document file and three files are pinned against yq v4.53.3 in `tests/yq_cli/i6973.rs`. A union left operand that mixes reads and literals, `line` of a computed result and an `as` binding over the list stay open in #6973.
- **yq: an empty block scalar after a key that starts with `---` no longer swallows the next entries** (#6976). In `----: >` followed by `b: 1` (also `---a: |` and `---: >`) the scalar read `"\nb: 1\n"` and `b` was also read as an entry of its own, where yq reads the scalar as empty (`{"----":"","b":1}`). The block-scalar reader took any line starting with `---` for a `--- >` marker line, where the scalar is the document's own node and may sit at column 0; a marker is `---` followed by white space, a line break or the end of the text, as the parser already has it. Found by a mutation fuzz of the yaml-test-suite inputs against yq v4.53.3.
- **yq: an empty block scalar after a key, `- ` or flow key on a `---` line no longer swallows the next entries** (#6978). In `--- x: >` followed by `b: 1` (also `--- x: |`, `--- &a x: >`, `--- - >` and `--- [a]: >`) the scalar read `"b: 1\n"` and `b` was also read as an entry of its own, where yq reads the scalar as empty (`{"x":"","b":1}`). The reader took every header on a marker line for `--- >`, where the scalar is the document's own node and may sit at column 0; that holds only when nothing but node properties (`!!str`, `&a`) sit between the marker and the header. Found while probing the shapes around #6976.
- **yq: `@uri` and `@base64` of a value the filter computes refuse a non-string as yq does** (#6980). `1 | @uri`, `.a + 1 | @uri`, `null | @base64` and `[1] | @uri` encoded the value's text (`"1"`, `"bnVsbA=="`); they now stop with yq's `cannot encode !!int as URI, ...` / `cannot encode !!null as base64, ...`, as a document node already did (#5836). Behind `--jq-extensions`, `format("uri")` and `format("base64")` follow `@uri` and `@base64`, as `format("sh")` already followed `@sh`. `succinctly jq` still stringifies first, as jq does.
- **yq: `-`, `*`, `/` and `%` with an empty left operand no longer evaluate the right one** (#6982). yq answers nothing there without evaluating the right side, so `.[] * error("x")` on `[]` prints nothing in yq and stopped with `Error: x` here; the same for every `*` merge flag and `.[]? * (.[-1])`. `+`, the comparisons, `and`, `or` and `//` still evaluate the right side, as yq does.
- **jq: `limit`, `nth` and `abs` compare a number literal too small for a double with `0` as jq does** (#6983).
  `jq -nc '[limit(1e-1000; 1, 2)]'` is `[1]`, and `succinctly jq` answered `[]`: jq's `$n > 0`, `$n == 0` and `. < 0` compare two number literals exactly, so `1e-1000` is above `0` although its double is `0.0`, and `-1e-400` is below it (`limit` passes every output through, `nth` raises `nth doesn't support negative indices`, and `abs` negates it to a computed `0` where it printed `-1E-400`).
  The same holds for a literal read from the document, `--argjson` or `tonumber`; a computed number (`1e-1000 * 1`, or `-1e-400` written in the program, which jq negates) is a double and still zero, as in jq. `succinctly yq` reads such a count by its double, as before.
- **jq: a slice bound below zero with a fractional part is added to the length before it is rounded, as jq does** (#6984). `jq`'s `parse_slice` adds the length to a negative bound in double arithmetic and rounds the sum, so `-1e-66 + 5` is exactly `5.0` and `[1,2,3,4,5] | .[-1e-66:]` is `[]`; `succinctly jq` floored the bound first and answered `[5]`. The same sum decides `-1.0000000000000002` (`[5]`, not `[4,5]`), an end of `-0.9999999999999999` (`[1,2,3,4]`, not the whole array: #3404's past-the-end answer was only right for ends that round to zero at every length), and a bound over a long array (`[range(1;1000001)] | .[-1e-10:]` keeps one element where `-5e-11` keeps none). Strings, `.[{"start":s,"end":e}]` and the read routes of both evaluators now agree with jq 1.7.1 on a sweep of 24 bounds against lengths 0-13 and a million; the path, write and `del` routes already did.
- **`succinctly yq`'s `map(f)` over a flow-style sequence or mapping prints its result in flow, as yq does** (#6986). `printf '[1, 2]\n' | yq 'map(. == 1)'` is `[true, false]`, not a block list, for every body (`map(.)`, `map(tag)`, `map([.])`, `map(select(...))`, ...), and `.m | map(.)` over `m: {x: 1, y: [2]}` is `[1, [2]]`; the result takes only the node's style, not its line comment or anchor. A block document after a first document that opens with `[` no longer reads as flow (`style` answered `flow` for it). A document with no comment keeps the streaming route for these queries; one with a comment takes the DOM route, as `--arg` does.
- **jq: `flatten($depth)` and `range($from; $upto; $by)` compare a number literal too small for a double with `0` as jq does** (#6993).
  jq defines both in jq, and two number literals compare exactly as decimals there: `[[[[1]]]] | flatten(1e-1000)` is `[1]` (the depth is not `0`, and its `- 1` is a computed `-1`, which never is), `flatten` of a depth read as `-1e-400` raises `flatten depth must not be negative`, and `[limit(3; range(0; 1; 1e-1000))]` is `[0,0,0]` (a positive step that adds `0.0`), where `succinctly jq` answered `[[[[1]]]]`, `[[[[1]]]]` and `[]`.
  `range/3`'s first `$from < $upto` reads its literals too, so `[range(0; 1e-1000; 1)]` is `[0]` and `[range(0.1; 0.10000000000000000001; 1)]` is `[0.1]`, as in jq; `range/1` and `range/2`, which jq computes in C over doubles, are unchanged, as is `succinctly yq`.
- **`succinctly yq`'s `@base64d` answers a line break inside the text as yq does** (#6997). It now reads the text through the same port of yq's base64 decoder as `-p base64` (#6925), over Go's stream decoder: a `\n` or `\r` inside the text is dropped after the text was padded by its raw length, so `"aGVs\nbG8=" | @base64d` is `unexpected EOF`, where it was `illegal base64 data at input byte 4`. An error's offset in a text longer than 680 bytes now counts from the decoder's chunk, as yq's does. It agrees with yq v4.53.3 on 800 random texts.
- **`succinctly yq`'s `@base64d`, `@urid` and `load_str` write one U+FFFD per invalid byte, as yq does** (#7000). A truncated UTF-8 sequence in the decoded bytes (`"4oI=" | @base64d`, the bytes `e2 82`) is two U+FFFD under `-o json`, Go's count, which yq's JSON encoder writes for the raw bytes it keeps; it was one, Rust's maximal-subpart rule. An `@base64d` fuzz over 500 random binary payloads now agrees with yq v4.53.3 on every one.
- **jq: `strftime`, `strflocaltime`, `todate` and `todateiso8601` of a negative timestamp just below a whole second print the second jq does** (#7004).
  jq formats a number through the array `gmtime` (or `localtime`) returns, whose seconds are `tm_sec + (t - floor(t))`, and for a negative timestamp a hair below a whole second that sum rounds up to the next integer: `-1e-17 | todate` is `"1970-01-01T00:00:01Z"` and `-1.0000000000000002 | todate` is `"1969-12-31T23:59:60Z"` in jq, where `succinctly jq` printed `"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"` and `"1969-12-31T23:59:59Z"` although its own `gmtime` already held the seconds jq does.
- **jq compare: `robust:mem-limit-64m-wide` is no longer stale on Linux aarch64** (#7009).
  The ledger entry is `volatile`: jq 1.7.1 aborts this 64 MiB-capped probe on x86_64 Linux and fits on Linux aarch64, so `succinctly dev compare jq --full` on aarch64 Linux reports `ledger.stale = []` and exits 0.
- **`succinctly yq --jq-extensions` now reaches the text `eval(...)` runs** (#7012). `eval` parsed its text with the flag off, so `eval("paths")` was a parse error even under the opt-in that makes `paths` run in the program itself. The call now carries the run's flag and parses its text under it, in the read position and in the path position a write or `del` names (`eval("limit(1; .a)") = 5`), and through a nested `eval`. Without the flag the text is refused as before, as yq refuses it.
- **yq: no `---` between results yq builds with no document** (#7019).
  yq separates two results only when their document index differs, and a node it builds from a document's root or from nothing (a literal, `[...]`, `length`, `keys`, `tag`, `to_entries`, `@json`, `@props`, interpolation, a comparison) has index 0, as the first document's do: `length` over three documents prints `2`, `2`, `2`, and two files print no separator between them either.
  A filter whose results are all of that kind is now recognised from its stages and prints them back to back, under `-0` and `--split-exp` too; a navigation (`.a`, `.a | length`, `{"k": .a}`) keeps the separator, and so does `-i`, where yq's output would rewrite several documents as one.
  Over a 5,850-row three-way differential (yq v4.53.3, `main`, this change) 2,070 rows now match yq and none that matched stopped matching; `map` over a document's node, `//`, and a comma that mixes the two kinds still differ (recorded with #2427).
- **yq: a file with a UTF-8 byte-order mark and a first line `--- text` or `--- # comment` is read as yq reads it** (#7025). The default's header glue, which joins the line after a leading `--- text` marker line onto it, ran on such a file although a mark leaves yq no header to slurp: `--- # c` / `a: 1` lost its mapping (`.a` was empty) and `--- x` / `y` read as `"xy"`. They are `{"a": 1}` and `"x y"` now, as in yq.
- **`succinctly yq` reads its first positional as yq does** (#7027). `yq file.yaml` was `parse error ... unexpected character '.'` because the first positional was always the expression; it now prints the file. A first argument that names an existing file (a symlink counts, a directory does not) or is `-` is an input and the expression is `.`; one that ends in `.yq` and is a file holds the expression (`yq x.yq d.yaml`, `yq -n x.yq`); anything else is the expression, as before. `-n` with input files is now `Error: cannot pass files in when using null-input flag`, where the files were ignored. An empty `--expression` counts as none. 23 rows from yq v4.53.3 are pinned. A file named like an expression (`.a`) is read as a file, which is what `--expression` is for.
- **yq: `--split-exp` appends the output format's extension to a file name that has none, as yq does** (#7028). `printf 'a: 1\n---\na: 2\n' | yq -s '"x" + (.a|tostring)' .` writes `x1.yml` and `x2.yml` (`x1.json` under `-o=json`, `x1.properties` under `-o=props`, `.yml` for every other format, `xml`, `toml`, `lua` and `csv` included); `succinctly yq --split-exp` wrote `x1` and `x2`. A name that already ends in `.` and ASCII letters or digits is kept (`x1.txt`, `x1.1`, `x1.tar.gz`, `x1.YML`), and one that ends in `.`, `.a-b` or a non-ASCII letter is not (`x1..yml`, `x1.a-b.yml`), which is the regular expression yq tests, not a file-extension check. The extension follows the format the run resolves to, so JSON input read without `-o` writes `.json` files and stdin writes `.yml`. Pinned by 50 rows captured from yq v4.53.3.
- **yq: `--split-exp` creates the directories a name needs and names a file after any value, as yq does** (#7029). `yq -s '"d/e/x"' .` writes `d/e/x.yml`, making `d` and `d/e` with mode `0750`; `succinctly yq` failed with `failed to write --split-exp output file` and wrote nothing. The name is the first value the expression produces, read as its scalar text: `.a` over `a: 1` writes `1.yml` (it raised `must evaluate to a string`), `true`, `null` and a source `0x10` write `true.yml`, `null.yml` and `0x10.yml`, and a mapping, a sequence or no value at all writes `.yml` (it raised) as yq does, silently. Later values are ignored (`"x", "y"` writes `x.yml` only), where two or more raised `must evaluate to exactly one string`. A path component that is a file is an error (exit 1), and `d/../x` has the directory `.` once cleaned, so nothing is made and the write fails, as in yq. Pinned by 44 rows captured from yq v4.53.3. A source `~` still names `null.yml` where yq writes `~.yml` (#2802).
- **yq: a write on `-p props` input prints its result with the quoting yq's encoder picks, and `style` is empty** (#7031).
  `a=1` with `.a |= . + "x"` prints `a: 1x`, as yq does, where it printed `a: "1x"`: the YAML text a properties file is read as records the quoting its transcode chose, and a write kept it, where yq's properties nodes have no style.
  `.a | style` reads `""` (it read `double`, or `literal` for a multi-line value). The text's quoting still decides the tag, so a date or a `<<` key stays a string and a write quotes it again, as yq's encoder does.
  Against yq v4.53.3 on 660 random properties files (dates and `<<` keys among the values) under 17 filters and `-P`, `-o json`, `-o props` and `--eval-all`, no file that agreed before differs now, and outside the `<<` key (whose handling differs before and after alike) every difference left but one is a comment `-o props` loses after a write; the one is #7057.
